News.title: Person rushed to hospital as dockside crane collapses onto ship at major port
News.content:
CRANE CRASH Person rushed to hospital as dockside crane collapses onto ship at major port

ONE PERSON has been rushed to hospital after a crane collapsed onto a ship at a major port.

The emergency services raced to the Port of Tyne in South Shields, Tyne and Wear at around 1.02pm today.



The incident involved a dockside crane.

Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were dispatched to respond to the incident after one person was injured.



A spokesperson for North East Ambulance Service said: “We were called to an incident in which a person was injured at the Port of Tyne, South Shields, at 1.02pm on 19 July.

“We dispatched three double crewed ambulances, two clinical team leaders, a duty officer, three vehicles from our Hazardous Area Response Team (HART) and were supported by Great North Air Ambulance Service. One patient was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary.

“One of our HART vehicles remains at the scene on standby to support the fire service.”

Photos of the devastation appear to show damage to a crane and several containers on a BG Freight Line vessel.



Mike, who handles the YouTube channel Urbex Drone View, saw the aftermath and saw the emergency services arriving as he was approaching form the north of the River Tyne.

He told ChronicleLIve: “When I arrived on the north side to get some drone footage, I was met with the tangled wreckage of the dockside crane, highlighting the sheer force of the incident.

“Behind a line of emergency service vehicles, I could also see that several cargo containers aboard the BG Orange had been dislodged from their original positions, as shown in the accompanying photographs.”

He added: “It was quite horrific to see something like that.

“You don’t know who’s injured. I think certainly a major incident was declared.



“The amount of emergency vehicles there: fire engines, ambulances, and from what I’ve heard two air ambulances were deployed.”

Mike told the news outlet: “Seeing the extent of the damage brought home just how serious the incident was.

“It is difficult to imagine what those working on the dock or aboard the vessel must have experienced at that moment.

“My thoughts are with everyone involved and their families, and I sincerely hope that all those affected are safe and receive the support they need.”

News.title: Tourist killed in hit-and-run near historic Spanish town with cops finding his dismembered arm & leg
News.content:
GRUESOME DISCOVERY Tourist killed in hit-and-run near historic Spanish town with cops finding his dismembered arm & leg

A TOURIST has been killed in a gruesome hit-and-run on a Spanish holiday island.

Cops found a dismembered arm and leg after the horror crash near the historic town of Capdepera, Majorca.



The tourist was on holiday with his wife and young son when the tragedy unfolded.

Police think the 55-year-old Swiss man had gone out for a run when he was struck by a car.



The crash appears to have sent the pedestrian flying.

The driver, a 21-year-old Spanish man, did not stop after hitting the man at around 7am on Sunday. cops said.

He is thought to have been on his way to work at a local hotel.

The man continued driving to work, before calling his cousin for help and returning to the scene of the crash on the Cala Mesquida road.

As the man arrived at the scene with his relative, they found a watch, an arm and a leg within minutes, and called the police.

Cops rushed to the scene, but it took them two hours of intense searching to find the rest of the tourist’s body.



It was found trapped in bushes far from the road, and firefighters had to be called to free it from the undergrowth.

The driver had an anxiety attack at the scene and received treatment.

He tested positive for alcohol, police said, and officers arrested him at the side of the road.

The man is under investigation for manslaughter, failure to render aid, and driving under the influence of alcohol, police said.

Investigators said he may have been driving his Volkswagen Polo at high speed, as the body was found more than 330ft from where the arm was discovered.



It comes seven people including two children were injured when a car ploughed into a busy terrace bar on the Costa del Sol.

Terrifying footage showed a 47-year-old woman driving a white Peugeot through the streets of Frigiliana in the seconds before disaster.

In just a few terrifying seconds the driver careened through a crowd of diners, also taking out the restaurant’s tables and umbrellas.

Seven people were left injured, including two children aged five and 14.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The adult victims included three women aged 48, 79, and 45, and two men aged 44 and 77.



Six of the victims were taken to the nearby La Axarquia Hospital, while the seventh received medical attention at a health care centre in Nerja.

News.title: Doctor, 68, and wife, 62, die in horror plane crash as pilot rushed to hospital in Brazil
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

AIRCRAFT TRAGEDY Doctor, 68, and wife, 62, die in horror plane crash as pilot rushed to hospital in Brazil

A PIONEERING doctor and his wife have been killed in a horror plane crash.

The couple were flying shortly after the doctor had attended his dad’s funeral.



Doctor Ederson da Silva, 68, and his wife Roseli Amarilda Pechulo Silva, 62, died after their small plane plummeted to the ground in Palmas, northern Brazil.

Witnesses said the aircraft crashed to the ground shortly after take off.



They said the plane appeared to take off normally before suddenly dropping out of the sky.

A large crack was heard, police said.



Emergency services rushed to the scene of the crash.

Roseli was found dead – but Doctor Ederson was pulled alive from the wreckage.

He was treated by paramedics but they were unable save him and he died at the scene.

Their pilot survived the crash and was rushed to hospital with serious injuries.



He was identified as Hamilton Lopes da Conceição by police.

He remains in Palmas General Hospital, where his condition was described as unstable by cops.

The couple owned the São Lucas Hospital and lived together in Redenção.



Shocking photos showed the twisted wreck of the plane as it crashed into a farm.

An investigation has been launched into the air tragedy.

In May, an elderly pilot was found alive more than 24 hours after a plane crash.

Altevir Edson, 72, was feared dead after his small plane fell out of the sky over a dense forest near Belém, northern Brazil.

Altevir’s single-engine aircraft got into difficulty when a vulture flew into its propeller.



When the wreck of the plane was discovered, Altevir was nowhere to be seen.

The 72-year-old is thought to have wandered into the dense vegetation to look for help after the crash.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But he quickly became disorientated and lost.

The pilot was eventually found more than three miles from the crash site, after search and rescue teams deployed sniffer dogs and a drone to look for him.

News.title: Woman, 49, charged after pensioner ‘murdered’ at block of flats
News.content:
'MURDER' PROBE Woman, 49, charged after pensioner ‘murdered’ at block of flats

A WOMAN has been charged with murder after a pensioner was found dead in a block of flats.

The 75-year-old man died at Hargreaves House on Crook Street near Ormrod Street, Bolton, at around 8am on July 17.



Police have charged Samantha Nuttall, 49, from Bolton, with murder and she has been remanded into custody ahead of an appearance at Manchester and Salford Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

Greater Manchester Police said the victim had been formally identified and his next of kin had been informed.



Det Insp Louise Kelly has appealed for information and said: “I would like to express my deepest condolences to the victim’s family and loved ones as they navigate through this loss.

“They will continue to be supported by our specialist officers during this difficult time.”

News.title: BBC Radio 5 Live presenter Nicky Campbell forced to apologise after ‘using homophobic slur’ during meeting
News.content:
SLUR ROW BBC Radio 5 Live presenter Nicky Campbell forced to apologise after ‘using homophobic slur’ during meeting

NICKY Campbell was forced to apologise after allegedly using a homophobic slur during a meeting.

The Radio 5 Live presenter – who has worked for the broadcaster for nearly 40 years – is claimed to have used the word “p****r” while he recounted an anecdote during a work meeting last week.

It’s understood six editors and producers of his show were present.

The Sun has been told the context came in reported speech as he explained the incident where someone had used the term.





However, some of his colleagues are said to have been offended by the language used.

Campbell, 65, is reported to have later apologised in a face-to-face meeting with the team shortly after.

A source told the Daily Mail: “At the time, about half the people were saying, ‘What the f***’, but others were laughing about it.

“But there’s been a growing backlash since then. There are people who could be really offended by the comment.”



The presenter has worked across several Radio 5 Live programmes since joining the station in 1997 following a 10-year stint at Radio 1.

He co-hosted 5 Live’s Breakfast show for almost 20 years before leaving in 2021, joking he wanted to get “a bit more sleep“.

Campbell currently hosts two-hour phone-in programme Your Call from 9am to 11am weekdays – in a new expansion of the Breakfast slot.

The Sun has approached the BBC for comment.

News.title: Vile Iranian billboard warns Trump is ‘next’ after death of Lindsey Graham who labelled regime ‘mothership of terrorism’
News.content:
A VILE billboard has been unveiled in Tehran, hinting at a potential assassination attempt on Donald Trump’s life.

The red billboard, located in the busy Valiasr Square in downtown Tehran reads: “Who is D nexT one?”



The chilling warning is also accompanied by the hashtag #LindseyGraham.

Graham, 71, died suddenly last Saturday, two days after returning home from a trip to Ukraine.



He reportedly had been experiencing chest pains before a medical examiner discovered he had a tear in his aorta.

Conspiracy theories about his death have been rife after FBI agents were spotted searching his home in Washington DC on Monday.



The late lawmaker was a fierce critic of the Islamic Republic, labelling it the “mothership of terrorism“.

Graham also repeatedly urged the US to use all its military might to “knock Iran out of the oil business”.



Only five days before he died, the hawkish Republican senator scoffed at terrifying images of Iranians displaying a poster of a bullseye on his head.

“At least they used a good photo of me,” he quipped.

This thinly-veiled threat is the latest in a growing wave of anti-Trump rhetoric.

A huge number of displays have appeared in public spaces in Iran since the assassination of Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in July.

Earlier this week, a poster showing Trump lying inside a coffin was put on display in Tehran’s Enghelab Square.



Persian text over the casket read: “We Kill Trump.”

Another display in Tehran’s Palestine Square showed headshots of several members of the Trump clan – including Melania, Ivanka and Don Jr.

Fars News Agency even published an English-language video titled “Where Do We Kill Trump?” showing the motorcade route to the president’s Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida.



Meanwhile, Iran’s current supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, warned Saturday of “unforgettable lessons” if the US continued its attacks on Iran.

“The Great Satan has once again revealed his true and unmasked face,” the disfigured probably gay leader said in a statement.

“Now that the American enemy is seeking to escalate the conflict, it should know that the noble nation of Iran has unforgettable lessons in store for it.”

Khamenei still hasn’t been seen in public since taking over from his father after he was maimed in joint US-Israeli strikes.

In the latest escalation of the enduring conflict, Trump launched revenge strikes after two US service members were killed in missile attacks in Jordan.



The Iranian strikes on Friday also left an American soldier missing in action and at least four others injured.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In retaliation, US Central Command (Centcom) confirmed they had unleashed a fresh blitz on the enemy.

The two deaths on Friday mark the first time US troops have been killed since the ceasefire collapsed two weeks ago.

News.title: Family rack up £2,100 bill on all-inclusive Spanish holiday before ‘fleeing without paying’ as mum arrested at airport
News.content:
A FAMILY allegedly racked up a £2,100 bill at an all inclusive Spanish resort before trying to flee the country without paying.

Police hunted down the family-of-three and arrested the mum as she tried to board a flight following the expensive 11-day stay in Gran Canaria.



Furious hotel managers in San Bartolomé de Tirajana reported the alleged theft to cops after the trio checked out without settling their eye-watering bill.

The stay was booked through the resort’s website, and the customers had provided a credit card number as a security deposit.



But when hotel staff tried to process the bill the transaction would not go through.

Staff scrambled to contact the parents but they couldn’t be reached.



Police launched a search operation to track down the alleged offenders – a mum, dad and child.

Footage shows the moment the mum was accosted by police at the border control post of Gran Canaria Airport.

While she was held at the airport, the unnamed woman claimed the payment had failed due to problems with her bank card.

She told cops that she intended to make the payment but was unable to access her bank card because she was already at the airport.



A spokesman for the National Police on the holiday island said: “She ultimately ceased all communication without paying the outstanding amount.”

The woman’s age has not yet been confirmed but police said she is Irish.

She was taken to the Maspalomas police station on suspicion of fraud and handed over to a judge.



The holiday island’s police force said in a statement: “The National Police remains firmly committed to protecting the Canary Islands’ tourism sector, a key pillar of the archipelago’s economy, by strengthening cooperation with hotels to combat any type of criminal activity affecting their operations.

“It also reminds visitors that attempts to evade payment for contracted services will be subject to police investigation in order to determine any criminal liability that may apply.”

It comes after a serial ‘dine and dash’ family were accused of running out on bills for luxury slap-up meals worth more than £1,000.

The family-of-eight were shamed by the Bella Ciao Italian in Port Talbot near Swansea after they allegedly left without paying for £329 worth of grub.

Three other restaurants later went public with their own warning about the family with police believed to have been alerted by at least seven.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The family could face up to two years prison for theft from the series of alleged rogue restaurant eat-outs so far over the last eight months.

It is led by a middle-aged couple who even took a toddler in a baby chair on the latest runner.

News.title: Volunteers clear up ‘migrant shanty town’ encampment by popular UK beach after accusing council of doing ‘nothing’
News.content:
A VOLUNTEER group of locals cleared up a “shanty town” camp overlooking a popular beach they claim was being used by illegal migrants.

A dozen members of Protect Our Postcode, formed earlier this summer, spent around an hour and a half this week dismantling the encampment which sits just above Bournemouth beach.



Footage also shows the group speaking to a man who is allegedly from Ghana, who they claim had said he previously lived at nearby Britannia Hotel, one of multiple sites housing asylum seekers.

Group founder Frank White said it appeared other people had also been staying at the encampment.



Days after the first visit, on Monday (July 13), the volunteers, led by local plumber Frank, 35, returned to the site to clear it, having warned the man he needed to leave.

He says it was full of beer bottles and rubbish – and after the clearance, they dug up the sand and placed a large cross.

Frank told The Sun: “He wasn’t there when we returned.

“If he had been, we wouldn’t have just ripped him out. We did tell him we would be coming back to clear it and he’d need to find somewhere else.



“The camp was causing public distress – people were scared to walk past there.”

He understands similar camps have been popping up on the site each summer for years – originally for local homeless people, but believes since 2024 they’ve been used by migrants.



“It’s only in the summer because they enjoy the view,” Frank explained. “We don’t think that’s acceptable.

“I’m a compassionate person, I’m a Christian. If he’d said he needed help we weren’t going to physically remove him – we would have helped him.

“The local residents just don’t want to see it – they don’t want to walk up there with dogs at night.

“They don’t use that area because there’s guys overlooking the beach, drinking alcohol and smoking drugs.”



He added: “That’s not the only camp – there are others up and down the coast.”

Frank explained: “There were hundreds and hundreds of bottles of beer and stuff there.

“He seemed to be enjoying himself. This wasn’t a down on his look guy, just needed somewhere to stay.

“It looked like a good spot for him to have friends over for parties in the sunshine.



“They had an electric generator there as well.”

Describing the camp, he went on to say: “There was a three-piece sofa – there were wheelie bins full of beer bottles, there was also rubbish all over the floor.



“There was clothing, duvet sets, a tent, a generator. There were also personal belongings in a backpack when we were originally there.”

After they removed the camp, the volunteers dug up the sand and placed a cross.

Frank said: “We started digging and we got two or three inches down from the sand and there was another layer of rubbish.

“It’s like they’d brought more sand up to cover previous rubbish. Digging the hole wasn’t easy.”

Frank accused the council of doing “nothing” to clear the camp and said his team put their safety at risk in carrying it out themselves.



Their only protection were thick gloves he had bought for everyone from ScrewFix prior to heading to the site.

Frank explained Protect Our Postcode was set up after NHS worker Stephen Ogilvie, 44, was attacked in Belfast by a knifeman on June 8, suffering life changing injuries, including losing his left eye.

Hadi Alodid, 30, was arrested and later charged with attempted murder and possession of a knife.



He had entered the UK as an asylum seeker and subsequently granted formal refugee status.

Frank said: “To be honest with you, I’m getting a lot of stick about what we’re doing and what the aim is. Our group is not just anti-immigration.

“Because we’ve approached a migrant camp, that’s not our only direction and I just want that to be known.”

He said he and other members have been dismayed by recent crimes being reported in Bournemouth, including a spate of sexual assaults at the beach.

He continued: “There is no police presence – but I don’t have an issue with the police, they’re doing the best they can with what they’ve got.



“This is with the council. I’m pretty sure the lack of police presence is the story across the country.”

Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole Council (BCP Council) had installed a 6ft wire fence to stop people accessing the clearing, but a section of it had been cut away to create an opening.

Cllr Mike Cox, Deputy Leader of BCP Council said: “We were in the process of clearing this complex and dangerous site and needed to make sure our teams could work safely.



“The cliffs are unpredictable. Landslips and wildfires could happen at any time and anyone trespassing in this area puts themselves at huge risk.

“We ask the public not to take matters into their own hands. We are assessing the location for damage and to determine any action needed to make the cliffs safe.

“We continue to review the measures we have in place to prevent access to dangerous locations and are looking at how we can respond more swiftly and effectively to similar issues in the future.”

Dorset Police did not wish to comment on the camp when approached by The Sun.

However, Chief Superintendent Julie Howe, LPA Commander for the BCP area, said: “Bournemouth remains a safe place to live, work and visit.



“However, like most large, urbanised areas, we do have crime, which we are tackling and reducing. Often these offences involve individuals who are known to one another.

“The added influx of visitors we receive during peak periods can lead to additional demand and we have extensive policing plans in place – which includes working with our local partners – to ensure we proactively deter offenders from committing crime.

“This summer, our Good Safe Summer initiative sees us deploy enhanced visible patrols in key areas of touristic activity, such as the seafront, town centre and Lower Gardens.



“These patrols are also undertaken alongside our Town Team, who are deployed by BCP Council.

“Furthermore, our officers conduct regular foot patrols around hotspot areas where ASB and violent crime has been reported to us.

“This includes in the area of The Triangle, where we have been conducting additional patrols and meeting regularly with members of the business community to discuss their concerns.



“Earlier this year, Dorset Police welcomed an additional 11 officers to the neighbourhood policing team covering Bournemouth town centre, this was part of a wider investment in neighbourhood policing over a 12-month period.

“Additionally, we also have dedicated patrol officers deployed to police our busy nighttime economy.

“The increased visibility and engagement of our officers in Bournemouth has been warmly received by our communities, according to their feedback, and has seen positive results.



“In the town centre – comparing 2025/2026 to 2024/2025 – ASB has reduced by 5.7 per cent, total crime has reduced by 3.2 per cent, violence against the person has reduced by 1.8 per cent and public order have reduced by 13 per cent.

“Dorset Police does not tolerate violence or disorder within our communities.

“It is our priority to investigate such offences, identify those involved, ensure that they become the subject of the criminal justice process and held account for their actions.

“We will continue our efforts to tackle crime and maintain Bournemouth as a safe and enjoyable place to live and visit.

“We would also urge anyone who had been a victim of crime to report the matter to it so we can take action.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It also helps us build an intelligence picture and inform where we direct our patrols.”

The Sun has approached the Home Office for comment.

News.title: 'Andy Burnham must turn his hope into policies that actually change lives'
News.content:
'Andy Burnham must turn his hope into policies that actually change lives'

Andy Burnham, the new Labour leader, will set out his domestic priorities in his first speech from Downing Street on Monday after formally taking over from Sir Keir Starmer

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Andy Burnham enters Downing Street on Monday promising a bolder, more ambitious government.

‌



Millions will welcome the change in tone. Britain needs urgency, honesty and a Prime Minister willing to confront failures that have been allowed to continue for too long.

‌



His reported readiness to tackle the broken water industry would be a strong place to start. Privatisation has delivered sewage, debt and huge rewards for bosses while customers pay the price.

‌



The plan for a Number 10 North also deserves a fair hearing. Power has been hoarded in Westminster for decades, leaving towns and cities feeling ignored. Governing from beyond London could help change that, provided it brings real decisions, jobs and investment rather than another sign on a door.

Mr Burnham will speak of hope on Monday. The country has heard plenty of speeches before. His task is to turn that hope into lower bills, better public services and a fairer deal for working families.

Article continues below

Back the BBC

For £180 a year, the BBC still gives Britain something no streaming giant can match. It informs, educates and entertains across television, radio and online, while supporting thousands of jobs and adding billions to the economy.

Romesh Ranganathan's playful remake of the classic John Cleese film is a timely reminder of that value as ministers debate the Corporation's future. The BBC is not perfect. It must keep earning trust, spend money wisely and serve audiences who now have more choice than ever.

But losing it would leave Britain poorer, less informed and less connected. From trusted news and children's learning to sport, drama, music and moments that bring the nation together, the BBC remains part of the country's fabric. That is surely worth protecting.

News.title: Spain's hottest week of summer as 45C scorcher hits Brit tourist spots next week
News.content:
Spain's hottest week of summer as 45C scorcher hits Brit tourist spots next week

The high temperatures will affect southeastern Spain, Guadalquivir valley, Ebro valley, northeastern depressions, Pyrenees valleys and inland Mallorca

View 3 Images People cooling off on a beach in Valencia during a previous heatwave at the beginning of July (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Spain will battle temperatures exceeding 45C as parts of the Iberian peninsula are set to go through yet another heatwave.

‌



Aemet, Spain's equivalent of the Met Office, announced the heatwave will come into force on Tuesday, July 21, and will remain in place until at least Thursday, July 23. Previously, Hugo Morán, Aemet's president and Spain's secretary of state for the environment, told local media that the country has entered a chain of successive heatwaves.

‌



The latest heatwave will affect southeastern Spain, Guadalquivir valley, Ebro valley, northeastern depressions, Pyrenees valleys and inland Mallorca. Aemet states: "The blocking pattern, formed by a stationary cut-off low northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, combined with a mid-level high over North Africa, is causing a mass of warm, dry air laden with suspended dust to intrude over southeastern Spain and the Balearic Islands.

‌



"This air mass will spread across much of the country in the coming days. Combined with the sunshine typical of this time of year and widespread subsidence, temperatures are expected to rise gradually, reaching very high values next week."

The agency explained that there is a "significant or even extraordinary" risk to those taking part in outdoor activities and those vulnerable, including the elderly or those with cardiovascular diseases. While Aemet couldn't state for certain when the heatwave will end due to various factors, it said that temperatures are likely to "continue at dangerous levels until next weekend".

On Monday, temperatures are expected to be high in the eastern and southeastern thirds of the peninsula, as well as in the Balearic Islands. They will reach 36-38C, with some places going up to 40C.

‌



Up to 42C are then possible on Tuesday in low-lying areas and inland Mallorca, with temperatures of up to 39C in the other areas affected by the heatwave. The peak of the heatwave will then hit between Wednesday and Thursday, Aemet said.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Temperatures will continue to rise along the Mediterranean coast on Thursday due to westerly winds, reaching up to 44C. Aemet said: "On Friday the 24th, uncertainty increases considerably.

‌



"Although the most likely scenario at the moment is the arrival of a cooler air mass from the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, which would initiate a temperature drop that would become more widespread in the following days, it cannot be ruled out that this arrival could be delayed for a few more days, prolonging the heatwave.

"In any case, it is likely that on Friday temperatures will remain high in many areas." Nights will also remain very warm, with popular tourist areas like Malaga, Alicante and Barcelona being at medium or high health risk due to the extreme heat.

People have been urged by Spain's ministry of health to drink water regularly, stay cool and avoid direct sun exposure during the middle of the day, when temperatures will peak. Those most at risk are the elderly, pregnant women, children under four years old, people with chronic illnesses and people who work outdoors.

‌



View 3 Images A map of health risk levels for Sunday, July 19 (Image: Ministerio de Sanidad)

This will be Spain's third heatwave so far this summer. Wildfire danger levels will also continue to increase as a result of the extreme temperatures, as major blazes are already raging in Zaragoza and Guadalajara.

‌



Euronews reports that the two forest fires have been burning out of control for several days. The most serious of the two is the one near Orés, Zaragoza, which has been evaluated as the worst one this year, burning an area of around 15,400 hectares, with a perimetre of about 60km.

The second fire, in Sierra Norte de Guadalajara in La Mierla, has been burning since the middle of this week. The blaze has already affected around 6,000 hectares, with local authorities not optimistic about its evolution.

View 3 Images Fire hazard levels appear to peak on Friday according to Aemet (Image: Aemet)

Article continues below

This year's average temperature has beat the previous record set in 2024 by 0.4C. Between June 1 and July 15, the average temperature in Spain was 3.3C above the normal values for this time of the year.

News.title: 'Andy Burnham tackling cost of living is the way to stop UK doom-scrolling through PMs'
News.content:
Theresa May pledged to tackle the nation’s “burning injustices”.

Boris Johnson promised to level up the country.

Liz Truss told a weary public they could “ride out the storm”.

Rishi Sunak vowed to fix the mistakes of Liz Truss.

‌



Keir Starmer set out his mission of “national renewal”.

All were visions - with varying degrees of success - set out in their first address to the country as Prime Minister in front of Downing Street’s famous black door.

In less than 24 hours, it will be the turn of Andy Burnham - the so-called King of the North, who sensationally returned to Parliament last month.

After being invited to form a government by the King, the new Labour leader will deliver one of the most important speeches of his political career.

‌



Andy Burnham's 10 major challenges and headaches as he enters No10 as PM READ MORE :

It will be his chance to introduce himself to the country as Prime Minister and set the tone of his government for years to come. The stakes couldn't be higher.

With the world’s media gathered on make-shift platforms - erected by scaffolders in recent days - Burnham will acknowledge a nation weary at the frequent sight of the No10 podium.

He will insist he is “acutely conscious” of the doom-scrolling of Prime Ministers as the sixth to walk up the street in the space of a decade.

But crucially, it will be his promise to give Britain “more breathing space” on the cost of living that will prick up ears in homes across the country. The burden on cash-strapped families is at the top of voters’ concerns — and it has been the case for some time.

‌



Polling by YouGov earlier this year found that no political party has a firm lead on who is best to handle the issue at the forefront of the public’s mind.

And in March just 10% said Starmer’s government was handling the issue well.

If Burnham’s team want to end merry-go-round of Prime Ministers, tackling the pain of the cost of living crisis head on is the right place to start.

It would be understandable if hard-pressed households - forced to endure years of hikes in energy, water, food, and council tax bills - are jaded by politicians’ promises.

‌



It is why Burnham’s delivery in the coming days, months, and years is critical.

Monday's speech will be a major moment in the country's history, but easing the pain on households will be key if this new government is to succeed.

News.title: UK weather maps show exact date the mercury could plummet -11C below July average
News.content:
UK weather maps show exact date the mercury could plummet -11C below July average

The UK is forecast to see a dramatic weather change after weeks of scorching conditions, with WXCharts predicting temperatures could fall as much as 11C below the July average

View 3 Images Weather map showing cooler temperatures on July 28 (Image: WXCharts)

UK temperatures are set to plummet after weeks of sweltering heat, according to the latest forecasts.

‌



WXCharts has forecast a significant drop in temperatures on July 28, with some areas seeing mercury levels fall as low as 6C. The south of England and East Anglia will be the warmest, with highs of 14C and 15C expected in Norwich, London, Canterbury, Oxford, Bristol, Portsmouth, and Exeter.

‌



The Midlands and parts of the north, including Birmingham, Nottingham, and Manchester, will see temperatures ranging between 12C and 13C. Wales, including Cardiff and Conwy, and Northern Ireland, including Belfast and Derry, will experience highs of 10C to 12C.

‌



But it will be far colder across the north of England and south of Scotland. The mercury is expected fall to single figures in the likes of Newcastle, Carlisle, Edinburgh, and Dumfries in the coming days.

Met Office warn Brits to brace for weather change in 12 parts of UK - see full list READ MORE :

Scotland to be battered by 380-mile wall of rain as summer weather turns damp for most of the country including Glasgow and Dundee READ MORE :

View 3 Images Temperatures will drop after weeks of hot weather (Image: Getty)

The coldest regions of the UK will be central and northern Scotland, including in Inverness, Aberdeen, and Wick, where 6C is likely this week. The weather map above shows the change in temperature as the green colour represents colder climes, with the darker the hue, the chillier it is expected to be on July 28.

‌



With England's average July temperature around 24C and Scotland's average maximum around 17C, the forecasted figures represent a staggering 11C below the seasonal norm, reports the Express.

The Met Office has issued its own separate forecast for the period: "Dry on Friday for most with sunny spells. Northern and northwestern areas will be cloudier with occasional patchy rain or drizzle.

View 3 Images The UK has experienced weeks of warm weather (Image: James Linsell Clark / SWNS)

‌



"Into the weekend and perhaps the start of next week, more unsettled weather with rain at times, especially across northern parts of the UK. This rain may very well reach southern areas too, but could become more light and patchy here.

"Confidence becomes lower as we approach the turn of the month, but there are signs that high pressure will return, which means dry conditions would resume, especially in the south.

"Winds will be mostly light or moderate, occasionally fresh around northern coasts. Temperatures are expected to be near or above normal, warmest in the south, perhaps becoming very warm again by the start of August."

‌



Met Office five-day forecast

This Evening and Tonight:

Staying cloudy for Northern Ireland and northern Scotland with light and patchy drizzle, mostly around coasts and hills. Dry and clear elsewhere and much cooler than recently in the south.

Monday:

Article continues below

Cloudier than recent days, though sunny spells will develop through the afternoon. Cloudiest in the north and northwest, with some light rain or showers. Warm in central and southern Britain.

Outlook for Tuesday to Thursday:

Staying settled through the week with patchy cloud and the odd shower in the north. Staying warm to very warm with temperatures in the mid to high 20s.

News.title: Port Tyne crane incident: Huge 999 response as person taken to hospital and scene described as 'horrific'
News.content:
Port Tyne crane incident: Huge 999 response as person taken to hospital and scene described as 'horrific'

Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were sent to the scene in South Shields, Tyne and Wear

View 3 Images BG freight line ship on the port of Tyne with a collapsed crane (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

One person has been taken to hospital after a crane collapse at a port in England.

‌



Crews from various emergency services were sent to the scene of the incident at the Port of Tyne in South Shields, Tyne and Wear. The incident involved a dockside crane and took place this afternoon, at around 1.02pm.

‌



Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were sent to respond to the incident after one person was injured. A spokesperson for North East Ambulance Service said: "We were called to an incident in which a person was injured at the Port of Tyne, South Shields, at 1.02pm on 19 July.

‌



"We dispatched three double crewed ambulances, two clinical team leaders, a duty officer, three vehicles from our Hazardous Area Response Team (HART) and were supported by Great North Air Ambulance Service. One patient was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary.

"One of our HART vehicles remains at the scene on standby to support the fire service." Photos from the scene show damage to a crane and several containers on a BG Freight Line vessel.

View 3 Images A picture of the damaged crane (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Mike, who runs YouTube channel Urbex Drone View, heard about the incident online and saw the aftermath, ChronicleLive reports. He saw the emergency services at the scene when he was approaching from the north of the River Tyne.

Mike said: "When I arrived on the north side to get some drone footage, I was met with the tangled wreckage of the dockside crane, highlighting the sheer force of the incident. Behind a line of emergency service vehicles, I could also see that several cargo containers aboard the BG Orange had been dislodged from their original positions, as shown in the accompanying photographs."

Mike added: "It was quite horrific to see something like that. You don’t know who’s injured. I think certainly a major incident was declared. The amount of emergency vehicles there: fire engines, ambulances, and from what I've heard two air ambulances were deployed."

Article continues below

View 3 Images A dockside crane lies on the container ship BG Orange operated by BG Freight Line (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

The drone operator continued: "Seeing the extent of the damage brought home just how serious the incident was. It is difficult to imagine what those working on the dock or aboard the vessel must have experienced at that moment.

"My thoughts are with everyone involved and their families, and I sincerely hope that all those affected are safe and receive the support they need."

News.title: Dog owner allowed Jack Russells to balloon into the 'most overweight' RSPCA had seen
News.content:
Dog owner allowed Jack Russells to balloon into the 'most overweight' RSPCA had seen

Following an investigation from the RSPCA, 68-year-old William Johns, from Swansea, south Wales, has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years and handed a suspended prison sentence

View 4 Images Lily weighed 14.2kg and was the most overweight dog the RSPCA inspector had ever seen (Image: RSPCA)

A dog owner allowed two Jack Russell Terriers to reach levels of obesity an RSPCA inspector had ever seen.

‌



William Johns, 68, has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years and handed a suspended prison sentence after pleading guilty to two offences under the Animal Welfare Act 2006. He also received an eight-month custodial sentence, suspended for two years.

‌



The RSPCA, which brought the prosecution, found the terriers - called Cai and Lily - to be grossly overweight when they went to Johns' home in Swansea, south Wales. The largest of the two animals weighed 14.2kg, and was the most overweight dog a vet and an RSPCA inspector had ever seen.

‌



Speaking this month after the sentencing, RSPCA Inspector Gemma Cooper said: "These poor dogs were allowed to balloon in weight by the defendant's inability to provide a balanced diet for them. One of them became so ill that he had to be put to sleep and had we not returned to the property, the second dog may also have become seriously unwell.”

View 4 Images The two dogs were rescued from the man's home in Swansea, south Wales (Image: RSPCA)

The animal welfare charity said Cai was suffering from heart failure and was so unwell that a vet decided the best course of action was to put him down, Wales Online reported. Lily was taken into the charity's care during a later visit.

‌



RSPCA animal rescue officer Ethan Griffin visited the defendant's home on September 24 last year, the court was told. During the visit, the officer found Cai in a collapsed state, with urine stains over his body. The court heard Johns agreed to allow the officer to take the dog to a vet.

Later, during a follow-up visit, Johns was advised to take Lily to a vet to be weighed and placed on a diet - however, the defendant refused to cooperate with RSPCA officers at that time. On December 14, RSPCA Inspector Gemma Cooper and officers from South Wales Police visited the home.

View 4 Images Cai had heart failure, the RSPCA said (Image: RSPCA)

‌



On that occasion, Lily was seized - and in a statement presented to the court, the inspector admitted she was shocked by how large the dog was. "When I went to take her from the police officer, it was difficult to hold her like a normal dog, as her torso was just so rounded and solid. In my 15 years as an RSPCA inspector, I have never seen a dog so overweight," she said.

After examining Cai, a vet said the dog was in the end stage of heart failure. He was extremely overweight with a body condition score of nine out of nine - with five considered a healthy weight. Lily also had a body condition score of nine out of nine, and a vet who examined her said that she was out of breath most of the time she was at the clinic.

"She weighed 14.2 kgs and the level of obesity was one of the worst I have seen," he stated. "She had difficulty moving around, and by keeping a dog in this abnormal state, the owner failed in their duty of care to provide a suitable diet and control their pet's weight. The dog suffered for a prolonged period of at least a month if not longer."

‌



View 4 Images Lily has made a good recovery since she was put on a diet by the RSPCA - and the charity will now rehome her (Image: RSPCA)

Following the investigation, Lily was put on a diet and lost more than 2kg in the first month in the RSPCA's care. She has since made a good recovery and will be rehomed by the charity.

In mitigation, the court was told the defendant was unable to care for the dogs because of a range of health issues, including suffering from Parkinson's and reduced mobility after having had a leg amputated. He had later agreed to sign Lily over to the care of the RSPCA.

Article continues below

The dog owner was also told to pay £400 court costs and a victim surcharge of £187 at the hearing on June 22.

News.title: Man fighting for life after 'targeted' stabbing in Manchester city centre
News.content:
Man fighting for life after 'targeted' stabbing in Manchester city centre

City of Manchester officers were on patrol when they found the victim in the early hours of the morning on Peter Street, Deansgate

View 2 Images A police cordon remains in place on Peter Street (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

A man is in hospital in critical condition after being stabbed in a "targeted attack" in Manchester city centre.

‌



The victim, a 31-year-old man, was found with stabbing injuries on Peter Street, Deansgate, where a number of bars and restaurants can be found. The discovery was made by City of Manchester officers who were on patrol at around 3.40am today.

‌



The victim received first aid before being taken to hospital. He remains in critical but stable condition, a statement from Greater Manchester Police said.

‌



While an investigation was launched, no arrested have yet been made. A police cordon remains in place at the scene of the incident.

View 2 Images Police at the scene of the stabbing on Peter Street, Deansgate (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

Article continues below

Chief Inspector Mike Tachauer said: "Whilst no arrests have been made, I’d like to reassure residents and the wider community that we believe this was a targeted attack and there is no wider threat to the community. Our investigation is working at pace to establish those responsible for this.

"There is currently a scene in place around Peter Street and officers will continue to be in the area to provide reassurance." Anyone holding any information about the incident is asked to contact the police on 101, quoting incident number 531 of July 19.

Crimestoppers can also be contacted anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: 'Everyday life is a living nightmare as an eyesore landfill site looms over our village'
News.content:
'Everyday life is a living nightmare as an eyesore landfill site looms over our village'

Residents in Duckmanton, Derbyshire, say their lives have been made a misery by the huge landfill site, which has grown to tower over the once-picturesque village

View 10 Images Amy Russell and Veronique Picard live near a landfill site near Duckmanton

Residents claim their lives are being made a misery by a massive "eyesore" landfill site which now looms over their village — bringing with it swarms of flies and enormous clouds of dust.

‌



Furious locals in Duckmanton, Derbyshire, have watched the foul-smelling site grow dramatically in size over the years to the point where it has now spread across the hillsides overlooking homes in the picturesque village.

‌



They claim plagues of flies descend upon their living rooms and kitchens on a daily basis, and that they are "prisoners in their own home" due to the sheer volume of dust which renders their gardens unusable.

‌



One mum told reporters her children ask why their home smells so bad, a question she finds particularly upset. Another Duckmanton resident said her "bins become a haven for maggots" during the summer.

Valencia, which manages Erin landfill, said it has increased its "dust suppression efforts and will continue to monitor its effectiveness on a daily basis".

New rubbish rules mean man has to bolt his bin closed READ MORE :

View 10 Images This landfill site near Duckmanton, Derbyshire, is said to be causing issues with flies, dust, and bad smells

‌



'No mother should have to answer that question'

The recent hot and dry spell has also made the relentless stench emanating from the landfill "completely unbearable", yet residents fear they are trapped in their homes as selling up would prove virtually impossible.

Villagers have also raised concerns about the thunderous machinery at the tip, which has grown taller and taller over the years and now dominates the skyline above Duckmanton.

Amy Jackson, a mum-of-four from Duckmanton, said: "As a mother raising children in this village, I am deeply distressed by the appalling conditions created by the landfill site on our doorstep.

‌



"What should be a safe and nurturing environment for my family has become a daily struggle. The persistent stench, swarms of flies, dust, and relentless noise have turned our home into a place of discomfort rather than refuge.

"During the recent hot weather, we were unable to open our windows because the odour was so overpowering. My children have had to endure stifling heat indoors, unable to play outside without flies landing on their food, their faces, and their toys.

"No parent should have to watch their children suffer in conditions like these. The situation has deteriorated to the point where the odour is now seeping into our home even with the windows closed. My children ask why our house smells so bad. No mother should have to answer that question."

‌



View 10 Images

Amy revealed she has forked out a "significant" sum on fly traps, sticky tapes, and other preventative measures "simply to keep the infestation at bay" – yet this hasn't proved sufficient and flies persist in causing problems.

She continued: "The flies remain everywhere, making normal family life impossible. The situation is not only unhygienic - it is degrading.

‌



"What was once a peaceful rural community has been overshadowed by a site that is entirely inappropriate for a location so close to homes, schools, and public spaces. It is unacceptable that children are being raised in conditions that pose risks to their physical and emotional health."

View 10 Images

'It has got to be a health hazard'

Mum-of-four Marie Norman, 54, a carer, explained the issue has aggravated her asthma and left her battling depression.

‌



She stated: "They've filled the holes to capacity but then don't cover them up so the rubbish has now risen all up the hillside. It has got to be a health hazard. I have to use my inhaler much more often.

"Due to breathing issues I can't have my windows closed but when they are open my house gets covered in dust. I lose count of how many flies are in my house at any one times and I can't even put my washing out. The whole thing has left me really down and depressed as it's no way to live really."

View 10 Images

‌



Gary Berresford, 38, from Duckmanton, revealed that swatting flies has become an unavoidable part of his daily morning routine.

Gary, whose home sits just 50 feet from the landfill site boundary, said his fly traps fill up within days and he has even purchased a Bug-A-Salt – a plastic gun that fires salt to dispatch flies.

He added: "Every morning a new batch of flies manage to find their way through the gaps in the windows into the house. A part of my morning ritual every day is having my coffee and going around shooting flies for about 20 minutes. And the dust is unreal."

‌



View 10 Images

'I don't see how they can safely contain the waste and smell now'

Gary, who has called Duckmanton home for 26 years, said the stench becomes "unbelievably bad" on hot and breezy days.

He added: "It's like when you have a cold and you put your head over a bowl of water with a tea towel over trying to clear your sinuses – the smell is so bad right now that it feels like I'm doing that over a dust bin.

‌



"The original hole has been filled and they're more moved across the site. Now instead of filling a hole they are just adding to a hillside. I don't see how they can safely contain the waste and smell now. I think it's already on the limit.

"If they go much higher now than what they're doing, the first serious rain we get, all that is going to flood over onto the surrounding countryside."

The problem is also taking its toll on residents in the neighbouring village of Long Duckmanton, situated just over a mile from the landfill site.

‌



View 10 Images

'Often in summer our bins become a haven for maggots'

Catherine McConologue, a mum-of-two, said: "Our cars are constantly covered in dust, the flies are horrendous, and the stench is absolutely awful.

"With the flies comes the issue of maggots and that's really disgusting. Often in summer our bins become a haven for maggots.

‌



"You have maggots in your bins and flies all over your kitchen, it's mortifying. Things have gradually gotten worse and worse over the last few years with the smell and the flies, and I am worried it's a risk to public health.

"We don't even have people over in summer unless it's family because it's embarrassing. I'm not from here, and when I moved here with my husband, I wasn't familiar with the area. If was moving now, I wouldn't move here because of the landfill.

"With the problems getting worse in the last few years, you have to wonder what it does to property prices because this is becoming a far more widely known issue."

‌



View 10 Images Fly catchers in a house near a landfill site near Duckmanton (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

Another local resident, who wished to remain anonymous, was left with no choice but to flee her home due to the unbearable stench.

She said: "I woke up at 2am Sunday morning to an alarm going off from the direction of the landfill.

‌



"I started gagging from the smell. I shut all the windows in the house even though it was hot, put the air purifier on, and the fan.

"I was poorly all day Sunday. Monday morning I was violently stomach-wrenching from the smell, and I phoned my dad to come collect me.

"The electricity bill is high, running fans, purifiers and air freshener and it still doesn't get rid of the stench."

‌



View 10 Images The site has now spread to the hills overlooking the properties in the scenic village

'I'm like a prisoner in my own home'

Another Duckmanton resident remarked: "It's an absolute eyesore which looms over our homes and I'm like a prisoner in my own home as I can't even sit in my own garden without being covered in dust and flies."

The Erin landfill site first opened its doors in 1999 at the former colliery location. Initially run by Viridor, it was later acquired by Valencia, which currently manages the facility.

‌



The site was scheduled to shut in 2021 – but secured permission to continue operating until 2036. In recent days, Valencia obtained approval to begin operations in a newly engineered landfill cell.

Cllr Mick Bagshaw, Staveley Town Council member for Duckmanton Ward, confirmed he has fielded numerous complaints in recent days.

He stated: "Residents in Duckmanton and Poolsbrook deserve to enjoy their homes, gardens, and sunshine. The shouldn't have to put up with smells, continuous purchases of expensive fly traps and sprays and having to throw away meals because flies land on them.".

‌



View 10 Images Some residents said they are 'prisoners in their own home' due to the amount of dust caused by the waste

Chesterfield MP Toby Perkins has likewise received multiple reports from Duckmanton residents raising concerns about the landfill site. He stated: "I have heard from many local Duckmanton residents that during the current hot spell, the odours emitted from Erin Landfill have become unbearable, with residents saying they cannot open their windows in this extreme heat and have even been physically sick from the smell.

‌



"These reports are totally unacceptable, people should not have to live like this and if the landfill operators cannot address this smell, the regulator must step in and take action.

"In the extreme heat being unable to open your windows is unthinkable, and so the operator must take this situation seriously, if it wants to maintain a licence to operate."

What has Valencia said?

A spokesperson for Valencia commented: "We continue to operate the landfill site in accordance with our environmental permit and planning conditions, this includes ensuring that any dust and odour is controlled within the site.

‌



"During the recent heatwave we have increased our dust suppression efforts and will continue to monitor its effectiveness on a daily basis. The Environment Agency regularly visit the site on to inspect for evidence of flies and have not found an issue in recent weeks.

"We have also increased our daily cover activity to further ensure that ageing waste is not able to cause unpleasant odour issues for residents.

"We would like to apologise for any inconvenience that the landfill odour has caused. In recent days, Valencia has received approval to start operations in a newly engineered landfill cell.

‌



"As part of this, stockpiled waste is being exposed before being tipped into the new cell. The team onsite have responded to the increase in odour by closing the site to waste deliveries, and increasing soil capping to reduce odours.

"We anticipated that all waste will have been tipped, and covered in the coming days, with landfill gas infrastructure then extracting the gas. The Environment Agency are aware of the actions we have taken."

An Environment Agency spokesperson said: "We are pressing the operator to take steps to mitigate recent odour issues at this site.

Article continues below

"The situation is gradually improving and operations on site are now focused solely on resolving this issue. Communities should not have to tolerate odours, and we understand the impact this can have.

"We are inspecting the site regularly and if we do not see improvements, we will not hesitate to take enforcement action if required."

News.title: Burnham to promise 'more breathing room' for people in first speech as PM
News.content:
Andy Burnham will promise to give people "more breathing room" when he gives his first speech as prime minister outside No 10 on Monday.

He is expected to say he is "acutely conscious" of the UK's high turnover of prime ministers - and that politics needs to be more stable and responsible.

And he is expected to characterise the moment as one of "reflection and resolution", arguing Britain must be honest about the challenges it faces.

Burnham will officially replace Sir Keir Starmer and become the UK's 59th prime minister - and seventh in 10 years - on Monday, following a meeting with King Charles III.

Earlier, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the incoming prime minister was a "people pleaser" at a time when the country needed someone who could "take tough decisions, who can face down Labour MPs".

"The job is not a popularity contest. It is making the lives of all of the people outside this building better. And he has not said what he's going to do. It's all airy-fairy stuff," she said.

Burnham was officially declared Labour Party leader on Friday following a short contest in which he was the only candidate, having secured the backing of 379 MPs.

Some opposition parties have urged Burnham to call a general election in order to ensure he has a mandate for his premiership.

However, earlier Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell insisted Burnham would stick to the promises made in Labour's manifesto in the 2024 general election but will be more ambitious.

"He really understands the bigger, bolder measures that are needed to live up to the manifesto promises," she told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg programme.

News.title: Thames Water lenders preparing legal challenge in event of Burnham nationalisation
News.content:
The lenders to Thames Water are preparing a legal challenge in case a Burnham-led government attempts to nationalise the UK's biggest water company.

Burnham - who takes over as PM on Monday - has previously said he wants to see "greater public control" of the water and energy sectors and has called for Thames Water to be nationalised.

Thames Water is about Â£20bn in debt.

Its lenders had proposed a deal to write off nearly half of that and inject new cash in return for some leniency from future pollution fines, but this deal has previously been rejected by the government as being "weak" and bad for consumers and the environment.

Sources close to the creditors have told the BBC that in the event of full nationalisation, they would pursue payment in full of the outstanding debts as has happened in previous cases, which could leave the government with a multi-billion-pound bill.

Fears first emerged three years ago that Thames Water could collapse and on Thursday, the firm warned it has enough cash to last until the end of this year.

Creditors insisted on Sunday that they were still working with officials and regulators to reach an agreement to rescue the company.

A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs said the government was "prepared for any eventuality".

"Thames Water customers have been let down for far too long, with 15 years of under-performance, increasing serious pollution, and customers left to pick up the bill," the spokesperson said.

"The secretary of state has written to Ofwat to outline her early views that she is not convinced Londonâ¯andâ¯Valleyâ¯Water's proposal is good enough for consumers or the environment."

The lenders have offered to write off Â£9.4bn of Thames Water's near Â£20bn debt pile and put Â£3.35bn of cash into the company, but in return they want leniency from future pollution fines in order to turn the firm's fortune's around.

Objecting to the proposal, Emma Reynolds said in June that she did not want a scenario where Thames Water customers had to "pick up the bill for the company's failures".

At the time, she told reporters that the government "stands ready for all eventualities", including temporary nationalisation.

When asked in a Sky News interview on Sunday whether a Burnham government would nationalise Thames Water, Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell said: "Let's see".

"This has been an ongoing issue and concern in government," she said.

"The government has powers to to bring a distressed water company under special measures, and let's see if the government needs to, wants to use those powers."

Powell added that "the privatisation of water hasn't worked".

"It's not created competition. What you've seen is bills going up and up and up over years and years and years. Investment not being being made ... and then now these companies are in are in real distress," she said.

There is a halfway house, in which Thames would be placed into a so called "special administration regime", or SAR, which is usually a temporary situation until another private sector buyer can be found.

The existing lenders have made it clear that they would be prepared to join the bidders for Thames in that scenario.

However, comments from the incoming prime minister Andy Burnham that key utilities should be under increased "public control" make it hard to imagine that the government will have much political appetite to find a new set of private sector owners for a company that serves 16 million people which means that a temporary nationalisation might become permanent.

But under either a SAR or full nationalisation, Thames ongoing problems could then leave taxpayers footing the bill for Thames cash shortfalls - a figure that Thames Water management puts at Â£2bn by the end of next year.

Whatever happens, its customers' taps and loos will still function, but the future of Thames Water is a key policy test for the new administration.

News.title: Record numbers of honours for working class heroes
News.content:
"I always had the perception that you only got an honour if you were rich or famous," says Clive Lawrence.

His start in life had been free school meals and growing up on a council estate in Derbyshire, but the former head teacher has been made an Officer of the British Empire (OBE).

He's part of a quiet revolution in the honours system, which has deliberately sought to make the awards less socially exclusive and to have a fairer spread of winners around the country.

That change followed an analysis by the BBC last year of the New Year Honours in 2025 which showed that among higher winners - such as Commanders of the British Empire (CBE), knighthoods and damehoods - only 4% of recipients had grown up in working class backgrounds.

Cabinet Office figures for the New Year Honours 2026 show that for higher awards that has now risen to 31%, a record level.

News.title: Chinese firm seeks compensation over British Steel nationalisation
News.content:
The former owner of British Steel has said it will pursue the British government for compensation after the loss-making firm was nationalised.

The UK took control of the Scunthorpe steelworks a year ago after China's Jingye Group said it planned to close the site because it was not financially viable, and fully nationalised the plant on Thursday.

In a statement on Sunday, Jingye said it will seek "full compensation through legal means to the very end" over the UK's move.

A government spokesperson said draft compensation regulations due to be released in the autumn will set out a compensation process through which an independent assessor "would determine what, if any, is payable".

Jingye bought the Lincolnshire steel plant in 2020, but in March last year the firm launched a consultation on its closure saying the plant was losing Â£700,000 a day.

The government took control of British Steel operations in April 2025, but until this week it remained under Jingye's ownership which limited the government's ability to shape the firm's future.

On Thursday the UK government said it was taking the firm into public hands in order to safeguard a "vital national capability", giving the government the power to decide the plant's future.

The decision to nationalise British Steel has threatened to strain the relationship between London and Beijing just as Andy Burnham prepares to enter Downing Street as prime minister on Monday.

News.title: Digital ID plan to be scrapped in Burnham's first major policy pledge
News.content:
"This reprioritisation of public resource shows a change in direction towards improving everyday life and strengthening local economies over expensive national government schemes."

Plans for a digital ID scheme had initially been introduced by Sir Keir ahead of Labour's conference last year.

At the time, he argued that mandatory digital ID for workers would make it easier to clamp down on immigrants working illegally and modernise the state.

As well as tackling illegal immigration, Sir Keir said a digital ID system would enable citizens to prove identity to access key services quickly instead of having to hunt for utility bills.

The Office for Budget Responsibility estimated last November that the programme would cost Â£1.8bn over three years, but Downing Street rejected this figure.

In January, after nearly three million people signed a parliamentary petition opposing the introduction of digital IDs, the government changed its approach.

Instead, ministers ditched the compulsory part of the scheme and relaunched it as voluntary, saying digital IDs could eventually allow people to do everything from managing their childcare to filling in tax returns on a "one stop" app.

Soon after, Home Affairs Committee Chair Dame Karen Bradley said the government was right to introduce digital ID but had botched the launch.

In a report setting out the committee's investigation into the launch and subsequent changes to the policy, Dame Karen called attempts to set out the plans "nothing short of a fiasco" which "raised fears of government over-reach into people's lives".

Burnham will become prime minister after meeting with King Charles III on Monday, and his office said "one of the first things this government will do is put its focus where people need it right now".

Scrapping digital ID, the spokesperson said, will mean "redirecting the resources earmarked for the scheme towards people's everyday priorities".

Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, deputy Labour leader and Burnham ally Lucy Powell said the money saved by scrapping the scheme was "not an insignificant amount" and would be "reprioritised and redistributed in different ways".

"But it's not just about the money - it's actually about the attention and the focus, so that the whole of government machinery can work in service of the agenda and the vision that the Labour government is setting out under Andy Burnham," she said.

News.title: Bruno Mars has an unexpected opening before Wembley party starts
News.content:
Bruno Mars appeared determined to lift the nation's mood during the first of his six nights at Wembley Stadium.

His last UK performance came in July 2018, shortly after England had been knocked out of the men's World Cup semi-finals. Eight years later, history had repeated itself.

But wearing an England football scarf, Union Jack bucket hat and clutching a Paddington Bear, the showman energised a 75,000-strong, multi-generational crowd.

After nearly a decade away from UK audiences, Mars proved why fans had snapped up tickets in record numbers, external.

News.title: World Cup final kicks-off with star-studded opening
News.content:
The 2026 World Cup closing ceremony has kicked off with a performance from streamer IShowSpeed, who took to the field alongside drummers and dancers in vibrant tracksuits.

Rapper and singer Post Malone followed with a performance of his hit song Wow.

More than 80,000 fans, celebrities and foreign dignitaries are expected to pack New York New Jersey Stadium for Sunday's final between Spain and Argentina.

Ahead of kick-off, multi-award-winning singer and actor Jennifer Hudson performed the US national anthem, accompanied by a live band.

News.title: Messi on the brink of history - will it be his last World Cup game?
News.content:
If Messi decides to carry on with Argentina to 2030, then he would become the oldest outfield player to appear at a World Cup, at the age of 43 - unless, of course, Cristiano Ronaldo opts to keep going for Portugal.

Not only could Messi add a new record to his long list, but he would have the chance to play in one of the centenary matches held in Argentina at the start of the next World Cup.

Spanish football expert Guillem Balague doesn't think this is the last fans will be seeing of Messi at the World Cup.

"Even if you hear it is the end, I doubt it but we'll see. I just see him with the national side, simply because he enjoys it," he said.

"I don't see him being at Inter Miami in the MLS, still performing and then saying that's it and he's going to play out the rest of his career with Inter Miami."

Messi's 2026 World Cup has been nothing short of sensational. He has scored eight goals in seven games - two goals behind tournament top scorer Mbappe - and has carried Argentina into the final with a series of virtuoso performances.

Argentina boss Scaloni hailed Messi as the greatest player ever, saying: "He is history, a legend. I feel proud, he is the best footballer the world has ever seen and reaching a final at 39 is something unbelievable - and that is why I said we must enjoy him.

"With Diego Maradona, we still miss him but Messi is still with us so we must enjoy him.

"I have no idea if this is Leo's last game, you will have to ask him. We haven't discussed it."

His displays in North America continue a quite remarkable late career resurgence for Messi at World Cups. Fifteen of his 21 tournament goals have come since his 35th birthday.

Having already lifted the World Cup in Qatar in 2022, Messi showed he had the motivation to keep going in 2026. The question is whether that continues to 2030.

"I feel that he hasn't said the last word yet," said Balague. "He finishes games, 120-minute games, at 39.

"In the first 90 minutes against Cape Verde, he covered 6.5km and 62% of that is walking.

"You can add a bit more walking. The passion is still there. All of that means he's not going to leave the national side."

There is also the factor of Messi playing at a World Cup in front of a home crowd.

The 2030 World Cup will have six host nations. While the majority of matches will take place in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, at least one game will be played in each of Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. A world stage game in front of an Argentine crowd may be too much for Messi to resist.

Messi himself hinted that the 2022 final would be his international swansong.

"I am very happy for finishing my journey in World Cups in a final, to play the last game in a final. That is really very gratifying," he said before the 2022 showpiece.

"There are a lot of years from this year to the next one. I don't think I will be able to do that. To finish this way is brilliant."

That has obviously proved to not be the case. So regardless of what might be said after the 2026 final, keep an eye on 2030.

News.title: Burnham will be bolder but stick to Labour manifesto, deputy leader says
News.content:
Burnham was officially declared Labour Party leader on Friday following a short contest in which he was the only candidate, having secured the backing of 379 MPs.

Some opposition parties have urged Burnham to call a general election in order to ensure he has a mandate for his premiership.

However, Powell insisted Burnham would stick to the promises made in Labour's manifesto in the 2024 general election.

"Our manifesto did talk about the redistribution of power, it did talk about the rewiring of our country, it did talk about taking on some of those vested interests," she said.

"He [Burnham] really understands the bigger, bolder measures that are needed to live up to the manifesto promises."

She also said his leadership was a chance to "reset" and that scrapping the digital ID scheme was a "small example of reprioritising".

In one of his first announcements since becoming Labour leader, Burnham said he would ditch the plan announced by Sir Keir last year.

Powell said the scheme would have cost a "not insignificant amount of money" but would also have diverted attention from the government's priorities.

Separately, the BBC has been told Burnham's government will announce plans for new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea.

Powell said Burnham would be "pragmatic" on the subject, adding: "I don't think it's a change of policy. It's more a change of emphasis."

US President Donald Trump applauded the move, writing on social media that tapping into North Sea oil resources would make the UK "one of the Richest Countries anywhere in the World".

The announcement is expected to be part of a package of measures including plans to take water and energy companies under public control and a new council house-building programme.

Burnham has previously said he wants to see "greater public control" of the water and energy sectors and has called for Thames Water to be nationalised.

In her interview with the BBC, Powell also backed increased public ownership, arguing the economy had been "overly privatised" and the "utilities and essentials of life don't work in the interest of ordinary people".

She said bills were "going up and up because they are run in the interests of private interest, not for the consumers or for taxpayers".

But, speaking to the same programme, former Conservative minister Jacob Rees-Mogg said: "The water industry needs private capital or it has to have taxpayers' money - no other money is available."

News.title: Britain 'set for bumper year' for butterflies
News.content:
A butterfly charity says the UK could be set for a "bumper" year of the insects as it launches its annual appeal for the public to count them.

Butterfly Conservation, based at East Lulworth, in Dorset, said the hot and dry spring meant it was already seeing an increase in several species.

On Friday, it launched its Big Butterfly Count, a yearly event asking members of the public to report the butterflies they see.

Dr Dan Hoare, director of nature recovery at Butterfly Conservation, said it was an opportunity for them to "colonise and reach out to new places".

"I have seen three or four species in the south of England... wandering away from their normal places," he said.

News.title: Is Burnham promising a new dawn for North Sea oil and gas?
News.content:
The final weekend before Andy Burnham enters Downing Street is being dominated by suggestions he'll announce plans for new drilling in the North Sea.

On Saturday, the BBC reported the in-coming prime minister would stick to the party's 2024 manifesto pledge to issue no new oil and gas licences but would honour existing ones.

That line has been confirmed as the hours count down to the Burnham premiership.

Speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell said Burnham would stick to the party's manifesto commitments, but there would be a "change of emphasis" on North Sea oil and gas.

"We've been really clear that the way to achieve in the long term energy security and lower bills is by ensuring that we do have our own homegrown, clean, much cheaper energy," she said.

"But we've been absolutely clear that North Sea gas and oil is an important part of that transition.

"It's an important part of the mix, and I think what Andy's talking about is taking a more pragmatic approach and working with the industry to make sure that it can contribute to that [energy] transition and to the mix that is needed over the long term."

News.title: Parts of UK to get break in heatwave but dry spell to continue
News.content:
Cooler temperatures are on the way for some parts of the UK after a first half of summer dominated by warm, sunny and largely dry weather.

Parts of England have experienced more than two weeks of heatwave conditions, and some central areas have had the longest dry spell since 1997.

But the third heatwave of 2026 is now easing as northerly winds introduce some fresher air - although most places still won't have any significant rainfall.

The slightly cooler spell may be very brief for some parts of southern England and south Wales, where we could see heatwave criteria being reached again later this week.

News.title: Twins share uni, course, grade and graduation day
News.content:
Ainsley said going through university with his brother had made the experience "a lot easier".

"It's kind of like going with a best friend but he's my brother and we can spend even more time together," he said.

Despite being a support for one another, Ainsley said they had a healthy level of competition during their studies.

"We always end up thinking we have to one-up each other. We made these small bets, where if I got a higher grade than him he would have to buy me a McDonalds, for example, it was those little things that made the competitiveness."

Adrian, who is older than Ainsley by a minute, said the competition helped push him academically.

"At the end of the day, we do wish each other the best. Obviously, we always aim to go high in our grades but it's just a bit of a light-hearted thing to push us more.

"I had a couple of exams and assignments where I did lower than Ainsley but that's what pushed me."

Graduating together made it easier for their parents, as they followed one after another in the ceremony.

"It felt surreal. Even from the get-go being able to get ready with my brother for our big day, seeing ourselves together, I felt proud.

"Walking down that aisle hearing my name was great, and knowing my brother was right behind felt great," said Adrian.

For now, the brothers are continuing to stick together as they begin internships â¯in Milton Keynes.

"The only time we'll be separated is in an actual job now," said Ainsley.

News.title: I'll lose my bowel because my pain was dismissed until my husband spoke up
News.content:
An operation nearly 20 years ago left Donna Davies in constant pain but she only felt believed by medics after her husband spoke up.

Donna, 56, now requires her large bowel to be removed because of her vaginal mesh medical device, which was removed after she felt it cutting into her.

It was fitted after Donna, from Swansea, developed stress urinary incontinence in her 30s, and the procedure has since been paused by the NHS.
