She was invited to attend a women's health summit in Wales this week, which looked at how women's pain is too often dismissed as "normal" within healthcare.

Donna is one of an estimated 100,000 women in the UK who had the procedure to treat incontinence or prolapse.

She said: "The mesh was leaving me in daily pain - the only way I can explain it was that I was being cut by glass every time I moved.

"I didn't feel as if I was believed and I didn't feel my pain was acknowledged until my husband spoke up about an incident we had and then I felt that the surgeon believed my husband."

The device was eventually removed and a "sling" made from her own muscles was created at the same time as a total hysterectomy.

"I've never recovered from this operation - I'm still in constant pain, neuropathic pain as well and sadly I'm about to lose my large bowel and have a permanent stoma.

"I feel that women in Wales are being forgotten. There are no specialist services in Wales for women like myself, yet nine specialist centres in England - we do feel forgotten."

Delyth Jewell, the women's health minister in the Senedd, said she wanted rules to be strengthened so that health boards are required to include women in the design of services for them.

"I am determined to strengthen women's voices so that women will be believed about their bodies," the minister said at the women's health summit.

"I wonder how many women will have heard the words 'this might hurt' when they go to the doctor?

"That shouldn't be normal. Too often women's health services are considered a 'should' not a 'must'.

"We need to make sure that in theatre space they are prioritised more, we need to be making sure that training is improved."

News.title: Eight released over alleged threat to Islamic event
News.content:
Eight more people have been freed from custody, as police continue to investigate an alleged extreme right-wing threat to an Islamic event in Suffolk.

Officers became aware of the threat to the UK Ijtima event at Shrubland Hall, near Ipswich, last weekend.

Thousands of people attended the gathering but it closed early on police advice.

The Metropolitan Police said on Saturday, external that seven men were released from custody without charge, while another man was released on bail with strict conditions pending further inquiries.

The force said the investigation involved searching homes and vehicles, and more than 35 digital devices were seized.

Following those searches, a 42-year-old man was charged with two counts of possession of offensive weapons, extendable batons, and possession of a stun gun.

Police said the charges were not believed to be connected to the alleged threat on UK Ijtima.

The man was remanded in custody to appear at Reading Magistrates' Court on Monday.

Four other people were previously released on bail pending further inquiries.

News.title: Woman killed while asleep with baby ‘was my world’, sister says
News.content:
The sister of a 24-year-old mother who was stabbed and killed as she lay in bed with her husband and baby in west London has said "she was my world".

Kirandeep Kaur, who was originally from India, was fatally attacked at her home in Hayes on 12 July.

Speaking through a translator from the Majha region of Punjab, India, her sister Gursharan told BBC London: "She is everything for me, she video calls me and my mum. What are we going to do without her?"

A man has been charged with Kaur's murder.

Gursharan, who is 21, said her sister came to London looking for a better job so she could support her family.

"My sister moved to the UK in September 2024 to study at Buckinghamshire New University.

"She completed her studies and worked at a grocery store.

"We spoke to each other on the phone. But she hasn't been back, so I haven't seen her.

"When she reached London, she told me it was beautiful and she was happy."

Gusharan said her sister was "very intelligent".

"She was the top of her class here in India when she was studying, she's a very hard worker. She loved us all very much.

"Our family is very poor. She always thinks about us first. She was very supportive to me. She was my world. My heart hurts."

News.content:

England held their nerve after Ben Duckett’s masterful 141 inspired a first ODI series win over India since 2018 with a thrilling 27-run victory in a dramatic Lord’s finale.

Joe Root’s unbeaten 99 in Cardiff on Thursday set up a winner-takes-all contest at the home of cricket and England were halfway there when Duckett’s magnificent century was the bedrock of a record-breaking total of 387-3.

The best ever List A score at Lord’s was helped by 91 from new ODI opener Jacob Bethell, who almost marked Friday’s death of mentor Sir Garfield Sobers with a century, before Root’s latest fifty was backed up by Jos Buttler’s blistering 13-ball innings of 41.

Rohit Sharma had other ideas and put retirement rumours to bed with an equally stunning 138 to become the first India player to score an ODI hundred at the historic venue, but he was bowled after captain Harry Brook turned to Bethell to flip the momentum at 260-2.

Virat Kohli had already picked up the baton after Shubman Gill’s 77 and scored 50 on what may be his final innings in England, but two wickets for Sam Curran in the 44th over on his way to 4-75 further turned the screw.

Brook’s team eventually restricted India to 360-7 to make it six wins out of seven white-ball matches this summer and provide a boost to head coach Brendon McCullum, who lost his Test job this month but secured only a second ODI series triumph for England over India since 2012.

open image in gallery England celebrated an impressive win ( Reuters )

After Brook put England into bat, Bethell set about paying the ultimate tribute to family friend Sobers, who provided a reference which got the Barbados-born left-hander a scholarship into Rugby School in Warwickshire.

The first of 13 Bethell boundaries was an inside edge off Prasidh Krishna, but he settled into his groove with an early exquisite drive for four.

Bethell survived a run-out chance on 25 but Prince Yadav’s next delivery was pulled over deep square leg for six.

Two more exceptional drives for four were followed by Bethell’s 51-ball fifty via a top edge, which also brought up the hundred partnership in 15.3 overs with Duckett, who had played in a composed fashion.

Duckett reached his own half-century with a cut for four before all eyes were on Bethell but he picked out Sharma and had to drag himself off nine short of three figures.

A partnership of 192 still represented an ODI best for England against India and back-to-back fours off Arshdeep Singh moved Duckett closer to raising his bat.

Duckett had survived a DRS review on 67 off Axar Patel and brought up a fourth ODI international hundred when he pulled Gurnoor Brar to the boundary during the 36th over.

After Duckett required 108 balls for his milestone, three fours off Brar’s next over took England beyond the 250-mark before KL Rahul carried across the boundary rope for six, but Yadav’s slower ball finally accounted for the Nottinghamshire opener.

Duckett walked off for 141, a new highest ODI men’s score at Lord’s after Viv Richards’ 138 in 1975 before Root and Buttler produced late fireworks.

Root’s reverse sweep for four off Patel took him beyond his own past record of 309 runs without being dismissed in ODIs and he finished 74 not out, but largely played second fiddle to Buttler.

Buttler heaved Brar over long-on for six during a 23-run over which was followed by two more maximums back past Krishna, which took England to 387 for three.

Sharma strolled out amid speculation this could be his final match and a thick edge off Gus Atkinson was hardly a signal of intent, but the statement of consecutive fours off Josh Tongue followed before a trademark pull into the crowd welcomed Curran.

Gill beat Sharma to fifty but cramp struck like at Edgbaston and he was pinned in front lbw for 77 off Adil Rashid.

With India on 147 for one off 25.1 overs, Kohli’s entrance sparked enormous noise and the decibel level increased when Sharma reached three figures.

Back-to-back sixes off Tongue took Sharma into the nineties and a slog-swept over deep midwicket from Rashid earned a richly deserved century.

Sharma barely celebrated but Brook’s decision to turn to Bethell proved inspired and two tight overs were followed by a breakthrough.

Sharma exited bowled for 138 after he dispatched Bethell into the stand before Curran’s two 44th over scalps of Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer – both caught by substitute fielder Rehan Ahmed – knocked the stuffing out of India, who lost Kohli (74) and ended on 360 for seven.

The World Cup 2026 final between Argentina and Spain did not kick off on time and was delayed by six minutes. Kick-off at the New York ⁠New Jersey stadium was scheduled to be 8pm BST (3pm ET) but the most-watched sporting fixture in the world did not begin until 8:06pm.

The start of the match followed a performance by Robbie Williams, the singing of the national anthem by Jennifer Hudson, a bizarre pre-game speech by actor Tom Cruise, and a ‘let’s get ready to rumble’ build-up by ring announcers the Buffer brothers - Michael and Bruce. There was also the World Cup closing ceremony, 90 minutes before kick-off, featuring performances by Post Malone and streamer IShowSpeed.

The World Cup final will also stage an extended half-time show, with performances from Shakira and Madonna expected to delay the restart of the final by several minutes. Donald Trump's attendance at the match also added extra ⁠layers of security, with hundreds of journalists, entertainers, and volunteers waiting in ​lines for ⁠up to three hours.

Lionel Messi’s Argentina are bidding to become the first World Cup champions to defend their title since Brazil in 1962, while Spain are attempting to win the World Cup for the second time and add to their Euro 2024 victory.

Spain are the favourites after brilliantly beating France 2-0 in a surprisingly one-sided semi-final, so perhaps it is no surprise that Luis de la Fuente opted for an unchanged starting XI from that fixture.

open image in gallery ( Getty )

open image in gallery ( Getty )

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

Lionel Scaloni made three changes from the Argentina side that started the semi-final victory over England. Nahuel Molina, Giuliano Simeone and Leandro Paredes all drop to the bench, with right-back Gonzalo Montiel and midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Nico Gonzalez starting instead.

Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic will officiate the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina; Vincic will be joined by compatriot assistants Tomaz Klancnik and Andraz Kovacic, making history as the first ever referee from Slovenia to take charge of the landmark fixture.

Donald Trump arrived at the final of the World Cup on Sunday afternoon, where the U.S. president will take in his first and only match of the championship as Argentina and Spain battle it out for the trophy.

Pool reports indicated that Trump departed Bedminster, New Jersey via Marine One just before 1:00 p.m. eastern time, and reporters were quickly afterwards ushered onto the field for the pre-game events. His helicopter completed a brief flyover, which went largely unnoticed by the crowd, according to reporters in the stadium. Marine One then touched down outside the arena.

At around 2:45, he appeared onscreen via MetLife Stadium’s scoreboard screen. Once again, according to pool reporters, there was no discernable reaction from the crowd.

The president hosted a press conference on Friday as he hosted a reception with FIFA’s president, Gianni Infantino, and said that he’d bring up the idea of hosting the championship again to Infantino. Hosting rights for the next two World Cups have already been decided.

"It turned out we were a soccer country, and I think it’s going to remain," he said on Friday, during the event at Trump Tower in New York. "This has really brought the world together."

Donald Trump and Gianna Infantino attend the World Cup Final ( AP )

He also spoke to reporters on the Fox Sports pregame show ahead of Sunday’s game.

Trump is set to present the trophy to the winning team after the game. He isn’t outright backing Argentina, but told Fox reporters earlier in the day: “It’s hard to bet against [Lionel] Messi.”

"I thought about it a lot. I knew that was a question. I hate to get involved, even though politically, it doesn't matter so much. The head of Argentina is a friend of mine, he's done a terrific job. But I would say that it's hard to bet against Messi," Trump told Fox’s Jenny Taft. "I won't pick sides. I just think it's very hard to bet against Messi. He's great."

He described his idea for helping FIFA avoid controversy by allowing the U.S. to host again in the near future, adding: “I had a great idea for Gianni. I said: ‘You have to do two countries. So announce us for next time, and then announce another country after that and it’ll take out some of the anger and the shock!’ Now I think it’s a great idea. Based on the numbers, we will be requesting it again immediately. I said, to take out the shock, you could announce another country for the next one... but we have to do this again.”

The president sparked anger among football (soccer) fans after he called on a FIFA referee to overturn a red card against a player on the U.S. team before their elimination earlier this month. That incident put a sour note over that has generally been a successful effort by the U.S. to host the World Cup, which played out in more than a dozen stadiums across the U.S., Canada and Mexico this year. Roughly 10 million people were projected to travel to the three countries to witness the games.

The next FIFA World Cup tournament will be primarily hosted by Morocco, Portugal, and Spain, and the 2034 event will be held in Saudi Arabia.

The earliest the U.S. could concievably host the next World Cup would be 2038, or nine years after Trump leaves office.

News.title: Spain v Argentina LIVE: Fascinating World Cup final sees Messi takes on Yamal
News.content:
Moment Messi responds to photo with baby Yamal ahead of World Cup Final

Footballing giants Argentina and Spain will clash in a blockbuster World Cup final, as Lionel Messi graces this stage for perhaps the final time.

All-time great Messi, 39, will look to lead Argentina – who broke English hearts by coming from behind to win their semi-final – to a second straight World Cup trophy and the nation’s fourth overall, after triumphs in 1978, 1986 and 2022.

But they face formidable foes in the reigning European champions: Spain, who are seeking their second-ever world championship, having previously lifted the trophy in 2010. La Roja were superb as they downed France with a clinical 2-0 win in the last four and also have 19-year-old star Lamine Yamal in their ranks, a winger who can change any game in an instant.

There have been chaotic scenes outside the New York New Jersey Stadium ahead of the match however, with a Fifa system glitch meaning tickets are unable to be scanned properly and lengthy queues forming.

Donald Trump has revealed he is backing Argentina to win today’s World Cup final, saying: “It’s hard to bet against Messi.”

The president is set to present the World Cup trophy to the winner of the Sunday game between Argentina and Spain.

Speaking to Fox ahead of the match, Trump was asked who he thought would triumph and said he’d been giving the question a lot of thought as he “knew” they would ask.

After describing Argentinian president Javier Milei as a “friend of mine” who has done a “terrific job”, Trump declared that he thought the South American country would come out on top because of their star player.

He went on to describe Messi’s game-winning assist in the semi-final against England, saying: “I watched that pass... I guess you’d call it a pass... that was perfect. If you had a strike zone, it was exactly where it had to be. I watched also just before that, the way he got away from the defender. He was very well defended, and then all of a sudden he was standing by himself... It’s hard to bet against Messi, he’s great.”

President Donald Trump reveals he's backing Argentina ahead of the Fifa World Cup final ( Fox Sports )

Trump declined to be drawn on whether Messi is the greatest player of all time, citing his friendship with Cristiano Ronaldo and his memories of watching Pele play for the New York Cosmos.

“I got to see Pele play, and he was great,” said the president. “Look, these are great players, and there are others. Look at France, he had a rough game the other day, but he’s [Mbappe] certainly one of the greats. I get this information from my son. My son Barron is a tremendous soccer fan.”

He continued: “You have some other really incredible players playing here, but I would say right now, when you look, I’ve always liked Ronaldo and I’ve always liked Messi. I met Messi just recently, and I have known Cristiano, and they have a pretty good life. I think they have a pretty good life, actually, much easier than my life! I’d like to switch for about a month or so.”

Asked when he would like to see the World Cup return to the United States, Trump said he had “an idea” for Fifa President Gianni Infantino.

“He got it all started, and I brilliantly said: ‘Well, we’ll do it, but you could have a lot of empty stadiums!’ Didn’t work out that way, I think they were 99.9 per cent full, I think they were overflowing actually,” said the president.

He added: “I had a great idea for Gianni. I said: ‘You have to do two countries. So announce us for next time, and then announce another country after that and it’ll take out some of the anger and the shock!’ Now I think it’s a great idea. Based on the numbers, we will be requesting it again immediately. I said, to take out the shock, you could announce another country for the next one... but we have to do this again. You hear that, Gianni?”

The World Cup 2026 final is drawing closer with Spain booking their place in Sunday’s match in New Jersey after a fine display to beat France 2-0.

England battle Argentina in tonight’s other semi-final in Atlanta to decide the other finalist.

But Fifa President Gianni Infantino has modernised the tournament with influence from its co-hosts United States and the way some of its biggest sporting events operate, including the Super Bowl in the NFL.

This will mean a half-time show appealing to more forms of culture and new fans.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Fifa World Cup 2026 final half-time show:

When and where is the half-time show?

The half-time show will be on Sunday, 19 July 2026 at New York New Jersey Stadium, USA, the location for the final match, with kick-off set at 8pm BST (3pm ET), the half-time show is due to start from 8:50pm BST (3:50pm ET), with stoppage time and additional time to set up the stage and infrastructure perhaps leading to a start time after 9pm BST (4pm ET).

open image in gallery A view of MetLife Stadium in New Jersey ( AFP/Getty )

How long will the half-time show last?

Sources tell the Independent that the show will be around 20 minutes. There is the prospect of the usual 15-minute half-time break, followed by the planned 11-minute show, with Infantino emphasising the figure is inspired by 11 players on the pitch for each team.

Due to the laws of the game, governed by Ifab (the International Football Association Board), it is understood half-time breaks should “not exceed15 minutes,” but Sunday is due to break that law.

There is a precedent set from last year’s Club World Cup final between eventual winners Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, which was also organised by Fifa and held in the same venue in New Jersey. That show lasted 24 minutes, with Coldplay, J Balvin, Doja Cat, Tems and Emmanuel Kelly featuring.

open image in gallery Tems, Doja Cat, Emmanuel Kelly, Chris Martin of Coldplay and J Balvin perform during the halftime show during the FIFA Club World Cup 2025 Final ( Getty )

Where can I watch the half-time show?

The game is on both BBC and ITV in the UK, with ITV revealing that it will broadcast the entire World Cup half-time show at the New York New Jersey Stadium, as well as match analysis.

The BBC will confirm its plans in the coming hours. Alternatively you can follow The Independent’s coverage in our live blog, which will be packed with updates from the show and reaction from social media and our reporters in the stadium.

Who is performing at the half-time show?

The 11-minute Super Bowl-style show will be co-headlined by Madonna, Shakira and K-pop boy band BTS.

Justin Bieber was added to the bill, while Burna Boy, Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay also involved, and Chris Martin has curated the show.

open image in gallery Singer Shakira and her sons Sasha and Milan in the stand during Argentina v Austria ( Reuters )

Is there a closing ceremony and how is performing?

The closing ceremony starts at 18:30 BST (1:30pm ET), with the show including Tom Cruise, Laura Pausini, Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams and IShowSpeed. And Jennifer Hudson is to sing the United States' national anthem.

News.title: ICE now required to wear body cameras for most traffic stops after fatal shootings, Trump’s border czar says
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents will be required to wear at least one body camera during most traffic stops, according to the Trump administration’s border czar, after ICE officers without cameras fatally shot two people in the span of a week this month.

Agents will be required to use the body-worn cameras “whenever possible,” White House border czar Tom Homan said in an interview on Fox & Friends on Sunday.

“I’m a big proponent of body cams, always have been,” Homan said.

“They exonerate more law enforcement than they convict, and I want officers to wear body cameras because I want the American people to see what the officer saw when they took that action.”

In a separate interview on Sunday with Face the Nation on CBS News, Homan blamed recent Democrat-led government shutdowns for delaying the rollout of ICE body cameras.

open image in gallery ICE agents will be required to wear body cameras during most traffic stops, according to the Trump administration, after a string of recent fatal shootings ( Getty )

“Everybody in ICE would have a camera now if the government wasn’t shut down by Democratic members of Congress,” said Homan, adding that cameras are being purchased and deployed now, while officers are being trained on how to incorporate the cameras into operations.

ICE told The Independent earlier this week that more than half of its field offices already have body cameras deployed, with the remaining offices set to receive the cameras within the next 60 days.

The new requirement comes after ICE agents without cameras fatally shot two men during vehicle stops in Houston, Texas and Maine within one week.

Those men were not the intended target of immigration enforcement operations, prompting widespread protests and calls for accountability.

Critics of the Trump administration argue such cameras are necessary, given that White House officials have often made misleading claims about the facts of high-profile incidents involving Department of Homeland Security officers using lethal force.

open image in gallery ICE agents were not wearing body cameras during the recent shootings of Joan Sebastian Guerrero in Maine and Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas, despite a push earlier this year to equip agents ( Reuters )

“Even if the government is telling the truth, however, most Americans no longer give the Trump administration the benefit of the doubt,”The Washington Post’s editorial board wrote Monday. “DHS has made these situations more combustible by squandering credibility in previous cases when force was used.”

At the beginning of this year, after immigration agents carried out a pair of fatal shootings against protesters in Minnesota, then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem vowed that agents nationwide would soon be equipped with body-worn cameras, and the agency was awarded an additional $20 million in April to aid in getting cameras into the field.

open image in gallery The Trump administration claims recent government shutdowns slowed the rollout of ICE body cameras ( Reuters )

Even with a change in body camera policy, ICE continues to face scrutiny over the shootings in Texas and Maine.

The brother of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, the 52-year-old Mexican national who was fatally shot by an ICE agent in Houston, claims they were unaware that the unmarked cars following them were federal agents. Homan told Face the Nation he had not seen video evidence that the officers turned on their emergency lights in the operation.

In Monday’s shooting in Biddeford, Maine, in which an ICE agent killed Joan Sebastian Guerrero, a 26-year-old father with work authorization, a witness told Reuters he heard the victim tell law enforcement, “I tried to stop.”

An ex-wife of the agent accused of committing the Maine shooting told The Independent she had long worried about his temperament, but ICE failed to properly vet him.

“For years, I told people he was going to hurt somebody,” she told The Independent.

ICE appeared to suggest that The Independent’s reporting on that subject was an attempt to “dox our law enforcement officers” and did not respond directly to the claims.

The shootings briefly prompted a pause in ICE vehicle stops, though President Donald Trump ordered agents to resume the stops on Wednesday, calling them one of the agency’s “most important and effective Crime Fighting tools” in a social media post.

News.title: Harry Kane backs Thomas Tuchel to stay on as England boss after World Cup heartbreak
News.content:

Harry Kane admitted England will be “grieving” their World Cup heartbreak for some time to come although he backed Thomas Tuchel to stay on as head coach.

England were five minutes of normal time away from a first men’s final in 60 years but Argentina turned a 1-0 deficit in Atlanta on Wednesday into a 2-1 victory courtesy of two late goals.

While England rebounded with a dizzying 6-4 win over France in Saturday’s bronze-medal match in Miami, Kane believes he and his team-mates will be licking their wounds at their near-miss for a while.

“Of course we’re still feeling it from the other night, the emotion and the what ifs,” the England captain said. “That will be with us for a while now.

“We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks.

“Every time you get closer, knock on the door. You think you’ve learned and you have but we just have to keep going.”

Tuchel’s tactics in the final half hour against Argentina, making a number of defensive substitutions that exposed England to wave after wave of attack from their opponents, have drawn scorn from far and wide.

open image in gallery Harry Kane scored six goals during the World Cup (Bradley Collyer/PA) ( PA Wire )

Even Donald Trump questioned the decorated German’s approach, with the United States president flummoxed by how Kane was used after England had taken the lead via Anthony Gordon after 55 minutes.

But Kane, who revealed last week he had a round of golf with Trump around 18 months ago in Florida, threw his weight behind the England boss, who presided over their best result since their 1966 triumph.

“It’s our highest finish in 60 years,” Kane said. “The enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has. It doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time.

“He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year. That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way.

“Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself. It won’t be until the next camp where you think about what the future holds and what the next target is.

open image in gallery England player ratings in their win over France (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

“We’ll have conversations as captain and manager and with other team-mates and staff, to see where we can be better.”

In the aftermath of the Argentina defeat, Kane spoke cryptically about England “missing that final piece of the jigsaw”.

Elaborating further, the 32-year-old Bayern Munich striker added: “The last 30 minutes of Argentina is not the team we want to be.

“We spent a lot of time over the last two years talking about that situation, to attack those moments. The bottom line is we lost anyway.

open image in gallery Kane captained England to their best finish at a World Cup since 1966 (Martin Rickett/PA) ( PA Wire )

“It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations.

“We can train, play the qualifiers… I think the Nations League will be big for us, against Spain and Croatia, big teams.

“Getting used to those big environments and finding our best form against those teams, like we did against France – albeit not in the most competitive match.

“We have to learn, improve. The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.”

News.title: Ryan Fox matches father Grant’s sporting folklore with Claret Jug
News.content:
It’s the final day of the Open Championship, golf’s oldest and most-prestigious major. The leaderboard offers up hope of a seesaw day where little-known-of golfers tussle it out with big names under the north-west English sun. All in all, it should be an exciting day.

But, as with the past two days, we head into the round with talk dominated by a certain Bryson DeChambeau. It’s as frustrating and annoying as it is, in these days dominated by social media/content etc etc, painfully predictable. So let’s get the DeChambeau news out the way. Having been fairly hit with a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on Friday, the YouTube content creator had a tantrum, threatened to withdraw, caused a delay in the release of third-round tee times, before turning up and shooting a one-under 69 to lie four behind the leader heading into today.

That’s not all, The Bryson DeChambeau Show carried on after yesterday’s round where James Corrigan takes up the script...

Bryson DeChambeau marched straight to the offices of the R&A after being heckled with a cry of “you’re a cheat” on Birkdale’s 18th green on Saturday. As the controversy over his two-shot penalty from Friday’s second round rumbled on, Telegraph Sport understands DeChambeau, who shot a third-round 69 to lie four shots off the lead of the Open, asked R&A chief executive Mark Darbon for his scorecard from Friday. It is against policy so his request was rejected. DeChambeau then went back to the recorder’s hut and asked if they had it. Again, the answer was in the negative. It is unclear why he wanted it, but a theory emerged that he wished to put it on his social media channels.

All in all it is pathetic posturing that you’d expect from a stroppy teenager. He’s only three off the lead and has the game to win at Royal Birkdale, he’d do well to forget the perceived slights (whatever they may be) and get on with trying to win the Claret Jug.

Oh, and to add another scene to the soap opera Rory McIlroy doubtless spoke for many inside and outside the rope when he called out DeChambeau saying: “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson. I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention. To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.”

So, I think it’s best we focus on the golf today and not the theatrics and sorry antics of the American.

Sam Burns, his playing partner yesterday, was brilliant as he backed up his 62 of Friday with a five-under 65. He leads by two on 10 under and is the man to beat. Lurking behind with intent are a host of big names and big hitters – Ryan Fox (eight under), Si Woo Kim (eight under), Lucas Herbert (six under), Ludvig Aberg (seven under) and the man himself YouTube’s very own DeChambeau (six under).

Also in with a hint of a hope is Tommy Fleetwood, the hometown boy in search of his first major, the Englishman will start the round on five under.

Stay here for all the action, where I hope all the talk during and after the day’s round is focused on the winner’s brilliance rather than the emotions of DeChambeau.

News.title: England set Lord’s record score in victory over India
News.content:
When he fell, bowled trying to sweep Bethell, India were 260 for two, still a tough ask but not impossible, especially against an England side with plenty of demons. Kohli fired up in Rohit’s absence, hitting Will Jacks for two sixes and Bethell into the pavilion.

But the run-rate faltered as Curran whipped out his slower-ball bag of tricks. He had Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer caught in the deep by sub Rehan Ahmed in the 44th over and Kohli in the next, slapping a catch to cover. The rest subsided, India short in the end at 360 for seven.

England’s ODI side have struggled for runs under Brendon McCullum and this was easily their best batting performance, not just for the collection of records but for the calm, controlled way they went about setting a huge total. The openers Duckett and Bethell gave them a 191-run cushion, Root was impregnable again and Buttler finished it off, proving what he can do when others give him a platform. India were without Jasprit Bumrah but that should not take the shine off England’s achievements.

This was the first Duckett-Bethell opening contribution and it was England’s highest for the first wicket since the last World Cup. Jason Roy and Jonny Bairstow were such an important part of the route to World Cup glory and they left a huge hole in the side. Duckett and Bethell are more touch players, capable of gear shifts rather than setting out at turbo pace like Roy and Bairstow. The fact they bat so often together in Test cricket, where Bethell appears at No 3, helps the level of understanding.

Duckett’s innings knocked Viv Richards’s 138 in the 1979 World Cup final off the top spot at Lord’s and continued the form he showed at the end of the New Zealand Test series when he scored his first Test hundred in nearly a year. He was out first ball in the second ODI in Cardiff but was never in any real bother at Lord’s as he compiled a fourth century in this format.

News.title: Antonelli wins Belgian Grand Prix to extend championship lead after Russell crashes out
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

Sports.title: What are the Argentina national anthem lyrics? All words in English to iconic song and reason behind shortened version
Sports.content:
ARGENTINA are looking to become just the third nation in history to win successive World Cups TONIGHT!

But before the match takes place, fans around the world get to hear their national anthem.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

SunSport has all the details on the Argentinian anthem.

Why is the Argentina national anthem shortened?

The first Argentinian anthem was composed as early as 1810, before it was adopted as the official song three years later following the Revolution.



Its lyrics were written by the Buenos Aires-born Vicente Lopez y Planes, whilst the music was composed by a Spaniard, Blas Parera.

There is a long, anti-Spain section in the middle of the piece which has been omitted since 1924 – and the whole piece is extremely long.

As a result, in the Olympics, rugby games and at the World Cup, only the instrumental introduction (which lasts 1 minute 6 seconds) is played.

WORLD CUP FINAL LIVE: ALL THE LATEST FROM SPAIN VS ARGENTINA

What are the Argentina national anthem lyrics?

The anthem is simply known as the Himno Nacional Argentino.

It had previous names that translated as the Marcha Patriotica (Patriotic March) or Cancion Patriotica Nacional (National Patriotic Song).

Full lyrics

Sports.title: Why do Spain not sing their national anthem?
Sports.content:
SPAIN face Argentina in TONIGHT’S World Cup final – but fans have noticed something strange when the national anthem plays.

Unlike almost every other nation at the tournament, none of the players sing along to the music. Here’s everything we know about why.



Why does Spain’s national anthem have no official lyrics?

The Marcha Real (Royal March) is one of just four national anthems in the world with no official lyrics, alongside those of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo and San Marino.

It dates back to 1761, when it was composed by Manuel de Espinosa de los Monteros and documented in a book of military calls for the Spanish infantry, where it appeared under the title Marcha Granadera.



It was adopted as a state anthem in 1770, and later became the national anthem during Queen Isabella II’s reign (1833-68).

WORLD CUP FINAL LIVE: ALL THE LATEST FROM SPAIN VS ARGENTINA

Has the Spanish national anthem ever had lyrics?

The anthem briefly had competition during Spain’s Second Republic between 1930 and 1939, when the Himno de Riego was used instead.

After taking power in 1939, General Francisco Franco reinstated the Marcha Real, this time with updated lyrics by the poet Jose Maria Peman, celebrating the “rebirth” of Spain under his rule.

Those lyrics were dropped not long after the dictator died in 1975, and the anthem has remained wordless ever since.

Attempts to bring back official lyrics have repeatedly failed.

In 2007, the Spanish Olympic Committee ran a public competition and selected a winning entry from over 7,000 entries.



But it was scrapped within days following a public backlash to the proposed lyrics, which opened with “Viva Espana”.

What do Spain’s players and fans do during the anthem?

With no words to sing, Spain’s players simply stand in silence as the anthem plays.

Supporters in the stands sometimes hum or sing “lo lo lo” along to the melody.

The lack of lyrics has occasionally sparked confusion among fans unfamiliar with the anthem.

Some viewers have even mistakenly accused Spanish footballers of disrespecting their own country.



Spain have impressed on their way to the last four, building on their Euro 2024 triumph, where they beat England in the final.

Sports.title: Harry Kane admits England fans SHOULD be upset after dismal World Cup exit to Argentina but vows team will ‘improve’
Sports.content:
HARRY KANE can finally put his feet up after the most extraordinary season of his life.

After delivering an incredible tally of 73 goals in 65 games, the England captain will take a few weeks off, presumably with a golf club in hand, before focusing on another season with Bayern Munich.



Yet the England captain admits he will once again reflect on another missed chance, another summer tournament where England had high hopes but failed to achieve what they dreamed of.

A bronze medal after beating France 6-4 in Saturday’s third place play-off against France is no consolation.



And Kane accepts that England fans have every right to be frustrated and angry.

Kane said: “The last 30 minutes of Argentina is not the team we want to be. We spent a lot of time over the last two years talking about that situation, to attack those moments.



“The bottom line is we lost anyway. It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations.

“We can train, play the qualifiers… I think the Nations League will be big for us, against Spain and Croatia, big teams.

“We have to learn, improve. The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.

“It’s so hard. I think the fans are behind the team and are behind the manager.

“But when something like this happens it’s very emotional – and rightly so. We’ve all been England fans when we wished we’d done this or that and it didn’t quite happen. That will die down naturally.

“Before we know it, we’ll, be back with our clubs and the focus shifts to Champions League or the Nations League.

“Things do move quickly. Fans have a right to be emotional, sad and angry. We all are, we all feel it.

“We have a chance to change it but it wasn’t to be this year. There is still a lot of positives to take from this, competing against the odds away from home and you finish third. Keep your chin on and go again.

“Every time you get closer, knock on the door. You think you’ve learned and you have but we just have to keep going.”



Kane scored six goals at the World Cup but did not feature in Saturday’s bizarre game.

Asked for his reflections on the tournament, he said: “A lot of positives. It’s the highest finish in 60 years, the highest finish on foreign soil. There is a lot to be proud of.

“Of course we’re still feeling it from the other night, the emotion and the what ifs. That will be with us for a while now.

“I’m proud of the boys, how we approached the France game. It wasn’t easy to find the mentality.

“We said before that every time you represent England it should be a proud moment. It’s the least we deserved, to grab a medal.



“We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.

“Fans are going to be angry and we understand it. It’s a major tournament and that’s why you dream so big.

“When it doesn’t go your way you have to take the criticism. We’re all willing to do that, to dare to reach the biggest goal of all.”

England’s problem is that Kane will be 34 when they co-host the Euros in two years. Providing he remains injury-free, he still be one of the best strikers in the planet but right now, he is THE best in that position.

So even if England win Euro 2028, which they will be one of the favourites, they will always look back on this tournament with a sense of regret.



The same applies to Tuchel, regardless of this being his first international tournament.

One thing that will stay in the memory was this weird 10-goal game against France. Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick with Ezri Konsa, Declan Rice and Jude Bellingham on target.

Kylian Mbappe got a double with Bradley Barcola and Ousmane Dembele getting the others for France. The stand-out goal was Bellingham’s individual strike which made it 6-4.



Kane said: “The game was impossible to judge because it was a complete opposite to what it would’ve been if it was a final.

England secured their best finish at a World Cup since 1966 by beating France in the bronze playoff on Saturday evening and Three Lions' captain Kane has issued a message to his teammates

Harry Kane insists England should be “proud” of their World Cup - even if it will take time to get over the disappointment.

‌



England produced one of the all-time great World Cup matches in their ten goal thriller with France which also delivered their best performance in the tournament on foreign soil.

‌



Thomas Tuchel’s men left the United States with a bronze medal even if Kane says the whole squad is still wracked with regret and disappointment.

‌



England captain Kane said: “A lot of positives. Obviously people are going to be talking about it already. It’s the highest finish in 60 years, the highest finish on foreign soil. There is a lot to be proud of.

“Of course we’re still feeling it from the other night, the emotion and the what ifs. That will be with us for a while now.

“I’m proud of the boys, how we approached this game. It wasn’t easy to find the mentality. We said before that every time you represent England it should be a proud moment. It’s the least we deserved, to grab a medal.

‌

“The game is impossible to judge because it’s a complete opposite to what that would’ve been if it was a final. It shows the quality we have. To score six against anyone you have to play a certain way and play well.

“Every time you get closer, knock on the door. You think you’ve learned and you have but we just have to keep going.”

Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick, Declan Rice was on target and provided an assist for Ezri Konsa while Jude Bellingham got a brilliant sixth to finally put the game to bed.

‌



France mounted an astonishing comeback from 4-0 down at half time as Kylian Mbappe scored twice, Bradley Barcola was on target while Ousmane Dembele also scored.

‌

Football does move quickly and the heroics in Mexico City followed by the win against Norway are forgotten amid the collapse against Argentina.

But, equally, this should be a game-changer in the other direction. Tuchel needed a quick reaction and it felt like his players, despite the heartbreak, wanted to send a message.

‌



View 4 Images Harry Kane speaks with Thomas Tuchel (Image: Getty Images)

Even if that message was partly what might have been. Saka hit a hat trick and was brilliant which quickly leaves everyone cursing Tuchel for not playing him more.

But that is unfair because Saka has not been at his best. Rice was also brilliant as he wore the armband but he has also struggled because of fitness issues.

‌



Rather than look back with recriminations, England need to embrace the first half performance and enjoy the positives and energy. Eberechi Eze driving forward from midfield. Djed Spence having another blinder. Marc Guehi and Konsa defending well.

This was France and, despite the fightback and crazy nature of the game, England lost in their last two third-place games in 1990 and 2018 and so this was something to be proud of no matter the fact they wished the game had been the final.

View 4 Images England's third place finish is their best at a World Cup since 1966 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Kane was given a rare day off but talked as captain on behalf of the group and now believes they must use the failings as “motivation” but also learn from their mistakes and take them into the Nations League campaign and Euro 2028.

Kane added: “It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations. We can train, play the qualifiers… I think the Nations League will be big for us, against Spain and Croatia, big teams.

“Getting used to those big environments and finding our best form against those teams, like we did against France – albeit not in the most competitive match. We have to learn, improve.

‌



“The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.

“We still showed signs of what we showed the other night unfortunately, when they started to come back into the game. We couldn’t quite get the pressure on the ball and keep the ball. There is stuff we need to improve on.

“We know over the next two years until we’re facing that situation again there is always going to be a question mark. It’s something we have to take and use as motivation.”

Sports.title: 'My heart really sank' - Hamilton relieved mechanic unhurt after hit
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says his "heart really sank" when his Ferrari car hit a mechanic in a pit stop in an incident that saw the team fined heavily by Belgian Grand Prix stewards.

Hamilton's right-front tyre struck the mechanic after the driver was given the green signal to leave the team's pit box, briefly knocking the crew member - who was in front of the wheel in an attempt to make a front-wing adjustment - to his knees. Hamilton promptly stopped his car as the mechanic, who was unhurt, was helped to his feet.

The incident was placed under a post-race stewards' investigation with Ferrari later handed a €30,000 fine, €10,000 of which is suspended for a year.

With no sporting sanction imposed on the driver, who stewards said had suffered a "sporting disadvantage" in any case due to the fact he was delayed at the pit stop, Hamilton retained his fourth-place finish in the race.

The result moved Hamilton back into second place ahead of George Russell in the Drivers' Championship with a deficit of 45 points to Kimi Antonelli, the race winner at Spa-Francorchamps.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix.

Speaking about the pit stop confusion after the race, Hamilton said his mind had immediately flashed back to an incident at the 2018 Bahrain Grand Prix when a botched Ferrari stop involving Kimi Raikkonen caused a mechanic, Francesco Cigarini, to suffer a double leg fracture.

Hamilton was therefore relieved as he enquired about the mechanic over team radio on his return to the track that he had been unhurt.

"The green light went and so I went," said Hamilton to Sky Sports F1.

"You're looking over here [to the left at the lights] you're not looking over there so that's more probably on the team, ultimately.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Despite being given a five-second penalty for an opening lap collision with George Russell, Lewis Hamilton was left more frustrated with his performance over the weekend as he finished fourth in Belgium.

"But when it happened, then I noticed him and I stopped and it just went through my mind in that moment was back when Kimi hit and broke a leg and my heart really sank for a second.

"I'm really grateful he's ok."

'We could have been challenging for the win' - Hamilton rues consequence of his Saturday crash

Hamilton's stop had already been elongated by the fact that Ferrari's crew had first had to wait five seconds before starting the car's tyre change owing to the serving of a time penalty for causing a collision with Russell at Les Combes on the opening lap.

The clash spun Russell out of the race although the Mercedes driver later blamed his own car's straight-line speed issues, rather than former team-mate Hamilton, for the incident at the end of the long Kemmel Straight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

Hamilton also preferred not to focus on the specifics of the collision, instead taking the blame for not qualifying higher than sixth, which became fifth on the grid, after crashing in Saturday's final practice session.

"I don't count on myself [being] unlucky, I think about my mistake that I made yesterday, so I take full responsibility really for the fourth place that I ended up getting," he said.

"I damaged the car then when they rebuilt the car they missed something on the suspension so the balance was completely different so it meant I was probably a good couple of tenths - maybe three tenths - slower than I should have been in qualifying.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow.

"Then I ended up further back, got in the incident. Five second penalty, so like a domino effect from a mistake from myself.

"But the team have been doing a great job with strategy, pit stops. We are continuing to improve the car. I think our pace today, without the damage, we could have been challenging for the win."

Sports.title: Antonelli takes big Belgian GP win as Russell's title woes deepen
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli overcame an unfortunately-timed Virtual Safety Car to overtake Charles Leclerc and win the Belgian Grand Prix on a day team-mate George Russell's title hopes suffered a major fresh blow.

Antonelli doubled his in-house advantage over Russell to 50 points after the Briton was spun out into the gravel at the fifth corner of the first lap in a collision with Lewis Hamilton that stewards judged the Ferrari driver was at fault for.

Hamilton was given a five-second penalty, which he served at his sole pit stop, and eventually finished fourth after overtaking McLaren's Oscar Piastri late on.

Hamilton and Ferrari faced a post-race investigation for an alleged unsafe Ferrari release at the same pit stop.

A mechanic was struck by the Ferrari's front-right tyre and was briefly knocked to his knees before being helped back up to his feet before Hamilton, who had stopped the car having incorrectly been given the signal to leave, fully exited the pit box. Ferrari were fined €30,000, of which a third was suspended for 12 months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari pit crew were unable to attach Lewis Hamilton's front wing as the British driver also knocked over a mechanic after being given the green light

Hamilton moves back ahead of Russell in second to Antonelli in the standings - 45 points behind the Italian, with one race to go in Hungary this coming week before F1's summer break.

Max Verstappen, who briefly took the lead from Antonelli on the first lap into Eau Rouge before the Mercedes almost immediately blasted back past, took third after he was also jumped by Leclerc during the VSC.

Isack Hadjar drove strongly to finish sixth in the second Red Bull from the back row, opportunistically making his first pit stop under the early Safety Car.

He just held off Lando Norris, who was on significantly fresher tyres, after the McLaren had run all the way to lap 30 before making his one pit stop having started a penalised 13th on the grid.

Gabriel Bortoleto was eighth for Audi ahead of Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto.

Belgian GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Lando Norris, McLaren



8) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



10) Franco Colapinto, Alpine

How faultless Antonelli was made to win the hard way

Mercedes' world championship leader had been the big favourite to win the race after qualifying on a dominant pole position but the 19-year-old's route to victory on Sunday did not prove quite as straightforward as many had expected across a tense 44 laps of racing at Spa-Francorchamps.

Antonelli had, though, always expected a battle to hold his lead through the first lap of the race from fellow front-row-starter Verstappen in particular due to the slipstream-friendly nature of the opening part of the undulating, power-sensitive Belgian lap.

He held the lead on the short initial run to La Source but, amid different approaches to energy deployment, was overtaken by Verstappen before the bottom of the fast run into Eau Rouge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

But Antonelli had more battery power in hand for the long Kemmel Straight and duly breezed straight back past the Red Bull before the next braking zone from Les Combes. Leclerc, meanwhile, had made an impressive start from fourth place and also passed Verstappen for second at the same point of the circuit.

Verstappen got back ahead of the Ferrari into second on lap six and, impressively given pre-race expectations, managed to keep Antonelli in view up front. He was less than three seconds behind the Mercedes when he pitted first on lap 17. Antonelli stopped a lap later and stayed ahead of the Red Bull to maintain the net lead.

But Ferrari had kept both their drivers out for longer and benefitted when, on lap 20, the Virtual Safety Car was initiated. This allowed their drivers relatively 'cheap' pit stops and, while Hamilton ran into problems in addition to having to first serve his penalty for the Russell collision, Leclerc was able to jump Antonelli and Verstappen into the lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings.

The gap between Leclerc and Antonelli was three seconds but the Mercedes simply had too much speed and on lap 34 regained the lead with a pass down the Kemmel Straight.

Antonelli went on to win by 1.9s and said after his first win in four races: "It's great to be back on the top step after obviously a few difficult rounds.

"It was a hard-fought race. We lost first place with a VSC but then we managed to make our way back.

"It was a tough win because Charles was quick and we had to hold onto them."

Second place follows Leclerc's victory at Silverstone a fortnight ago and the Monegasque said: "I believed in the win until the end.

"We had a little bit of luck with the VSC at the right time for us but the pace was relatively strong.

"There were five or six laps on the hard tyres when I was struggling with the front axle, then it came back a little bit."

Russell bemoans Mercedes straight-line speed issues after Hamilton tangle

Race day could barely have gone any worse for Russell in the other title-contending Mercedes car.

The Briton had qualified third, a position he held until the long Kemmel Straight when both Ferraris drafted past him and he also came under attack from Piastri's McLaren.

Russell attempted to come back at Hamilton on the outside of his compatriot under braking for the right-handed turn into Les Combes, but the Ferrari suffered understeer and tagged the Mercedes' right-rear wheel, spinning it round into the gravel.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch from onboard with George Russell as he crashes out of the Belgian GP after contact with Lewis Hamilton.

Stewards penalised Hamilton for the incident, but Russell instead took issue with the mysterious straight-line speed issues that had dogged his Mercedes all weekend.

"I just got totally swallowed up down the straight," said a dejected Russell.

"I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he (Hamilton) could have braked a bit more. The incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight."

Sports.title: Duckett, Curran the difference as England clinch India series in Lord's run-fest
Sports.content:
Ben Duckett's century and Sam Curran's late burst of wickets inspired England to a series-clinching 27-run win over India in the third ODI at Lord's.

Duckett struck a magnificent 141 from 135 balls, the highest individual ODI score at Lord's and his fourth century in the format, before a swashbuckling 41 from just 13 balls by Jos Buttler helped England post a daunting 387, setting India 388 to win.

Rohit Sharma led the chase with a superb 138 off 110 deliveries, registering his 34th ODI hundred and sharing century partnerships with Shubman Gill (77) and Virat Kohli (74) to keep India firmly on course.

India were 303-2 and needed 84 from the final 39 balls when a decisive seven-ball spell saw Curran dismiss Ishan Kishan (14), Shreyas Iyer (0) and Kohli, halting India's momentum as their chase fell 27 runs short.

After losing the series opener by six wickets at Edgbaston, England bounced back to secure a 2-1 ODI series victory over the world's top-ranked side, adding it to their 4-0 T20 series whitewash of India.

Sports.title: 'I reached rock bottom' - Antonelli admits shock as title charge accelerates
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli has admitted he couldn't have imagined being in a dominant position at the top of the Formula 1 world championship 12 months ago when he reached "rock bottom" during his rookie campaign.

Antonelli, 19, won the Belgian Grand Prix for Mercedes on Sunday to move 45 points clear of Lewis Hamilton at the top of the drivers' standings, with 10 of 22 currently scheduled rounds complete.

Having been fast-tracked in by Mercedes boss Toto Wolff to replace Hamilton following the seven-time world champion's decision to join Ferrari, Antonelli endured a chastening spell midway through his 2025 campaign.

The then 18-year-old went on a dismal run during which he finished above ninth just once in 10 grands prix, with one of the low points coming as he was knocked out in Q1 in Belgium last year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings

Asked after claiming his sixth victory of the season on Sunday whether he could have imagined this scenario a year ago, Antonelli replied: "No, absolutely not.

"Last year here, I probably reached the bottom, so it was a very difficult weekend for me mentally.

"But this year was definitely a lot better. If you had asked me last year at this moment, I probably would have said no."

Antonelli's advantage at the top of the standings could actually be far greater if it weren't for a spell of bad luck the Italian has endured in recent weeks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli wins the Belgian Grand Prix

He suffered an engine failure when running second to Hamilton in Barcelona, and then suffered a wheel-guard failure that dropped him out of the points at the British Grand Prix when he appeared to be on course to chase Charles Leclerc down for victory.

His pace dominance over his team-mate George Russell, who began the year as the clear title favourite, makes it hard to see how Antonelli can be caught unless Ferrari make major improvements to their inferior power unit in the near future.

Despite his strong position, Antonelli isn't dwelling on the increasing likelihood of him becoming by far the youngest driver to become an F1 world champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli joins Sky Sports' Karun Chandhok at the SkyPad to analyse the Italian's pole-setting lap at the Belgian Grand Prix

"I never want to relax too much," Antonelli told Sky Sports F1.

"Of course, it's a great result and good redemption after last year because last year was a very dark moment for me and to get the win is very special.

"But you can never relax because we have seen in the past how the situation can swing so quickly.

"So that's why it's important to really maximise and take every opportunity that is given and just make the best out of it because you never know what can happen."

Wolff: We're all surprised by Antonelli form

Wolff made the decision to give Antonelli one of the most desirable seats on the grid when several other strong options were available, and there were times during 2025 when the choice came under great scrutiny.

While Wolff says Antonelli's ups and downs during his debut campaign were expected, the Austrian admits the teenager's remarkable consistency in 2026 has "surprised" the whole team.

"We're all surprised, Wolff said. "I think the first season came as expected. Great moments where his talent shined through, and then moments which were very difficult - the long spell of lack of results in the middle of the season, as expected.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli goes past Mercedes teammate George Russell before retiring from the race with engine failure

"And then after the winter, also as expected, he knew the environment, he knew the pressures, he knew the demands of the team on the technical side, on the marketing side, knowing the tracks that we would go racing.

"But what was not expected is the serenity and structure that he brought into his game. With Kimi, whether the session was good or bad, you wouldn't see a difference in emotions in the debrief.

"It is absolutely transactional. What is the problem? How do we solve it? How do we move on? And that is new. And I think that's why it's almost when he wins, you can't see this absolute excitement that a 19-year-old would almost have."

Wolff highlighted Antonelli's reactions to the reliability issues that cost him in Barcelona and at Silverstone as further examples of his protégé's level-headedness.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Antonelli suffers damage during the British Grand Prix

Wolff added: "And at the same time, when he fails to deliver results, in Barcelona, when we had the car stoppage, or even in Silverstone, he comes back in and he was the one saying to the team, this is a mechanical sport, these things can happen.

"19 years old - that is very, very impressive to see. And I think this mindset and this attitude is probably one of the main drivers that has allowed the talent to shine so early in his career."

Sports.title: Russell blames Mercedes power issue for collision with Hamilton
Sports.content:
George Russell says a power issue with his Mercedes was to blame for leaving him vulnerable to a first-lap collision with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton that took him out of the Belgian Grand Prix.

Russell started third on the grid and retained his position through the first corner but was then passed by Hamilton and left side-by-side with McLaren's Oscar Piastri as they came to the end of the lengthy Kemmel Straight.

Russell broke late and attempted to reclaim third back around the outside of Hamilton, but the pair made contact which spun the Mercedes into the gravel and out of the race.

Despite Hamilton being given a five-second penalty by the stewards for causing the collision, Russell told Sky Sports F1 he was more frustrated with his car than his former team-mate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pointed to an issue with the car as a reason for his collision with Lewis Hamilton during the Belgian GP

"I just got totally swallowed up down the straight," said Russell, who dropped 50 points behind his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli after the championship leader won the race.

"I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he (Hamilton) could have braked a bit more. The incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight.

"Very, very disappointed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

The incident came after Russell had bemoaned a lack of power costing him in qualifying on Saturday, when he was more than half a second off pole-sitter Antonelli in fourth.

Russell has appeared confused in recent weeks as to what is causing him to generally be unable to match Antonelli's pace.

He said on Thursday's media day at Spa that he was working on changing his driving style as he believes that was costing him time in 2026's new generation of cars, but on Saturday revealed that he had changed his mind and no longer thought his driving style was the issue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell discusses his recent struggles with the Mercedes car and the gap between himself and teammate Kimi Antonelli

Asked how Mercedes can get to the bottom of the issue, Russell added: "I appreciate everyone is working hard to solve the problem, but I'm stood here [in the TV interview pen] on lap five of the race.

"It felt like I was in a good position to fight for the lead up to Turn One and then, suddenly, no power and it's all gone."

Wolff: Issue caused all Mercedes engines to lack power on straights

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said there was an issue with all of the team's engines that influenced power on the straights.

As well as building their own engines, Mercedes also supply McLaren, Alpine and Williams with power units.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "The accident that happened was unfortunate for us. We lost a lot of constructors' points and George's drivers' points.

"We had an issue on all Mercedes engines that we lacked the power out on the straights. That hit him badly and it 100 per cent goes on us.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok was at the SkyPad to analyse whether Lewis Hamilton should have been awarded a five-second penalty for his collision with George Russell on the opening lap

"We are trying our best as a team. We have the most powerful power unit, a strong car that is capable of winning.

"Everyone is giving their maximum to minimise the mistakes and still it happens because we are humans at work."

Mercedes have clearly had the fastest car over the opening 10 rounds of the season, but reliability issues have prevented them from building a points advantage to reflect their pace dominance.

Russell's DNF on Sunday was his second following an engine failure in Canada, while Antonelli retired in Barcelona because of an engine failure and then dropped from a likely victory to out of the points at Silverstone because of a wheel-guard failure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wins the Belgian Grand Prix

Wolff added: "We let Kimi down at Silverstone where George got a podium, which is maybe better than the result should have been.

"Then one DNF for Montreal, the other in Barcelona. That's a little bit of the story of our season. It's a technical sport, a mechanical sport.

"We came out with a product [power unit] that is so strong and I'd rather fix the reliability rather than accelerate a slow engine, or slow car.

"We are giving it 100 per cent and need to give it 100 per cent because we lost a lot of points with reliability. We should be much further ahead than we are."
