Sports.title: Fans left baffled by World Cup closing ceremony as YouTuber IShowSpeed performs in bizarre pregame show
Sports.content:
Popular streamer IShowSpeed kickstarted the World Cup final blockbuster with a surprise appearance in the FIFA closing ceremony following a morning of chaos in the buildup to the football extravaganza.

Defending champions Argentina bid to secure a second successive World Cup triumph in a showdown against Spain in front of 80,000 clamoring fans, including President Donald Trump, at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday.

Yet, even before the first kick of the game, the spectators inside the stadium, as well as the billions watching from home, were treated to an eye-catching spectacle, designed to pay tribute to all of the competing 48 nations from the tournament.

A bevy of Hollywood's finest had been billed as performers with Tom Cruise expected to headline the event, which took place 90 minutes ahead of kickoff.

However, it was YouTuber IShowSpeed who stole the show. The content creator - who has over 58 million subscribers on YouTube and streamed multiple matches - stunned fans by launching into song.

He had been listed as a performer but he surprised viewers when he began performing an original song, Champions, which was on the official 2026 World Cup album, amid a colorful array of backup dancers in neon tracksuits.

Popular streamer IShowSpeed kickstarted the World Cup final closing ceremony

The streamer surprised viewers when he began performing an original song, Champions

Tom Cruise had been expected to headline the ceremony before the World Cup final

Post Malone replaced IShowSpeed in the spotlight. More accustomed to performing, he opened with his new track 'Chrome Heartbreaker,' before leading into his 2018 song 'Wow' for his three-song performance.

He then brought out rapper Swae Lee to perform their grammy-nominated hit Sunflower.

Post, 31, rocked a classic Canadian tuxedo, accessorizing with his signature cowboy hat and sunglasses.

The American singer and rapper pulled aside his denim jacket to unveil a t-shirt that read: 'I just hope both teams have fun.' The shirt's message was a nod to Elmo's now-viral tweet ahead of the NBA Finals that left New Yorkers furious.

However, fans were left underwhelmed at the bizarre display with many bemoaning the lack of creativity while others questioned why a content creator was given the honor of performing on the world's biggest stage.

'Such an underwhelming closing ceremony. Zero creativity just artists singing,' one wrote on X.

'The lip syncing for these closing ceremony performances is horrific,' another shared.

'ishowspeed was so random,' said a third, while another baffled viewer branded it 'unreal scenes.'

The content creator performed at MetLife Stadium amid a neon swarm of dancers

IShowSpeed, who boasts over 58 million subscribers on YouTube, dressed in an all-white suit

Post Malone (right) performed his 2018 hit Sunflower with Swae Lee (left)

The closing ceremony took place 90 minutes before kickoff between Spain and Argentina

'Imagine telling someone a few years ago that ishowspeed is gonna perform at the world cup,' added a fifth.

Another went on: 'Worst closing ceremony.. obviously low budget.'

'The World Cup closing show was terrible - lousy production, just like the opening ceremony,' said one X user.

Cruise had been expected to be the main attraction and fans were left confused to see IShowSpeed dominating their screens rather than the legendary actor.

The Mission Impossible star has been spotted in the stands throughout the tournament and performed a stunt at the Paris Olympics' closing ceremony

His specific role was unclear, with FIFA merely teasing it as a 'special appearance' in its announcement. However, half an hour before kickoff, the Hollywood icon was still nowhere to be seen.

'WHERE THE F*** IS TOM CRUISE,' one furious social media user posted.

Tony winner and Pussycat Dolls alum Nicole Scherzinger was also slated to make an appearance, joined by Robbie Williams and Laura Pausini, the Italian singer who helped open the Milan Cortina Olympics.

Meanwhile, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson has been granted the honor of performing the US national anthem.

'Echoing the spirit of the opening ceremonies, which welcomed the world to the greatest stage in Canada, Mexico and the United States, the closing ceremony will bring the FIFA World Cup 2026 full circle through music, culture and football, before we kick off the highly anticipated match that will crown the champions of this groundbreaking tournament,' Heimo Schirgi, the World Cup's chief operating officer, had said before the tournament.

Post, 31, rocked a classic Canadian tuxedo, accessorizing with his signature cowboy hat

Fans were left underwhelmed at the bizarre display, slamming the 'random' performances

Mission Impossible star Cruise is pictured arriving at MetLife Stadium on Sunday morning

This year's showstopper is bigger and better than ever with the star-studded event also boasting the first-ever World Cup halftime show, featuring the likes of Madonna, Shakira and Justin Bieber.

The ceremony took place following a morning of chaos in New York and New Jersey as thousands of fans descended on the Big Apple region for the final.

Those lucky enough to have clinched a ticket - or forked out $10,000 for one - were urged to arrive up to four hours before the start of the game at the 80,000-seater stadium, a short drive outside of Manhattan.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

But it has become standard procedure for fans to arrive even earlier for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - lest they risk missing kickoff.

Trump has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl, and his attendance often means lengthy delays for fans with airport-style security measures enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

Delays on Sunday, however, were compounded amid reports of glitches in FIFA's ticket-scanning system, meaning those who were fortunate enough to be at the front of the long lines still faced frustrating delays.

Daily Mail also witnessed tensions simmering between fans, media members and security staff, with officials on the ground telling anyone who complained: 'Take it up with FIFA'.

Argentina fans arrive at MetLife Stadium before Sunday's hugely anticipated final vs Spain

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

But those members of security staff also appeared to be confused over how to manage the thousands of people arriving for the game.

There were multiple instances of organizers on the ground misdirecting people over where they should begin lining up to enter the stadium with over three hours to go until the start of the game.

Media members also faced extra checks from the secret service given the need to bring laptops and filming equipment inside of the stadium. DHS police and state police were also seen at the venue.

This all played out as other fans decided to leave it late to get to the stadium. With four hours to go until the game began, many supporters were still at Penn Station in Manhattan waiting to board a train into New Jersey and towards the stadium.

The game is set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

There weren't quite as many issues for the VIP guests, though. Cruise was pictured sauntering into the venue - renamed as 'New York/New Jersey Stadium' for the tournament - ahead of his anticipated appearance in the closing ceremony.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Lionel Messi and Co are hoping to seal back-to-back titles after winning the tournament in Qatar four years ago, while Spain have not won the World Cup since 2010.

At the end of the match, a new stage will be erected on the pitch to see either Messi or Rodri lift the World Cup for their country.

It is expected that Trump will be granted the honor of handing the trophy over to the victorious team.

The President carried out the same duties during the Club World Cup final, which also took place at MetLife Stadium.

He left the winning Chelsea stars, including Cole Palmer and Reece James, stunned when he remained on the stage throughout their celebrations.

Sports.title: Mayhem at World Cup final before Trump arrives as staff misdirect fans outside stadium and tension simmers over ticket issues - but Tom Cruise has no trouble getting in!
Sports.content:
World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

Organizers this week urged fans lucky enough to have a ticket to arrive up to four hours before the start of the game at the 80,000-seater stadium in New Jersey, a short drive outside of Manhattan, for Sunday's showdown between Spain and Argentina.

As the build-up to the game expected to be watched by billions around the world ramped up, fans were waiting for over four hours to have their tickets scanned in order to enter the stadium for the showpiece game.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

But the delays were compounded amid reports of glitches in FIFA's ticket-scanning system, meaning those who were fortunate enough to be at the front of the long lines still faced frustrating delays.

The Daily Mail also witnessed tensions simmering between fans, media members and security staff, with officials on the ground telling anyone who complained: 'Take it up with FIFA'.

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

There were reports of tech issues and security misdirecting people around the stadium

Argentina fans arrive at MetLife Stadium before Sunday's hugely anticipated final vs Spain

But those members of security staff also appeared to be confused over how to manage the thousands of people arriving for the game.

There were multiple instances of organizers on the ground misdirecting people over where they should begin lining up to enter the stadium with over three hours to go until the start of the game.

Sky's Rob Harris also posted on X from the stadium: 'Fans told to get to the World Cup final stadium now 4 hours before KO - already security staff saying FIFA system glitches not scanning passes and long queues forming. With extra security. People being misdirected around the stadium with a lack of stewarding and staffing.'

Brazilian journalist Mariana Spinelli said it took her four hours to make it in, writing on X: 'We've been in line for 2 hours for the x-ray to ENTER the stadium. Everything disorganized, a total chaos. If this were in South America, they'd call us animals, third-world country. Since it's in the US nobody says anything. A nightmare of organization, pathetic.'

Media members also faced extra checks from the secret service given the need to bring laptops and filming equipment inside of the stadium. DHS police and state police were also seen at the venue.

This all played out as other fans decided to leave it late to get to the stadium. With four hours to go until the game began, many supporters were still at Penn Station in Manhattan waiting to board a train into New Jersey and towards the stadium.

The game is set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

Extra security checks were in place ahead of the attendance of President Trump for the game

Tom Cruise had no such issue making his way inside before his closing ceremony appearance

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Even on the live television coverage, the stadium was bare with a little over an hour until that closing ceremony began.

There weren't quite as many issues for the VIP guests, though. Tom Cruise was pictured sauntering into the venue - renamed as 'New York/New Jersey Stadium' for the tournament - ahead of his anticipated appearance in the closing ceremony.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Fans were slow to fill the stadium despite a call for them be in place for the closing ceremony

There were plenty of fans who were determined not to let the chaos ruin their day, too. Thousands of Argentina fans have made the journey to the stadium for what will likely be star man Lionel Messi's last ever appearance in a World Cup at the age of 39.

Argentina are narrow underdogs against Spain, the European champions, despite being the holders after winning the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Trump is expected to hand the World Cup trophy over to the winning team after the game.

Sports.title: Terrified Zlatan Ibrahimovic swears live on TV during helicopter ride to World Cup final with Thierry Henry: 'If we go down, we go down together'
Sports.content:
He might be one of football's most braggadocious characters, but it turns out that Zlatan Ibrahimovic has a weak point after all: helicopter rides.

His fear of choppers is so great that he even admitted with a grin: 'I'm s*******in my pants!'

The Swedish giant, who stretches to 6ft5in and gave defenders nightmares throughout his career, looked petrified as he boarded a copter to the World Cup final.

Ibrahimovic, 44, has been working as a pundit for Fox Sports during the tournament alongside Thierry Henry and former United States star Alexi Lalas.

And after wiping some sweat off his brow, Ibrahimovic put on a brave face and tried to laugh off an impending flight to the final between Spain and Argentina in New Jersey.

He said: 'The adrenaline is pumping on the way, I'm s******* in my pants.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic admitted he was 's******* himself' ahead of a helicopter ride to the World Cup final

'I don't like helicopters but it's okay, I have Rebecca [Lowe, presenter] close to me, I have Thierry, I have Alexi.

'If we go down, we go down together.'

The former Manchester United, Barcelona, and Paris Saint-Germain striker was dressed to the nines in a cream suit for the air ride.

That was a departure from his attire on Saturday, when he went topless for a Cold as Balls interview show with Kevin Hart.

Zlatan doesn't tend to show vulnerability. He is known for his grandiose one-liners and self-exaltation, though it is often seen as an act.

He had this side to him even when he was a teenager. Offered a trial at Arsenal by Arsene Wenger, he recalls saying: 'I will not do a trial: either you take me or not, I'm not here to waste time.

'When I was young, in my mind no one was better than me.'

He has also said: 'I can't help but laugh at how perfect I am.'

Rebecca Lowe has spoken out on the tensions between Ibrahimovic and co-pundit Alexi Lalas

His personality has brought him into a jokey conflict with his co-pundit Lalas during the World Cup.

Recently, Fox World Cup host Lowe defiantly insisted that there is no tension between her colleagues Ibrahimovic and Lalas, despite multiple terse exchanges.

Ibrahimovic has branded Lalas 'the past' live on air and abruptly dismissed him for saying France were 'arrogant' in the first half against Senegal.

When Lalas then left the studio to report live from the Seattle stadium for the second United States group game, Ibrahimovic said: 'You're welcome, America.'

Footage also went viral from the Fox studio where the three analysts were playing soccer and Henry mercilessly tricked Lalas with a faked back heel while the cameras were rolling.

Host presenter Lowe, however, has insisted that the trio all get along fine when the cameras are off and claims that the suggestions of unrest behind the scenes is actually a source of amusement to all in the Fox setup.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Lowe said: 'These stories do make me laugh and we do laugh about them. We're like, "another one"? And it is getting a little out of hand.

'We are going through every newspaper now. Like, okay guys, maybe let's pivot and write about something else, that would be good. The football, maybe?'

Henry and Ibrahimovic posted a clip of themselves doing insane tricks, including one on Lalas

Lalas has attempted at times to get his own back, telling Ibrahimovic last weekend that his cream suit made him look like one of presenters on the 70s television show 'Fantasy Island'.

But Lowe says that amid the jokes the trio trade off at each other, there is an underlying respect between them all.

'There is nothing, there is no tension, nothing! We are laughing our heads off at all of this,' she added.

'Everybody respects everybody hugely. If people want to watch and listen to what the guys say to each other and work off each other, they would see that.

'It's a strange old narrative when you're in the middle of the thunderstorm, and I am right in the middle of it with them all day every day, and it just doesn't exist. It is crazy.'

Sports.title: Harry Kane insists England team-mates must stop talking about winning major silverware and focus on finally finishing the job after latest World Cup heartbreak
Sports.content:
Harry Kane insists England team-mates must stop talking about winning major silverware and focus on finally finishing the job after latest World Cup heartbreak

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harry Kane has told his England team-mates that the talking about taking the final step on the road to silverware must stop and the time has come to just finish the job.

Thomas Tuchel’s squad still appeared in a state of shock as they left Miami following Saturday’s absurd 6-4 victory over France, which clinched third place at this World Cup.

The win secured a best-ever finish on foreign soil but the scars of their painful late semi-final defeat by Argentina are still evident.

Kane believes the manner of that defeat will linger for weeks and revealed that the group had been theorising over how best to deal with specific scenarios against the best opposition since losing the European Championship final to Spain in 2024.

‘The last 30 minutes of Argentina is not the team we want to be,’ Kane said. ‘We spent a lot of time over the last two years talking about that situation, to attack those moments. The bottom line is we lost anyway.

‘It’s easy to go away and talk about it. We need to get better at actually being in those situations.

Harry Kane has urged his England team-mates to prove they can go on and win a major tournament such as the World Cup

‘We have to learn, improve. The coach will have improved from these learnings. I can talk as much as I want but ultimately it’s about showing it next time we’re in that situation.’

Kane insisted that the Nations League campaign, which pits them against Spain, Croatia and Czechia from September, should better equipe England ahead of the home Euros.

And he has thrown his backing behind Tuchel amid fierce criticism from supporters and pundits for the way in which a one-goal lead against Argentina was managed.

‘It’s the enthusiasm he has, the emotion he brings, the tactical experience he has,’ Kane added. ‘It doesn’t mean you’re going to get it right every time. We want to get it right on the biggest occasions and he expects that from himself as well. He’s a fantastic coach.

‘It was his first major tournament. He’ll learn a lot from the players, the situations, the pressures, the travel. And the players will learn a lot from the other night.’

That the players had been discussing their inability to close out the biggest games before Tuchel’s arrival suggests that internally they will shoulder a portion of the blame.

Tuchel had appeared hurt by widespread condemnation, claiming that his first media conference since Argentina had felt as if England had been knocked out of the group stage without picking up a win.

England suffered a heart-breaking World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina

‘He not only gave the players belief but he gave the country belief that it was our year,’ the England captain said. ‘That is why it hurts even more than other years because everyone believed we were going all the way. Everyone has to process it. He has to process it himself.

‘We’re still in that grieving stage, the emotional stage, and we’ll be in that for the next few weeks.

‘It’s so hard. I think the fans are behind the team and are behind the manager. When something like this happens it’s very emotional – and rightly so. We’ve all been England fans when we wished we’d done this or that and it didn’t quite happen. That will die down naturally.

‘We had a lot of good things, a lot of tough situations we overcame. The group is incredible, the best England group I’ve been a part of in terms of togetherness. The boss was a big part of creating that as well.’

Sports.title: World Cup final halftime show: Who is performing? How long will it take? And why is it so controversial?
Sports.content:
Argentina and Spain are one game away from winning the World Cup but on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, the victorious captain will be forced to wait longer than normal to lift the trophy.

Because, for the first time in history, FIFA has controversially decided to add a halftime show to the biggest game in global soccer.

Billions of fans will tune into Sunday's game as Lionel Messi and Co bid to secure a second successive World Cup triumph. This year, however, Messi will be forced to share the stage with the likes of Madonna, Shakira and Justin Bieber as soccer is given a slice of the Super Bowl treatment.

As well as a halftime show, the World Cup final will also include a closing ceremony that will feature performances and appearances from Post Malone, Tom Cruise, Nicole Scherzinger, influencer IShowSpeed, Oscar winner Jennifer Hudson, Robbie Williams and Italian singer Laura Pausini.

Cruise's specific role is unclear, with FIFA describing it only as a 'special appearance.' But soccer chiefs say the ceremony will pay tribute to all 48 nations from the tournament.

Here, the Daily Mail explains what viewers can expect at halftime.

Justin Bieber is among the music superstars performing during the halftime show on Sunday

Madonna is also among the headliners for the controversial show at MetLife Stadium

Donald Trump is set to attend the final and hand over the trophy with Gianni Infantino

WHO IS PERFORMING?

FIFA enlisted the help of Coldplay frontman Chris Martin to curate the show and back in May it emerged that Madonna, Shakira and K-pop band BTS would perform.

Bieber was recently added to the lineup, while Burna Boy will join Shakira on stage and Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel is also down to perform.

Coldplay will have their moment in the spotlight, too. Martin and Co will perform alongside the PS22 Chorus, an award-winning group of fifth graders from an elementary school in New York. Also among the lineup? Characters from Sesame Street and The Muppets.

'For the first time ever, football, music and social impact will come together as the greatest show on Earth reaches its pinnacle,' FIFA said.

'[The] Halftime Show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, an initiative aiming to raise $100million to expand access to quality education and football opportunities for children worldwide.'

FIFA provided a glimpse of what to expect at last year's Club World Cup Final, when Martin put together another halftime show for Chelsea's win over Paris Saint-Germain.

That took place up in the stands of MetLife Stadium but, 12 months on, Madonna and Co are expected to perform on the field.

Nicole Scherzinger and Tom Cruise will headline the World Cup closing ceremony on Sunday

Twelve months ago, FIFA hosted a halftime show during the Club World Cup final at MetLife

HOW LONG WILL IT LAST?

We shall see. The performance is expected to be wrapped up in 11 minutes but there has yet to be official confirmation about how long the entire circus will take.

Recently, however, reports claimed that soccer chiefs are hoping the show will last around 20 minutes. That is despite the sport's lawmakers stating that halftime should not 'exceed 15 minutes' - unless 'altered... with the referee's permission.'

On Sunday, Messi and Co look set to spend longer than normal in the locker room before returning for the second half.

That has raised concerns over injuries, while questions remain about how the process of erecting and dismantling the stage will affect the field.

Twelve months ago, at the Club World Cup final, halftime lasted nearly 25 minutes - despite the performance taking just 10 minutes.

Unlike last year, however, a stage will need to be put up and taken down on the field of MetLife Stadium. FIFA is also more squeezed for time than the NFL.

At the Super Bowl, halftime is typically extended to around half an hour - from 13 minutes in the regular season - to make room for the musical performance.

BTS, seen here in Mexico City, became the first K-pop group to receive a Grammy nomination

Bad Bunny performed the halftime show at Super Bowl LX between the Patriots and Seahawks

CONMEBOL put on a halftime show for the final of the 2024 Copa America in Miami. That performance, which also featured Shakira, saw Argentina and Colombia players wait 26 minutes before starting the second half.

World Cup games are already longer than normal thanks to FIFA's controversial hydration breaks in each half.

WHAT ARE PEOPLE SAYING ABOUT IT?

Well, it is fair to say that Infantino's decision to introduce a halftime show has been divisive and controversial.

The show's executive producer, Guy Carrington, recently told The Hollywood Reporter: 'We've spent months and months preparing this, developing it and working with all of the artists... it's a carefully-curated performance that’s going to be spectacular.'

The FIFA president, meanwhile, said the artists will 'play a key role in conveying a powerful message of unity and hope to billions of people worldwide.'

Infantino added: 'As the world unites for the most significant football match in history... this groundbreaking spectacle, curated by Chris Martin of Coldplay, will celebrate football, music and our shared values, ensuring a legacy that transcends the final whistle.'

But the verdict of Robert Smith of The Cure was rather less effusive. 'Please just f*** off,' he said about the halftime show.

Sports.title: Chelsea set-piece coach set for move behind the scenes as Xabi Alonso finalises his backroom staff - with ex-Bayer Leverkusen expert poised to join the Spaniard's team
Sports.content:
Bernardo Cueva, who has served as Chelsea’s set-piece specialist for the last two seasons, is changing roles to one more behind the scenes and away from the pitch.

The Mexican, 38, had been in charge of set-plays since 2024 when the Premier League club hired him out of Brentford, reportedly at a compensatory cost worth around £1million.

Now, Daily Mail Sport can reveal Cueva will be taking on a different position under Chelsea’s owners BlueCo in a more technical and advisory capacity.

Among his responsibilities, he will carry a particular focus on set-piece analysis, opposition preparation, and performance insights.

Usually a constant presence on the pitch, Cueva has not been spotted in Chelsea's training sessions since pre-season started under Xabi Alonso on Thursday, July 9.

Chelsea sources have stressed this change should not be seen as a demotion and that Cueva will continue to play a highly crucial role within their football operation.

Bernardo Cueva (right) is set to take up a role in a technical and advisory capacity at Chelsea

Chelsea have not yet announced Alonso’s backroom staff in full, though among his assistants will be Sebastian Parrilla, who arrives with a reputation for improving set-piece output, both defensively and offensively. Under Alonso, Parrilla was credited with boosting Bayer Leverkusen’s numbers when they worked together at the Bundesliga club.

Cueva worked with Chelsea in the 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons under Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior and then alongside interim head coach Calum McFarlane.

He was a regular feature in their dugout and, as well as overseeing set-pieces, usually took on the role of speaking with the fourth official about issues during games.

Chelsea previously identified Cueva as a prime candidate for a role which had been vacant since Anthony Barry exited for Bayern Munich. Cueva, who also holds a UEFA Pro Licence through the Football Association, was regarded as an impressive hire.

Before joining Brentford in 2020, and helping them secure promotion to the Premier League, Cueva was at Chivas in his homeland of Mexico. He has also had a role with Norway men's national team.

Sports.title: Donald Trump makes World Cup final prediction between Argentina and Spain - with the help of son Barron
Sports.content:
Donald Trump has backed Lionel Messi and Argentina to beat Spain in the World Cup final on Sunday.

Speaking to Fox reporter Jenny Taft, Trump said: 'Well, I knew you were going to ask me so I thought about it a lot. I hate to get involved even though poltically it doesn't matter so much.

'I would say that it is hard to bet against Messi. I watched that pass, it was exacrtly perfect (to Lautaro Martinez to score the winning goal against England). But that was perfect, if you had a strike zone it was exactly where it had to be.

'I just think it is very hard to bet against Messi, he is great.'

While discussing the all-time greats of the game Trump, who is attending the game, added that his son Barron, 20, talks a lot to him about soccer and shares a lot of his knowledge about the game with him.

'Messi is great and Ronaldo is great and I hate to say this but I watched Pele when he was with the Cosmos,' Trump said. 'I got to see Pele play. These are great players.

Donald Trump backs Lionel Messi and Argentina to win the World Cup final on Sunday

Trump pictured with son Barron and Zlatan Ibrahimovic at UFC 250 at the White House in June

'There are some others. I get this information from my son, my son Barron is a tremendous soccer fan.

'You really have some other really incredible players playing here but I would say right now, when you look, I have always liked Ronaldo, I've always like Messi.

'I met Messi just recently and I have known Cristiano. They have a pretty good life - much easier than my life, actually!'

Trump recently hosted Messi and Inter Miami at the White House to celebrate their 2025 Major League Soccer title.

Trump added that he is friendly with Argentina's leader, Javier Milei. The same cannot be said of Spain.

Trump launched a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said.

'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Trump hosted Messi and his Inter Miami team at the White House back in March

Spain player Borja Iglesias has been critical of Trump in the past and could meet him on Sunday

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Days later, though, and Trump could find himself center stage for an historic moment for Spain, who are the favorites to win the competition on Sunday.

Trump is expected to hand the trophy over to the winning team after the game alongside the FIFA president, Gianni Infantino.

One of Spain's players, Borja Iglesias, has been a frequent Trump critic but says he will shake his hand if he meets him after the final is over.

'I hope to greet him at a time when we are all very happy, and that it passes very quickly and I can forget about it,' he said.

Sports.title: Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear

A frightening pit lane incident at the Belgian Grand Prix saw Lewis Hamilton accidentally drive into a member of Ferrari's crew, sparking worries of serious damage

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton hit a mechanic (Image: X)

Ferrari have been fined £25,512 after Lewis Hamilton accidentally hit a crew member with his car during a terrifying pit lane accident at the Belgian Grand Prix. Hamilton was shown the green light during a pit stop, signalling that it was safe for him to pull away and get back onto the track at Spa-Francorchamps.

‌



However, the seven-time Formula 1 champion immediately checked in on the mechanic, who was attempting to adjust his front wing very late on, via his team radio. While the member of staff fortunately didn't sustain any serious damage, Hamilton has since admitted that his heart sank as he quickly remembered how Kimi Raikkonen had broke a mechanic's leg in Bahrain in a similar incident.

‌



Speaking after the Belgian GP, Hamilton said: "The green light went, and so I went. You're looking over here [at the light] and not over there [at the mechanic].

‌



Lewis Hamilton punished at Belgian GP after taking out George Russell in first-lap crash READ MORE :

"That's more on the team, ultimately. But when it happened, I noticed him and I stopped and what went through my mind at that moment was when Kimi hit and broke the leg, and my heart really sank for a second."

While the mechanic thankfully was not hurt in the process, Ferrari were unable to escape punishment for the incident, with the FIA announcing a sizeable fine to go Scuderia's way.

A notice read: "The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €30,000 of which €10,000 is suspended for 12 months on condition that the Competitor does not commit a similar infringement in the meantime and on the further condition that within 14 days the Competitor submits a report to the FIA regarding the incident and protocols introduced to mitigate the risk of such an incident occurring in the future."

‌



It added: "The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video evidence. As Car 44 was being released from its pit stop, a mechanic stepped in the path of the front right tyre as the F1 Car moved forward. He fell but was not injured.

"The team explained the incident occurred in the context of a complex and unusual combination of circumstances. HAM had been issued a 5 second time penalty for a driving infringement which had to be served before work could commence on the F1 Car.

‌



"LEC was in his pit box at the point HAM entered the pit lane. HAM told his engineer that he wanted a front wing adjustment but that was not conveyed to the super controller.

"HAM came into his pit box, served the time penalty and at the end of the 5 seconds one member of the team announced 'Go' and then '0.6 degrees,' the former being an instruction to commence the pit stop and the latter being an instruction for a wing adjustment.

"The tyre change was completed, the jack-man dropped the F1 Car and the super controller activated the green light signal for Car 44 to move off. Just as the driver moved off, another mechanic with a front wing tool moved forward into the path of the front right tyre. Before he stepped forward he had his head down looking at the tool and did not see the green light.

‌



View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton finished fourth in Belgium (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

"The team acknowledged that for Car 44 to have been released in these circumstances was unsafe and attributed the error to an inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic’s failure to notice the green light.

"The team committed to undertaking a review of their pit stop procedures to ensure an incident such as this will not be repeated. The Stewards determined that the driver was in no respect at fault."

Sports.title: Ryan Fox wins The Open with final birdie as Tommy Fleetwood misses out
Sports.content:
Ryan Fox wins The Open with final birdie as Tommy Fleetwood misses out

Brit Tommy Fleetwood missed out on becoming Open champion in the most heartbreaking way after Ryan Fox birdied the 18th to clinch victory

View 2 Images Ryan Fox celebrates after winning The Open with a birdie on the 18th

New Zealander Ryan Fox won The Open with a brilliant birdie on the 18th and final hole to beat Cameron Young by a stroke.

‌



For a few glorious hours it felt like Tommy Fleetwood's fairytale was going to come true before Fox birdied four of the last six holes to win the Claret Jug.

‌



That he would become Open champion. On the course he grew up dreaming of gracing on the greatest stage. With his family, friends and a legion of supporters cheering him to the rafters.

‌



But then his moment in the sun turned to darkness, in the space of 60 maddening minutes which left the hometown hero heartbroken once again.

Scottie Scheffler rages at The Open as tempers flare in dramatic scenes READ MORE :

As Fleetwood stood at the top of the hill on the ninth hole preparing to take aim at the pin with his approach, he was one shot off the lead. Two birdies in four holes had taken him to -8 and just two rivals were above him on the leaderboard.

Then all hell broke loose as the man with one of the finest temperaments in golf suffered a meltdown in the blazing heat.

‌



His approach shot almost pitched in the hole, but took a firm bounce before rolling off the back of the green. He failed to get up and down and finished with a bogey, instead of what should have been a birdie.

On the next hole, his tee shot ended in rough, from where he left himself a 9ft putt for par which he failed to make.

View 2 Images It wasn't to be for Tommy Fleetwood at The Open (Image: Oisin Keniry/R&A)

‌



The galleries were groaning, but worse was to come on the next hole, when Fleetwood got out of position again to leave another long putt for par. And another one he couldn't hole.

Fleetwood had made it a hat-trick of bogeys at the worst possible time, and the Open bubble he'd spent all week floating around in had been well and truly burst.

He found himself five shots adrift of leader Si Woo Kim with just seven holes remaining - and knew deep down his chances of landing his first Major title at the place he loves the most had gone.

‌



The supporters kept cheering him on, and Fleetwood gave them back two birdies, to finish with a round of 68, two shots behind clubhouse leader Cam Young.

An emotional Fleetwood thumped his heart in appreciation of the thunderous support he's had, in a week of what might have beens. Four rounds in the 60s hadn't been enough.

He said: "I'm going to look at me finishing two, three shots off and think what could I have done better.

‌



"That aside, walking up the 18th hole, I've dreamt of that as a kid and all my life. That ovation surpasses anything I can imagine.

"I haven't won The Open, I'd have loved to and I'll keep chasing but that was incredibly special.

"I was playing great and felt really good. It was just the terrible mistake on the ninth fairway. I hit it over the back and that's one place you can't hit it.

Article continues below

"I felt fine. I still actually felt on 12 there was a chance. I just couldn't quite do it. "When I look back, there will be things I'll learn from."

Sports.title: Arsenal to receive millions in FIFA compensation after disastrous World Cup blow
Sports.content:
Arsenal to receive millions in FIFA compensation after disastrous World Cup blow

Arsenal will be handed millions of pounds in compensation as a result of one of their key players suffering a serious injury at the 2026 World Cup

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta will be without William Saliba for the start of the new season after an injury to the defender (Image: ANTONIN THUILLIER, AFP via Getty Images)

Arsenal are expected to receive over £4million as a result of William Saliba's back injury at the 2026 World Cup. The 24-year-old has been battling through the pain barrier since March, but broke down during France's 2-0 semi-final loss to Spain on Tuesday.

‌



The centre-half was spotted limping off the pitch just 30 minutes into the action, substituted for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix. It has now emerged that Saliba could be sidelined for up to five months.

‌



He could also require surgery on his back. It mirrors a similar injury he picked up toward the back end of 2022/23.

‌



Bukayo Saka speechless before walking away from BBC interview over England World Cup remark READ MORE :

France boss Didier Deschamps confirmed after the match that Saliba's pain had become "unbearable" during the Spain fixture and the severity of the problem became apparent on the pitch. Then ahead of the World Cup third-place play-off against England, Deschamps offered a further update on Saliba's situation, stating.

He said: "William Saliba got injured and it's problematic. He went through some examinations.

"The injury did not worsen. He faced that injury since March. He had some pain and unfortunately the pain was not bearable."

‌



Arsenal are yet to give any indication of a recovery timeframe, though it's understood Saliba faces could be unavailable until mid-November at the earliest. While the Frenchman's absence will represent a significant setback for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta, the club are set to receive a substantial sum in compensation from FIFA given the back injury was aggravated during the World Cup.

View 2 Images William Saliba's injury worsened during France's clash with Spain at the World Cup (Image: Shaun Botterill, Getty Images)

Since 2012, FIFA's Club Protection Programme has provided cover for the wages of players who sustain injuries while on international duty. There are, however, certain conditions that must be satisfied beforehand.

‌



One stipulates that the player must remain sidelined for a minimum period of 28 consecutive days and that the injury must have been sustained during an 'accident.' Given that Saliba is anticipated to be absent for between four and five months, and that the injury deteriorated while he was competing at the World Cup, Arsenal look well placed to lodge a compensation claim with FIFA for the duration of Saliba's recovery.

It means Arsenal could pocket at least £4m from FIFA to cover Saliba, who is reported to be earning around £250,000 per week at the Emirates Stadium following the signing of a lucrative new deal last September.

Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa has been mooted as a summer target after turning heads for the Three Lions at the World Cup. Villa, however, are determined to hold on to the 28-year-old, who is valued at upward of £50m.

Whether Arsenal will opt for a short-term stand-in for Saliba, or pursue someone of Konsa's calibre who can deputise for the former Marseille defender or even slot in at right-back, remains to be seen.

Sports.title: World Cup final chaos as furious fans forced to wait HOURS to enter stadium
Sports.content:
World Cup final chaos as furious fans forced to wait HOURS to enter stadium

The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina is due to take place on Sunday evening but supporters and members of the media were met with mayhem outside of the MetLife Stadium

View 2 Images Fans have ran into serious issues getting into MetLife Stadium (Image: Getty Images)

The 2026 World Cup final has already been blighted by chaos before the game, with supporters struggling to enter MetLife Stadium.

‌



The arena - which is located a way away from Manhattan - has been criticised throughout the tournament for its unsuitability for the final. And FIFA’s decision to hand the game to the stadium now looks even more baffling given the troubles that both fans and members of the media have faced in attempting to enter.

‌



Even five hours before kick-off, some members of security suggested that FIFA’s ticketing system was throwing out glitches, making it tricky to allow people entry.

‌



That forced organisers to encourage fans, workers and members of the media to get to the stadium as early as possible. But that only worsened the issue, with long queues forming around the stadium, with many of those taking hours to clear. Those not at the stadium early were also met with long delays at Penn Station, ahead of even travelling to the stadium itself.

The presence of US president Donald Trump also appeared to make the situation even worse. Despite a heightened security presence due to his attendance, there was a lack of real organisation, with many in attendance given wrong instructions on where to enter.

Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy READ MORE :

It wasn’t just fans who bore the brunt of the problems. Accredited media also found it frustrating to gain admission due to Trump’s attendance.

‌



Extra Secret Service security checks were completed on their equipment, with many members of the press also facing delays of hours to get in.

Leading up to the final, there have also been concerns about the weather. New York was hit with heavy thunderstorms on the eve of the game, which saw Spain cancel their pre-match training session. Flash flooding also hit the region.

And with the stadium having no roof, the final itself would also face delays due to lightning protocols, albeit the weather cleared on Sunday. There have also been worries about the air quality ahead of the game, with a brutal smog having surrounded both New York and New Jersey due to wildfires in Canada.

‌



View 2 Images The World Cup final is set to take place at the MetLife Stadium (Image: Getty Images)

Away from the issues getting into the stadium, fans have also let their frustrations be known at MetLife being selected for the final. There is very little around the stadium - allowing for the American Dream Mall a 20 minute walk away - while prices for food and drinks inside are also extortionate, with ticket prices through the roof.

The stadium’s pitch has also been criticised throughout the tournament. Brazil star Vinicius Jr was among those to take aim at the playing service last month.

Article continues below

He said: "That makes things difficult because we want to play. We want to move the ball from one side to the other and this disrupts our game. But we have to adapt because I believe it will be like this all tournament."

Sports.title: Arsenal eye shock transfer for England World Cup hero after Morgan Rogers snub
Sports.content:
Arsenal eye shock transfer for England World Cup hero after Morgan Rogers snub

Arsenal look set to miss out on a deal for Morgan Rogers with Chelsea swooping in but they could still sign a key member of England's World Cup squad in the coming weeks

View 2 Images Arsenal could swoop for free agent John Stones (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

John Stones has emerged as a surprise target for Arsenal following the World Cup, with the veteran defender available on a free transfer.

‌



Stones brought the curtain down on a decade of domestic dominance with Manchester City at the end of the Premier League season before heading to the World Cup with England, playing a key role in the side's run to the semi-finals of the tournament.

‌



With Stones now deciding his next move, the 32-year-old's availability and extensive top-flight pedigree makes him an attractive proposition for elite clubs — and Arsenal look to be in need of defensive reinforcements amid concerns over William Saliba.

‌



The Arsenal star played through a back injury at the World Cup before breaking down in France's semi-final defeat to Spain, and there are now fears that Saliba could be sidelined for up to five months.

Chelsea strike mega £117m Morgan Rogers transfer with Arsenal set to miss out on star READ MORE :

With Stones available, he is viewed as a cost-effective option to help Arsenal cope in Saliba's absence according to The Sun, who claim the newly minted Premier League champions could soon swoop for a player who has battled against them in title races of years past.

Mikel Arteta knows Stones well from his stint working as an assistant coach for Manchester City and the opportunity to continue playing in the Premier League with a club primed to compete for major honours would likely appeal to the player.

‌



Stones, who is understood to have numerous options on the table including from suitors abroad, will consider his next move now that England's involvement with the World Cup is over.

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers is set to join Chelsea rather than Arsenal (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal's interest in Stones comes following the bombshell news that one of their primary summer transfer targets, Morgan Rogers, is on the cusp of a blockbuster move to Chelsea.

‌



The 23-year-old has been courted by both clubs for months with Arsenal keen to level up the left-hand side of their attack, an area Rogers is adept at operating in.

And while Arsenal have long been considered the red-hot favourites to land the former Middlesbrough star, it emerged on Saturday night that Chelsea have agreed a £117million for the Aston Villa attacker, with Stamford Bridge emerging as Rogers' preferred destination despite Arsenal's interest.

Sports.title: Conor McGregor announces return date as full extent of injury is revealed
Sports.content:
Conor McGregor announces return date as full extent of injury is revealed

Conor McGregor's comeback fight against Max Holloway lasted just 69 seconds after the Irishman injured his knee throwing the first kick of the fight

View Image Conor McGregor after injuring himself

Conor McGregor is targeting a return next summer after revealing he tore his ACL against Max Holloway.

‌



McGregor returned to the cage last weekend following a five year absence but hurt his knee throwing the first kick of the fight. The bout was stopped after just 69 seconds, handing McGregor a TKO loss and another spell on the sidelines. The Irishman has now revealed he tore his ACL and damaged his meniscus.

‌



"It was the ACL and meniscus," he wrote on social media. "It is the same injury as the first Holloway fight, only this time the opposite leg. Quite shocking. I returned to competition within nine months to fight Diego Brandao back then.

‌



Conor McGregor demands result of Max Holloway fight is changed READ MORE :

Conor McGregor issues three-word update on career after injury nightmare READ MORE :

"With today’s regenerative medicine advancements and improved training methods it is well within my realm to return by next summer. I am walking without a crutch. I did leg extension machine work the other day to no issue. So I can walk without aid, and activate my quad under resistance. All very positive.

"I am at maximum discipline and have maintained it fully since the bout. I wonder was I saved from something worse here. I believe so. I would have attended the after party as “the man” and who knows then. I believe I was saved."

‌



McGregor had previously announced his determination to return to the cage for the final fight on his UFC contract. "Surgery. Prehab. Return to martial arts practice. Go again. Final fight of the contract. Please God!" he said.

My faith is unconditional and I am thankful I get to prove it! My lifestyle changes are permanent and not just until. I am thankful I get to prove it. I am in Sin City and remain completely devoid of all sin.

"I will not open that door nor crack its seal! I am already back to collecting wins! In Jesus name I pray! Church was intense today, my heart is heavy but through Christ my mind is STRONG! I am so grateful to see my family fall more in love with God each day!

Article continues below

"I am a child of God. I am a friend of God. God makes a way for me where there seems to be no way. I am not a victim of my circumstances, I overcome them. God is at work in me to will and to work his good pleasure! My youth is being renewed like the eagles! In Jesus I am thoroughly loved, cherished, adored. I walk in divine health. I live under supernatural protection.

"All things work out for my good! All things are possible for me because I am a believer! I trust in You Lord! Show me Your way. Thank You God."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
