World.title: PM Al Zaidi carries Trump message to Iran; Tehran declines Supreme Leader meeting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Well-informed sources have disclosed to the Kuwaiti newspaper Al-Jarida, that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi is carrying a verbal message from U.S. President Donald Trump addressed to the Iranian leadership. This message, which al-Zaidi received during his recent official visit to Washington, comes as the U.S.–Iran confrontation edges closer to a broader war amid ongoing regional military escalation.

The sources from the Iranian Supreme National Security Council explained that the Iraqi Prime Minister’s stopover in the Qatari capital of Doha on Sunday was specifically aimed at coordinating the core substance of this message with the Qatari side. Baghdad is seeking to evaluate the possibility of transforming this verbal message into a tangible Iraqi initiative that works in tandem with current mediation tracks led by Qatar and Pakistan to de-escalate regional tensions.

Diplomatic Tracks and the Backstage of the Upcoming Tehran Visit

Timeline of the Visit: Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s state visit to Tehran is officially scheduled for next Thursday, though Baghdad has expressed full readiness to move the date forward if regional developments demand it.

Iraqi Request for a Supreme Leader Meeting: The Iraqi delegation expressed a strong desire to leverage the special bilateral relationship between the two neighbors to make al-Zaidi the first foreign official to meet with Iran’s new Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei.

Iranian Refusal Based on Security Protocol: The Iranian source completely ruled out the possibility of such a meeting, confirming that the Iraqi delegation was officially notified of the decision. The refusal was attributed to strict Iranian security anxieties regarding the potential exposure of the new Supreme Leader’s secure location, given that he has remained completely out of public sight since the outbreak of the war on Iran last February. Tehran noted that the standard official protocols and security footprint required for hosting a foreign prime minister would pose an unacceptable security risk.

Alternative Intelligence Claims: In contrast to Tehran’s official justification, regional and Hebrew media outlets quoted an Israeli security source claiming that Mojtaba Khamenei is not actually inside Iranian territory. The intelligence source alleged that the strategic messages attributed to the Supreme Leader are entirely drafted by Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Commander Ahmed Vahidi.

On the domestic front in Tehran, former Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is spearheading a political narrative that encourages the Iranian leadership to maintain its current stance and resist external pressures until the conclusion of the American elections. Zarif based his strategic view on recent communications he allegedly received from several U.S. Democratic politicians. According to his account, these American figures suggested that a potential electoral setback for Trump in November could push Congress to take decisive legislative action to halt the war.

Conversely, the governing domestic alliance uniting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf remains firmly committed to pursuing direct diplomatic understandings with Washington to end the crisis. The position of this moderate faction was recently reinforced following a directive issued by the Supreme Leader, which ordered an immediate halt to internal political public criticism of state officials.

This directive was translated into immediate action on the ground, as strict orders were handed down to hardline, ultra-conservative media outlets to completely cease their coordinated media campaigns against Pezeshkian and Qalibaf. The state warned that any violation of this freeze would result in severe regulatory and legal penalties, up to and including the permanent revocation of corporate media broadcasting licenses.

World.title: Iraq’s Integrity Commission arrests electricity official over 4.5B IQD cable theft
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Federal Integrity Commission announced on Sunday, July 19, 2026, the arrest of a senior official within the Baghdad Electricity Distribution Company for the embezzlement and illicit seizure of state-owned electrical infrastructure materials valued at nearly 4.5 billion Iraqi Dinars (IQD).

According to an official statement released by the commission, a specialized investigative and auditing task force was deployed directly to the Ministry of Electricity to audit regional inventory systems.

The investigation revealed that the head of the warehouses for the Rusafa distribution branch had illegally seized high-voltage electrical cables totaling 4,406,000,000 IQD in value. The commission noted that the primary suspect executed the embezzlement scheme in direct cooperation with two civilian vehicle owners who assisted in transporting the stolen state property out of the facility.

The arrest was carried out under a formal judicial warrant issued by the Judge of the Central Anti-Corruption Criminal Court, in accordance with the statutory provisions of Article 315 of the Iraqi Penal Code, which strictly penalizes the embezzlement of public funds by state employees.

A formal seizure record was legally documented, and the primary suspect was presented before the competent investigative judge, who subsequently ordered him to be remanded in custody pending further judicial proceedings.

Investigation Brief: Rusafa Grid Embezzlement Case

World.title: Influencer Andrew Tate and brother arrested in Miami
World.content:
Washington – Radical social media influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were on Sunday in custody in the US, officials said, as Britain seeks their extradition to face new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault.

Karena Thomas, assistant chief constable of the UK’s Bedfordshire Police, said the pair had been detained \”pending ongoing legal proceedings.\”

The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests.

US news outlet TMZ posted video of law enforcement officers placing the self-professed misogynist and his younger sibling in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles in Miami on Saturday.

Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on X showed.

UK prosecutors, who are now due to seek the brothers’ extradition, said the arrests came after they brought forward 38 further charges against the pair.

The Tate brothers now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan, British authorities said on Sunday.

\”We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,\” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service’s (CPS) Special Crime Division, said in a statement.

\”The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US,\” he said, adding that the latest charges stem from receipt of new evidence from Bedfordshire Police that brings the total number of alleged victims in the Tates case to seven.

Earlier this year, police in Hertfordshire, north of London, said they were reopening a probe into rape and sexual assault allegations made by women against Andrew Tate between 2014 and 2015.

They also face separate rape and human trafficking allegations brought by different women and investigated by Bedfordshire Police, which covers their hometown of Luton, also north of London.

\”There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,\” Bedfordshire Police’s Thomas added.

– ‘Face justice’ –

The Tate brothers are also accused of tax evasion and money laundering in the UK.

Their attorney, Joseph McBride, said in a press release that the brothers \”are innocent.\”

\”We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,\” McBride said.

The Tates are dual British-US citizens who have been avid supporters of US President Donald Trump.

Lawyer Matt Jury, of McCue Jury & Partners who represent four alleged British victims of Andrew Tate, said Tate was \”now facing the real prospect of extradition to the UK after years of public campaigning by the four British women I represent.

\”They have spent years fighting for action to be taken, and I now urge the authorities to ensure this case proceeds as quickly as possible.

\”Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of some of the most serious offences, including multiple counts of rape and human trafficking. It is time they face justice,\” he was quoted by the PA news agency as saying.

In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation against them. The status of that investigation is unclear.

Andrew Tate is one of the most prominent proponents of the so-called \”manosphere\” network of communities, many of them online, that focus on traditional masculinity, anti-feminism, and self-improvement.

He promotes his divisive views, often incorporating alpha-male and aggressively misogynistic themes, to millions on social media including 10.8 million followers on X.

In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the Tates face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering.

World.title: Iraqi dinar declines against US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar declined on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,520 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,526 Iraqi dinars on Sunday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,523 and 1,522.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Calm Antonelli takes sixth win of the season with victory at Belgian GP
World.content:
Spa-Francorchamps – Italian teenager Kimi Antonelli ended a three-race winless streak on Sunday to extend his lead in the Formula One drivers’ championship with a solid fighting victory for Mercedes in the Belgian Grand Prix.

The 19-year-old Mercedes driver came home 1.9 seconds ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc with four-time champion Max Verstappen finishing third for Red Bull.

Antonelli’s teammate George Russell, who began the race in second place in the championship, just 25 points behind the Italian, crashed out of the race on the opening lap after tangling with Hamilton.

Hamilton was fourth for Ferrari after an incident-filled race in which he almost hit a mechanic during a pit-stop. The incident was referred to the stewards leaving the seven-time world champion with the possibility of a further penalty.

Isack Hadjar, who began at the back of the grid, did superbly to work his Red Bull up to sixth, just holding off reigning world champion Lando Norris, who started 13th, in the second McLaren.

Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi), Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) and Franco Colapinto (Alpine) rounded out the top 10.

It was Antonelli’s sixth win of the season and came from his sixth pole of the year, the first driver to win from pole in Belgium since 2021.

It lifts him to 204 points in the championship, 45 clear of Hamilton with Russell third on 154.

\”It feels very nice to be back on the top step,\” said Antonelli.

\”We just have to keep performing, keep bringing the results and then we will see what will happen at the end of the year.\”

The race started in cool conditions under a grey sky with rain in the air as Antonelli made a good start to lead up to La Source, but he had no answer when Verstappen deployed his power pack to pass him through Eau Rouge.

The Dutchman was then immediately vulnerable to a counter-attack and both the Italian and Leclerc drafted past him into Les Combes where behind them Hamilton clashed with Russell.

– ‘Racing incident’ –

The four-time champion continued in fifth, but Russell bounced off into retirement as a Safety Car (SC) was deployed.

Hamilton reported that he “had no front end” control as a result of a car ahead moving across him and the incident was investigated by the stewards who gave Hamilton a five-second penalty.

A downcast Russell, whose title bid had taken a heavy blow, said: “It was a racing incident, but it shouldn’t have happened if I’d had the speed down the straight.”

Racing resumed on lap five with Piastri fighting and resisting Hamilton before Verstappen swept past Leclerc for second. Piastri then chased Leclerc and they touched at Les Combes, where the Monegasque defended and the Australian lost a piece of front wing end plate.

The stewards investigated again, but took ‘no further action’ while Hamilton advanced and passed Piastri for fourth on lap nine as the race settled after a frantic start with Antonelli two seconds clear of Verstappen at the front ahead of both Ferraris.

Further Virtual Safety Cars (VSC) intervened and on lap 20, Ferrari went for a ‘double-stack’. Leclerc went through cleanly but Hamilton, who had to serve his five-second penalty, made a messy exit touching a mechanic on exit.

The mechanic was reported to be fine but the stewards decided to investigate again for an unsafe release.

That left Norris, who had started 13th with a 10-place grid penalty, for taking a new battery, leading ahead of Leclerc, Antonelli and Verstappen until the Ferrari cruised by to take command on lap 23.

Antonelli swept past Norris three laps later and surged after Leclerc while Hamilton, who had requested a wing adjustment in vain during his pit-stop, fell back to sixth.

Norris finally pitted to swap his old hards for mediums on lap 31, rejoining eighth after a slow stop due to a sticky left rear, Hadjar rising to sixth behind Hamilton.

Leclerc led until lap 34 when, as he feared, Antonelli’s superior power carried him through at Les Combes.

But he hung on tight, within a second of the silver arrow, while Hamilton passed Piastri for fourth with five laps to go

World.title: Iraq proposes Energy City project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced the Energy City project on Thursday as part of a government plan to enhance energy infrastructure and strengthen partnerships with major international firms.

Al-Zaidi announced the Energy City initiative during an official visit to the United States, which included discussions with US officials and executives from American energy businesses.

This visit is part of Baghdad’s efforts to attract new investments that support plans to increase oil production, develop the gas sector, and enhance electricity generation capacity.

The Iraqi government is depending on the new project to turn the al-Faw Peninsula into an integrated center for the oil, gas, and electricity industries, taking advantage of its strategic location on the Arabian Gulf and proximity to oil export routes and the Development Road project.

The development takes place as Iraq continues to implement plans to eliminate gas flaring, expand domestic gas output, and reduce dependency on imported fuel for power plants, all while increasing refining capacity.

Al-Zaidi’s announcement took place during his participation in the Iraqi-American Chamber of Commerce’s Joint Economic Dialogue Forum in Houston, Texas, to finalize over $60 billion in deals with US energy companies.

The prime minister explained that the project includes integrated complexes for crude oil refining, gas production, processing units, and power plants, as well as connections to strategic oil pipelines and the Development Road, strengthening Iraq’s position as a regional energy and logistics hub.

Al-Zaidi highlighted that Iraq is seeking strategic partners, rather than just contractors, who can assist with technology transfer and contribute to the creation of new job opportunities.

Chairman of the Bilateral Chamber of Commerce David Phillips confirmed the Texas business community’s and large American firms’ willingness to invest in Iraq, notably in oil, gas, and energy projects.

World.title: US-Iran strikes: latest developments
World.content:
Dubai – US and Iranian strikes extended into Sunday, with Washington saying it was punishing Tehran for the deaths of two US servicemen in Jordan and Gulf states announcing responses to Iranian attacks.

Here are the latest developments:

Missile reported intercepted

Israeli and Jordanian forces intercepted an Iranian missile aimed at the Jordanian city of Aqaba on Sunday, the Israeli military told AFP.

When asked by AFP about reports of explosions near the Israeli city of Eilat, a military spokeswoman said both Israeli and Jordanian forces had intercepted a projectile.

The Jordanian military said it had downed \”three Iranian missiles that targeted the kingdom’s territory\”, without specifying where.

Sirens sounded in the Jordanian capital Amman on Sunday, an AFP correspondent said,

Kuwait, Bahrain attacked

Kuwait said Iran hit a power and water plant on Sunday causing a fire, while Bahrain also accused Tehran of targeting civilian infrastructure.

It was the third attack in as many days on a power and water facility in Kuwait, according to authorities, who als said an oil facility had been hit on Saturday.

Earlier on Sunday, Iran’s army said it had targeted two US bases in Kuwait with drones in response to American attacks on Iranian territory.

Iranian nuclear plant attacked

Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation said the United States attacked an under-construction nuclear power plant in Darkhovin, in the country’s southwest.

Iran says ships ‘stopped’

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said four ships attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz without their permission and two \”had an accident and were stopped in place\”.

The other two abandoned their journey, they said.

US strikes on Iran

The United States conducted its eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iran.

Its CENTCOM military command said they were partly to \”punish\” Iran for an attack on Friday on a base in Jordan which killed two US soldiers and left another missing in action.

The strikes were also to \”degrade Iran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz\”, CENTCOM said.

Iranian news agencies Fars and Tasnim reported US attacks on Sirik, a port located on the Strait of Hormuz in southern Iran.

World.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with ballistic missiles in escalating air war
World.content:
Kyiv – Russia fired two dozen ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 16, in an ever-escalating air war that is taking an increasing civilian toll on both sides.

The latest bombardment highlights a dual challenge for Ukraine in its fifth year of war. It is facing intensifying Russian missile attacks alongside rare domestic political instability triggered by a sudden wartime shakeup of its defence leadership.

In the morning, AFP journalists in Kyiv saw charred apartment blocks with windows blown out and mangled, overturned cars.

\”The missiles just kept coming one after another, the explosions were powerful, it was horrible,\” 47-year-old Kyiv resident Ganna Zagorodnia told AFP.

\”I thought that life was just about to end.\”

In a statement on social media, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said that \”overnight, Russia carried out one of its largest ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv,\” launching more than 40 missiles, 25 of them ballistic.

Zelensky added that one person was killed and 16 others wounded in the attack, which police said targeted six districts.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, afternoon Russian strikes killed four and wounded 20 at a post warehouse in Kharkiv, the country’s eastern second-biggest city, said local military governor Oleg Syniegubov.

In the Black Sea city of Odesa, a teenager was killed and 12 were wounded, including a two-year-old child, after a Russian attack on an amusement park, said governor Oleg Kiper.

Russia, which denies targeting civilians, said it struck military facilities and logistics hubs in Kyiv and port infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army in Odesa.

– Generals back commander –

Even as the war raged, thousands have been gathering in big cities across Ukraine for three consecutive days to protest at the removal of popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Demonstrators also called for the resignation of Ukraine’s chief commander Oleksandr Syrsky, who reportedly had demanded Fedorov’s dismissal after the two clashed over how to counter the Russian invasion.

Following the protests, two experienced top Ukrainian generals — the navy and the air assault force chiefs — backed Syrsky in rare political statements, calling for unity and saying divisions are playing into the enemy’s hands.

\”It is particularly painful to hear peremptory judgments from people who have never issued combat orders, never taken responsibility for the lives and health of the personnel,\” said air assault force commander Oleg Apostol, referring to Fedorov’s critisism of Syrsky.

Echoing that, navy commander Oleksiy Neizhpapa said: \”doubts about the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) during wartime are unacceptable. The AFU is perhaps the only institution that stands firmly on its feet, no matter what.\”

Fedorov, 35, who never served in the army, accused the 60-year-old, Russian-born general Syrsky of dividing the country.

He criticised slow bureaucracy and a lack of flexibility, questioning whether Ukraine could defeat Russia with Syrsky in charge of the army.

– Air defence hunger –

Since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran, Ukraine has suffered from a shortage of air defence projectiles for its US-designed Patriot systems, which are essential for fending off ballistic rounds.

Exploiting the shortage, Russia has intensified its air raids on Kyiv in recent weeks, launching barrages of balistic missiles — fast, hard to intercept weapons — roughly once a week.

\”Protection against ballistic missiles is our constant and top priority right now. Interceptors are needed every day,\” Zelensky said.

Overnight on Sunday, out of 25 Russian ballistic missiles, 17 were intercepted, the air force said — a rate suggesting Ukraine’s air defence situation might be improving.

On the Russian side, a Ukrainian strike killed one person in the Kursk region, near the Ukrainian border, regional governor Alexander Khinshtein said on Telegram.

Another drone salvo hit the Caspian Pipeline Consortium’s terminal near the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk — a key export route for Kazakh oil, partly owned by Chevron and Shell.

Kyiv has in recent months intensified its strikes on Russian territory, disrupting the lives of ordinary Russians — strikes it calls retribution for more than four years of bombardments against its territory.

World.title: Even as fertility rates drop, young still aspire to partnership, parenthood, shows UN report
World.content: NEW DELHI: A first-of-its-kind survey of young adults (aged 18-39) across 73 countries, including India, by United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) shows that even as much of the worldâs marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels, young people are not turning away from relationships or family life. Marriage, it says, remains âa common ideal relationshipâ arrangement among surveyed young adults.The report highlights that across countries â with very different demographic realities â many continue to aspire to partnership and parenthood, but say their decisions are increasingly shaped by financial security, stable employment, housing, gender equality and confidence in the future.UNFPAâs âLives, Choices and Futures â Demographic Futures Surveyâ 2026â gathered perspectives of more than 1,08,000 internet connected young adults, including 1,722 respondents in India.More than two thirds of respondents selected an ideal relationship and living arrangement that includes marriage â 36% before living together and 34% after a period of cohabitation. The survey says 16% reported remaining single as their preferred living arrangement.Its findings gain significance, as across much of the world partnership formation is occurring later, marriage rates have declined and fertility has fallen to historically low levels.âTwo thirds of the worldâs population now lives in a country or area where the total fertility rate is below 2.1 children per woman â the level commonly associated with the population size remaining stable over time,â the survey says.Among respondents aged 25â39, who ideally wish to marry or live with a partner, a quarter are currently single and not dating. The proportion is higher among male respondents (30% than among female respondents (19%).Financial security is the highest-rated consideration for partnership formation, cited as important by 81% of respondents. It turns out that economic and housing constraints constitute the most commonly reported category of barrier to partnership, rated important by 57%.The survey finds that among respondents â currently seeking a partner â personal networks, school or work environments, and online platforms are the most commonly reported channels for meeting potential partners, each reported by approximately one third of respondents. Overall the survey says more than 40% of respondents report spending over two hours a day on social media or the Internet for entertainment, making it the most time-intensive form of online activity examined.In India, while more than eight in 10 respondents (83%) said they feel positive or very positive about the future, nearly half of those surveyed (47%) said they are very worried about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality.While across most regional groupings of countries, two children is the most commonly reported ideal family size, the mean number of children reported by respondents aged 35â39 is lower than the mean ideal number of children reported by respondents aged 18â39.For instance, in the case of India, women aged 18-39 reported an ideal family size of 2.1 children, compared with an average of one child among women aged 35-39. Men reported an ideal family size of 2.2 children, compared with an average of 1.1 children among men aged 35-39.Parenthood is part of the future plans of most surveyed in India. Among respondents aged 35-39 in India who do not currently have children, nearly 85% said they would ideally like to become parents.

World.title: Less than half of 483 Lok Sabha MPs attended 90-100% of sittings in Parliament’s budget session, shows analysis
World.content:
NEW DELHI: As parties gear-up for taking up a wide range of issues during Parliamentâs monsoon session â expected to be fiery in light of Ram temple and NEET-UG paper leak issues â the presence of MPs in both Houses is most crucial.

An analysis of attendance record of the previous budget session, which ended in April, by NGO Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative shows that it is the smaller parties â with a handful of MPs â that have the highest average attendance record figures.

Overall in Lok Sabha, as many as 101 MPs had signed the attendance register for all 31 sittings of the budget session â less than a quarter, or just about 21% of the 483 MPs whose attendance record was publicly available.

In terms of average attendance record of parties in LS, RLP â that has one MP (Hanuman Beniwal from Nagaur â and RLD â that has two MPs (Chandan Chauhan from Bijnor and Rajkumar Sangwan from Baghpat â registered 100% attendance record for all 31 sittings. CPI(ML-L) stood second â with two of its MPs attending 30 out of the 31 sittings â as did Zoram Peopleâs Movement with its lone MPs. Samajwadi Party took third position â with 37 of its MPs averaging attendance of 28.43 days.





Overall less than one half (45.7%) of the 483 LS members had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register. The report examines the attendance record as available on the website of both Houses for the budget session to spot political party-wise trends and patterns.

The single-largest party in LS, BJP (with details of 191 members available) averaged only 26.46 sittings per MP. Congress â single-largest party in opposition â averaged only 23.13 sittings (with details of 97 MPs available).

Among regional political parties with more than 20 MPs during the budget session, TMC averaged only 15 sittings and DMK with 22 MPs even lesser with 14.64 sittings.

In Rajya Sabha, 119 MPs â less than 46.6% of 255 MPs had attended between 90-100% of the sittings or at least signed the attendance register for those many days.

The top 10 political parties clocking the highest percentage of attendance are regional parties. DMDK with its lone MP (LK Sudhish) is the only one who recorded 100% attendance, followed by J&K-NC with three MPs clocking an average of 94.62%. MPs from JDS, MNF, BJD, SP, NPP and SS all recorded an average of more than 90% attendance.

Despite being the largest party in the House, BJP recorded an average attendance of only 84.39% followed by Congress recording 80.66%, the report stated.

World.title: 'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Indian Embassy in Iran on Sunday issued a revised travel advisory, urging Indian nationals to postpone all travel to the country.

It also advised Indians already in Tehran to consider temporarily leaving the country using available commercial flights, as the security situation continues to deteriorate amid the escalating conflict in the Middle East.

The advisory comes as military hostilities between the United States and Iran have intensified, with fresh strikes, retaliatory attacks and growing concerns over the security situation across the region.

In its advisory, the embassy said, "The recent days have seen an increase in levels of instability and conflict in Iran."

It advised Indian nationals planning to visit Iran 'for any purpose' to postpone their travel until the security environment improves.

The embassy also urged Indians already in Iran to 'consider temporarily exiting Iran, using available flight options.'

For those choosing to remain in the country, the mission advised exercising the highest level of caution, closely monitoring local developments and avoiding areas witnessing increased military activity, particularly along Iran's southern coast.

"Indian nationals who choose to remain in Iran should exercise the highest possible level of caution.





They should carefully monitor the news to maintain full situational awareness, and should avoid locations seeing higher levels of military activity such as those along the southern coast of the country. Instructions issued by local authorities should be complied with carefully," the advisory read.

The embassy also asked all Indian nationals in Iran who have not yet registered with the mission to do so immediately and regularly follow its official website and social media channels for further updates.

The advisory was issued as the conflict between the United States and Iran escalated further on Sunday.

According to Iranian authorities, the United States carried out fresh strikes on the under-construction Darkhovin nuclear power plant and other military targets, while the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it targeted Iranian coastal surveillance systems, air defence networks, maritime assets and missile and drone facilities.

Iran, meanwhile, announced retaliatory drone attacks against two US military installations in Kuwait and claimed to have intercepted a US MQ-9 drone over Ahvaz. It also warned that the Strait of Hormuz remained under the control of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), amid heightened tensions over maritime security.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it was investigating reports of the attack on the Darkhovin nuclear facility and added that the site contained no nuclear material during its last inspection. The UN nuclear watchdog said the reported strike was not believed to pose any radiological risk but reiterated its call for military restraint around nuclear-related sites.

The latest escalation has raised fresh international concern over the widening conflict in the Middle East as the war completes nearly five months.

World.title: 'Stay here for the night': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke calls for night-long vigil ahead of 'Chalo Sansad' march
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday called on supporters to hold a night-long vigil at Jantar Mantar ahead of the outfit's proposed 'Chalo Sansad' march to Parliament on Monday.

Meanwhile, activist

's wife said he would end his hunger strike if political leaders assured him that the issue of education accountability would be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

The appeal came as Jantar Mantar witnessed a surge in the number of protesters a day before the Monsoon Session of Parliament, with supporters from different parts of the country gathering at the protest site.

Addressing supporters through a video message, Dipke urged them to remain at the protest site through the night to ensure the planned march proceeded peacefully.

"Our protest is going on. Please come here in large numbers. Stay here for the night. If you don't come, they will try to end the protest," he said.

Appealing for restraint, Dipke added, "Our protest and march will be peaceful. I request everyone to follow the rules and follow the guidelines."

He also said Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike was continuing from Safdarjung Hospital despite his removal from the protest site by police on Saturday.





"As you saw, they took away Sonam sir forcefully, but his hunger strike is continuing in the hospital," Dipke said.

According to CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das, nearly 20,000 people were 'at and around Jantar Mantar' even before the scheduled mobilisation.

In a post on X, Das said, "20,000 people are at and around Jantar Mantar. And it's not even July 20 yet. Dharmendra Pradhan -- your day of reckoning is here."

The protest also received support from several political leaders and public figures.

Actors Shabana Azmi and Prakash Raj visited Jantar Mantar during the day, joining Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra, CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and AAP leader Manish Sisodia in expressing solidarity with the agitation.

In a significant announcement, Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali J Angmo, told supporters that the activist was prepared to end his fast if political leaders visited him in hospital and assured him that the issue of education accountability would be raised during the Monsoon Session.

"If political leaders meet Sonam in the hospital and assure him that they will raise the issue of education accountability during the Parliament session, he will end his hunger strike tomorrow," Angmo said.

She also conveyed Wangchuk's message to supporters ahead of Monday's march.

"Sonam has requested all of us to take tomorrow's march peacefully and ensure that this protest is not misused," she said.

Angmo further alleged that the family had lost faith in Safdarjung Hospital and had approached the Delhi high court seeking permission to shift Wangchuk to a private hospital.

She claimed the hospital had neither discharged him nor allowed the transfer despite repeated requests and alleged that he was effectively under 'illegal detention' because of the heavy police presence.

Earlier in the day, Wangchuk issued a message from Safdarjung Hospital through Angmo, describing Monday's mobilisation as 'India's second freedom movement' and calling for 'freedom from injustice' over the alleged NEET paper leak and 'freedom from fear' over what he termed his 'illegal detention'.

He appealed to people to make the Parliament march a success.

The CJP also expressed concern over possible police action ahead of the march. In posts on X, the outfit urged supporters to reach Jantar Mantar immediately, claimed tear-gas equipment had been brought to the area and alleged that anti-social elements could attempt to infiltrate the gathering to provoke disturbances. It appealed to protesters not to respond to any provocation and to keep the march peaceful.

Following Wangchuk's removal from the protest site early on Saturday, Dipke began his own indefinite hunger strike. Entering its second day on Sunday, he said he had now understood the physical toll of a prolonged fast and appealed to people to strengthen the movement by joining Monday's Parliament march in large numbers.

The CJP has been protesting at Jantar Mantar since June 20, demanding the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, reforms in the examination system and justice for affected students.

Meanwhile, Delhi Police has clarified that no permission has been sought or granted for the proposed march to Parliament. It said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) are in force in the New Delhi district, prohibiting protest marches, processions and assemblies of five or more people except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar with prior permission.

The police said strict security arrangements have been put in place for the Monsoon Session of Parliament and warned that anyone violating the prohibitory orders would face action under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and other applicable provisions of law.

It also appealed to citizens to refrain from participating in any unauthorised gathering or march and cooperate in maintaining public peace and security.

World.title: 'We intend to work with PM Modi': Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar announces entry into NDA with 20 Mamata rebels
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Once a Mamata loyalist and now an NCPI leader after rebelling against the Mamata Banerjee-led

, Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar on Su

y announced that she would join the ruling NDA in the Lok Sabha ahead of Monsoon Session.

She said 20 former TMC MPs, who have formed a separate parliamentary group under the NCPI, would also join the PM Modi-led alliance in the Lower House.

She said the group intends to work with the NDA under the leadership of Prime Minister

and Union home minister Amit Shah.

The announcement marks a significant step in the Mamata rebels' realignment amid the continuing exodus from the TMC following its crushing defeat to the

BJP

in the West Bengal assembly elections in May.

Addressing the media, Kakoli said the group had decided to back the NDA and work under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.

"We, 20 AITC MPs, are joining the NDA alliance. Leaving AITC, we align ourselves with NCPI... we intend to work with the NDA, supporting the initiatives of PM Modi and our Home Minister Amit Shah and be involved in their work of nation-building. We stated in the all-party meeting that we would work together.





There are 8 women among our group of 20, and we will stand by the government on whatever issues they take up," she said.

Speaking about the NCPI parliamentary party meeting, Kakoli said the group's focus would be on constructive participation during the Monsoon Session.

"There will be discussions and debates on 5-6 bills... Everyone should debate, but we shouldn't waste the House's time, as that causes significant loss to the country and the public.

In the interest of the nation and for the progress of the people, we will debate the upcoming issues, whether they concern taxes or the registration of births and deaths, but we will ensure the House functions smoothly. That is what we discussed," she added.

The development comes amid an unprecedented rebellion within the Trinamool Congress after the party, led by

Mamata Banerjee

, suffered a stinging defeat to the BJP in the West Bengal assembly polls after 15 years in power.

While Ritabrata Banerjee has emerged as the face of the rebellion within the party organisation by staking claim to the leader of the opposition post in the assembly against the wishes of the party leadership. Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar also has led a large section of TMC MPs in the Lok Sabha away from the Mamata Banerjee-led camp. The rebel faction has since aligned itself with the NCPI and is now extending support to the BJP-led NDA in Parliament.

World.title: 'No permission sought or granted': Delhi Police on CJP's Parliament march
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ahead of the Monsoon Session,

on Sunday said no permission has been sought or granted for the proposed march to Parliament called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on July 20, warning that any unauthorised gathering would invite legal action.

In a statement, the police said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the equivalent of the erstwhile Section 144 of the CrPC, are in force across the New Delhi district.

Under these restrictions, protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are prohibited, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar and only with prior permission, the statement said.

Delhi police posted: "Prohibitory orders u/s 163 BNSS are in force in New Delhi District except designated protest site at Jantar Mantar Road. Further, no permission has been sought or granted for any proposed march to Parliament on 20 July 2026. Citizens are advised not to participate in any unauthorised gathering or procession. Please respect the prohibitory orders in force and cooperate with Delhi Police in maintaining public peace, safety and security.





"

With the Parliament session beginning on July 20, Delhi Police said elaborate security arrangements have been put in place to ensure public safety, protect vital government installations and provide security to protectees.

The police warned that anyone violating the prohibitory orders would be liable for prosecution under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and other applicable provisions of law.

Appealing to the public to maintain peace and order, Delhi Police urged citizens to refrain from participating in any unauthorised march or gathering and to cooperate with authorities in ensuring security during the Parliament session.

Earlier, the

upheld the Centre's decision to intervene in

's prolonged hunger strike after the educationist was shifted from the CJP's protest site at Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital.

The court observed that the Union government's action was well within its rights and found no arbitrariness or use of force in shifting Wangchuk for medical monitoring.

The move, however, triggered strong reactions from Wangchuk, his wife Gitanjali Angmo and members of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). Angmo has maintained that the hunger strike continues, alleging that Wangchuk has refused to consume even oral fluids offered by the medical authorities.

Meanwhile, Wangchuk's wife has vowed to lead the march to Parliament.

World.title: 'Parliament should discuss if new anti-defection law needed': Congress' Manish Tewari after TMC, Shiv Sena (UBT) splits
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress MP Manish Tewari on Monday called for a discussion on whether there should be a new anti-defection law, saying the current composition of the Lok Sabha no longer reflects the mandate given by voters in the 2024 parliamentary elections.

"The fundamental point is that in 2024, the people gave a mandate, and the Lok Sabha was constituted in accordance with that mandate. Today, two years later, the composition of the Lok Sabha is no longer in line with that mandate. It is contrary to the people's mandate," PTI quoted Tewari as saying.

Speaking ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, Tewari said the "foremost priority" of the session should be for Parliament to set aside other business and debate whether a new anti-defection law is needed.

The Chandigarh MP stressed the need to curb the "opportunistic politics" often described as "Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram", where politicians switch parties without regard for ideological or policy differences.

Tewari also emphasised the need to distinguish and address genuine ideological or policy disagreements.

"A balance needs to be struck both inside and outside Parliament and state assemblies, because all these recent developments have worked to weaken Indian democracy," he said.





In recent days, two parties opposed to the ruling BJP â the

(TMC) and

(UBT) â have witnessed splits within their ranks, with some MPs either extending support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) or joining parties already part of the NDA.

In the TMC's case, three of its Rajya Sabha MPs resigned from the party, joined the BJP, and were later re-elected as BJP candidates. Meanwhile, 20 of the TMC's 28 Lok Sabha MPs merged their faction with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India and extended support to the NDA.

From Shiv Sena (UBT), six of its Lok Sabha MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena, a BJP ally, reducing the Uddhav Thackeray-led party's strength in the Lower House to three members.

In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the NDA won 293 seats in the 543-member House, including 240 seats secured by the BJP. The recent developments have further increased its numbers.

World.title: 'He intends to continue the fast': Sonam Wangchuk's wife vows to lead Parliament march
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Educationalist and climate activist

's wife, Gitanjali J Angmo on Sunday said that she would lead the planned march to Parliament on Monday to represent her husband along with the students and parents protesting against the alleged NEET-UG paper leak, asserting that Wangchuk intends to continue his indefinite hunger strike.

Her remarks came after the Delhi high court declined to grant urgent interim relief seeking Wangchuk's immediate discharge from Safdarjung Hospital and his transfer to a private hospital.

Speaking to reporters outside the Delhi high court, Angmo said she would participate in the march on behalf of Wangchuk, who was shifted to Safdarjung Hospital on Saturday after being removed from the protest site at Jantar Mantar.

"I will definitely represent him in tomorrow's protest. We filed an urgent petition today because, had we been allowed to shift today, we could have gone to Medanta and then arrived at the protest site by tomorrow morning. But we knew they wouldn't allow that. I am ready to represent Sonam Wangchuk, and I will definitely join the march tomorrow," she said.

Appealing to those planning to join the march, Angmo urged protesters to remain peaceful and vigilant.





"To all the students and parents coming to join the march tomorrow, I would say: keep two things in mind. First, let us conduct this march in a completely peaceful manner. Second, remain vigilant against nefarious elements who might try to disrupt it. Let us stay alert and avoid falling into their traps. Attempts might be made to incite trouble or give the event a different complexion," she said.

She also said Wangchuk remained determined to continue his fast despite being admitted to hospital.

"Sonam wanted to continue the fast exactly as he had been observing it previously. He intends to continue the fast he has been maintaining. They have been urging him to consume fluids, but he refused, although he is drinking water," Angmo said.

Earlier in the day, Angmo described the Centre's concern for Wangchuk's health as a 'charade', alleging that the government feared his participation in the proposed Parliament march over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak.

"They said they brought him in because they were deeply concerned about his health, as it was declining. But these claims are incorrect. First of all, his health was not deteriorating at all. If you look at the reports from the evening prior, everything was absolutely normal; his potassium level was 4.3, and all other parameters were normal too," she said.

She claimed Wangchuk's health had not deteriorated before he was taken to Safdarjung Hospital and alleged that authorities could have informed the family before shifting him.

"If you were truly so concerned about his health, why did you send police personnel in plain clothes? Why did you so ruthlessly pick him up, put him on a stretcher, and take him away? You could have simply come to conduct a medical test and informed his family. That is the proper way to handle things in a democracy," she said.

Reiterating her allegation, Angmo said, "If you were genuinely concerned about his health, then this whole narrative about health concerns is nothing but a charade.

They were simply afraid that if Sonam set out on his march, hundreds of thousands of people would join himânot just in Delhi, but across the entire countryâand they were trying to prevent that."

Angmo also alleged that Wangchuk was not being allowed to freely consult doctors of his choice and claimed the atmosphere at the hospital resembled the conditions during his detention in Jodhpur Jail following his arrest during the 2025 Ladakh protests.

"He is not being allowed to meet his doctors. We want to consult our doctors, whom we are comfortable with. The police are constantly surveilling. When I am in the room with him, a constable accompanies me. The environment is similar to Jodhpur Jail. I was not allowed to carry my phone, and Sonam was not handed over his tablet. When we asked for orders, the police personnel had no written orders," she alleged.

The Delhi high court, however, refused to order Wangchuk's transfer from Safdarjung Hospital, observing that the material placed before it did not indicate he was under illegal detention.

The court noted that his wife, brother and other family members had unrestricted access to him and had been provided accommodation at the hospital.

The court also referred to the earlier order directing daily medical monitoring and recorded the Centre's submission that Wangchuk had been shifted to the government hospital because of his deteriorating medical condition.

According to the medical opinion placed before the court, his sugar and sodium levels were below normal and his potassium level had fallen to a dangerously low level.

The court noted that intravenous fluids had not been administered as Wangchuk had not consented to the treatment.

Security intensifies ahead of CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' march

Meanwhile, security has been intensified across the New Delhi district ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament and the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed 'Chalo Sansad' march on Monday.

In a statement, Delhi Police said no permission had been sought or granted for any march to Parliament by the CJP.

It also said prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), formerly Section 144 of the CrPC, are in force across the New Delhi district.

The police said protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are prohibited, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar with prior permission.

"As Parliament session is commencing from 20 July, strict security arrangements are in place to ensure public safety, security of protectees, and the protection of vital government installations," the statement read.

The police warned that anyone violating the prohibitory orders would be liable for prosecution under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and other applicable provisions of law.

Delhi Police also appealed to the public to respect the law, avoid participating in any unauthorised gathering or march and cooperate in maintaining public peace, safety and security.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Wangchuk will end fast if Parliament session focuses on education accountability, says Gitanjali Angmo
World.content:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk will call off his indefinite hunger strike if political leaders meet him at the Safdarjung Hospital and assure him that the issue of education accountability will be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament beginning Monday, his wife Gitanjali Angmo said on Sunday (July 19, 2026).

Also read: Sonam Wangchuk | Fast and composed

Thousands gathered at the Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Sunday (July 19, 2026) ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)’s planned march to Parliament, demanding resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, even as the Delhi Police issued a prohibitory order against marches, demonstrations, and assemblies of five or more people except at the designated protest site with prior permission.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Sachin Sharma shared a public advisory on X on Sunday (July 19, 2026), stating that the “Delhi Police categorically clarifies that no permission has been sought or granted for any such protest march/procession.” The prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS (formerly Section 144 CrPC) is currently in effect in the New Delhi district, according to the DCP’s post.

Also read: Parliament session, CJP’s rally plan key reasons for Wangchuk’s removal from protest site

Earlier, the Delhi High Court on Sunday (July 19, 2026) refused to interfere with activist Sonam Wangchuk’s treatment at Safdarjung Hospital. Ms. Angmo said the petition was “wrongly interpreted” and questioned why the government, if it had to intervene, couldn’t do so “democratically with the family’s trust”.

“He has fasted for 35 days in Ladakh. His health is fine. There was no need for government intervention,” his wife told the reporters after the hearing.

World.title: Students must unite against drugs: Minister Bindu Krishna
World.content:
Minister for Women and Child Development, Labour, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development, Bindu Krishna, has called upon the student community to become active participants in the fight against the drug mafia, which is attempting to destroy society. She was presiding over the distribution ceremony of the ‘Focus Kollam’ Minister’s Excellence Award-2026, organised for talented students from the Kollam constituency.

The Minister said that a clear sense of purpose is essential for students to build a bright future and added that the government will establish new educational institutions and create better employment opportunities for the next generation to ensure the comprehensive development of the State.

Inaugurating the event, Shafi Parambil MP said that students must move toward their future with well-defined goals in mind. He added that the government is always there to give wings to the dreams of students and provide them with maximum support.

The event honoured top achievers, including students who secured full A-Plus in the SSLC and Plus Two examinations, as well as those who scored full A1 or above 90% marks in the Class 10 and Class 12 CBSE and ICSE exams. Rank holders in Degree, Post Graduate (PG), and other professional examinations were also felicitated during the event. Ramya Haridas MLA was the chief guest while Mayor N.K. Hafees, District Collector Annie Jula Thomas, and deputy Mayor Udaya Sukumaran were among those who spoke at the gathering.

World.title: Poor response to Mamatheya Thottilu; only two infants surrendered in cradles across the state in a year
World.content:
Despite encouraging people to safely surrender infants in Mamatheya Thottilu rather than abandoning them in garbage, buses, trains or other places, the programme has received poor response.

According to data, Mamatheya Thottilu has received only two infants in the past one year. One infant was in Tumakuru and the other one in Mysuru.

Arundhati T.S., Deputy Director, State Adoption Resource Agency (SARA), said, “Two infants were found in Tumakuru and Mysuru. After a legal process involving the police, Child Welfare Committee, doctors and other stakeholders, the infants’ details were updated on the website to find potential parents for adoption. Parents who register on the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) portal can see the details of the infants.”

Ms. Arundhati explained, “The reason for a poor response is a lack of awareness among people and fear of their identity being revealed. Most of the cradles that we have placed are in district government hospitals, child care institutions and District Child Protection offices. We receive infants found in front of temples, government hospitals, petrol bunks, bus stations, railway stations. But people fear surrendering them in cradles. There are 46 such cradles placed across the State.”

When asked whether an FIR would be booked against those who surrender the child in Mamatheya Thottilu or other places, Ms. Arundhati said, “It is not about filing an FIR or punishing them. We trace the mother or parents or guardians to find out their reasons for abandoning the baby and register the child for adoption after following a protocol and getting a birth certificate for the baby within a particular time window. The police do not file an FIR under the Juvenile Justice Act 2015 in such cases. But it depends on different cases and the reasons for abandoning the child.”

Lack of awareness

Vasudev Sharma, child rights activist, said, “It is disappointing to read news of young girls giving birth to babies in toilets without being able to express it to their parents and teachers. The reason being a lack of sex education at schools and programmes like Mamatheya Thottilu. Not just school girls, such cases are noticed among unwed women. Due to fear of parents, they don’t reveal affairs and pregnancy. When they give birth, babies are abandoned in unsafe places. Hence, there should be awareness created among people about this programme.”

World.title: Quiz organised for students
World.content:
A Military History and Awareness Quiz 2026 for school students was organised by the Colour of Glory team at The Russian Centre of Science and Culture in Chennai on Sunday. A total of 110 schools from the city participated. A written round was followed by a final round with the top six teams. The event aimed at fostering military heritage among school students.

The quiz was conducted by war veteran Lt. Col. S V Sundar. The event was attended by nearly 220 students, over 100 parents and teachers. The event was organised by the team led by 1971 war veteran Captain D.P. Ramachandran. The chief guest was Director of Russian House in Chennai, Mr. Alexander Dodonov. The Army Public School was the champion and SVS Vidya Mandir were the runners up and DAV Gill Nagar school being the third. The other top schools were DAV Pallikaranai and Sri Shankara School, Adyar.

World.title: Deputy Commissioner of Police stresses on strict rotation of duties
World.content:
Deputy Commissioner of Police (North East Division), Mithun Kumar G.K., directed station officers to ensure the strict implementation of the rotation of duties among police personnel during the inspection of Amruthahalli Police Station.

The issue was raised by police personnel during the inspection, which also reviewed administration, investigations, personnel welfare and public service delivery.

The inspection was conducted under the directions of the Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru City.

During the inspection, the DCP reviewed administrative and investigation records, heard the grievances of police personnel and directed that pending issues be addressed promptly. Besides stressing the implementation of duty rotation, personnel also raised issues relating to the pending Dearness Allowance (DA) settlement of ex-servicemen serving in the police department. The DCP accepted their representation and assured them that the matter would be addressed.

The inspection also focused on expediting the disposal of vehicles seized in criminal cases and unclaimed vehicles in accordance with legal procedures. The management of case properties (Muddemal), maintenance of records and safety measures at the police station were reviewed.

The DCP assessed the progress of investigations and court-pending cases, directing investigating officers to conduct quality investigations, file charge sheets within the stipulated time and closely monitor court proceedings. The station was also instructed to organise Victims’ Day every month to hear the grievances of victims and facilitate legal assistance and support.

Special emphasis was laid on strengthening beat enforcement and beat policing. Personnel were directed to conduct regular Sub-Beat meetings to create awareness on cybercrime, drug abuse, the safety of women and children, road safety and other crime prevention measures. They were also instructed to maintain station cleanliness, ensure proper record management, enforce staff discipline, execute pending warrants, closely monitor rowdy sheeters and habitual offenders, effectively utilise CCTV surveillance systems and provide prompt, citizen-friendly policing services.

Following the inspection, an outdoor briefing was conducted for officers and personnel of Amruthahalli, Bagalur, Chikkajala, Yelahanka New Town and Kothanur police stations. They were instructed to intensify Cheetah and Hoysala patrols in markets, bus stands, temples and other crowded places, maintain constant vigil over suspicious persons, vehicles and activities, and take preventive measures to avert untoward incidents.

The personnel were further directed to respond promptly to emergency calls, maintain law and order, strengthen beat patrols, interact courteously with the public and discharge their duties responsibly to enhance public confidence and ensure a safe and peaceful environment across the North East Division.

World.title: Josh Kerr of Britain breaks the men''s mile world record that stood since 1999
World.content:
Josh Kerr, the British runner who helped stoke a revival in middle-distance drama on the track, added a new chapter Saturday (July 19, 2026) by running the mile in 3 minutes, 42.66 seconds to break the 27-year-old record for the distance.

At a Diamond League meet in London, Kerr broke Moroccan great Hicham El Guerrouj's mark of 3 minutes, 43.13 seconds, set in Rome in 1999. The 28-year-old native of Edinburgh celebrated with a lap of honour at London Stadium.

“It was just me, my shoes and the track,” he said. “I was absolutely deaf in that last 110 meters. Kerr finished more than three seconds clear of American Yared Nuguse in 3:45.69.

In an interview with the BBC, Kerr said the crowd support as he closed in on the record was “just incredible.” “I didn't take my foot off the gas," he continued, “but ... I started to glide, and I was like, oh wow, this feels incredible.' It's incredible because I'm slowing down. So, I was like, I better get to the line.' So, crossing the finish line, seeing 42-something — anything — was my goal, so it was great.” The 28-year-old Kerr's previous best time was 3:45.34 in 2024.

Kerr and Jakob Ingebrigtsen, the 2021 Olympic champion, put a charge in the slightly shorter but more widely contested 1,500-meter race in the leadup to the Paris Olympics, going back and forth on a number of issues, including Kerr's suggestion that his rival could only run his top times with the help of pacesetters, the likes of which aren't allowed at major championships.

Kerr, who won worlds at the distance in 2023, frequently sparred back and forth with Ingebrigtsen on the track and online in the early 2020s. When the Paris Games rolled around, Ingebrigtsen faded to fourth while American Cole Hocker pulled a huge upset, with Kerr finishing second.

Last year at world championships, Ingebrigtsen faltered in a preliminary heat while Kerr pulled up lame and limped into the finish in a race won by Issac Nader of Portugal.

This year, with no worlds or Olympics on the schedule, Kerr made the mile his key target. It's a distance that isn't run as much in big events, but that still has huge historical significance, most of it surrounding Roger Bannister's breaking of the once-intimidating four-minute barrier in 1954.

World.title: Villagers oppose new stone quarry, crusher unit near Cheyyar in Tiruvannamalai
World.content:
Villagers, mostly farmers and traders, in Palli, Irumanthangal, Mottur Nagar, Vadakkanpattu and Mangalam villages of Tiruvannamalai district have expressed their opposition against proposed stone quarry and crusher unit in Palli village.

The public hearings, chaired by Sub Collector S. Madhu Cheziyan, organised by the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB), were held at the village near Cheyyar town. “Public hearing is mandatory to give clearance for the setting up of a new quarry and crusher unit in the villages. Any objections or support for the new facility should be given in writing by participants, especially residents,” said a TNPCB official.

As per norms, TNPCB organises such public hearings only in cases where the proposed quarry or cluster of quarries are above five hectares of land together in the affected village. In other words, new standalone quarries or clusters of quarries that are less than five hectares will be given a nod without public hearings. The proposed stone quarry will be built in an over 10 acre plot.

Residents said large tracts of paddy fields are located around the proposed stone quarry site in Palli village. Farmers also cultivate green chilli, brinjal, groundnuts, greens and mango. The proposed quarry could pollute groundwater and waterbodies in surrounding farming villages, and affect agricultural activities. “Farmers depend on agriculture and cattle rearing, for which clean water bodies are required. The new quarry could affect the livelihood of residents in surrounding villages,” said K. Sampath, a resident.

Residents said noise from regular blasts in the proposed stone quarry will also affect senior citizens and children, and huge stone pieces from the quarry will fall on farmlands. Transport of excavated stones from the quarry will also damage village roads. Government bus and ambulance services will be affected.

TNPCB officials said at present, Tiruvannamalai district has around 150 stone quarries. Most quarries are located in Cheyyar, Vembakkam, Polur and Chetpet that were well-connected with adjoining districts.

Residents’ concerns will be submitted before the State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) that will decide on issuing licenses for the new quarry. Renewal of quarries is done once in five years.

World.title: Kajal bags gold in 76kg, Antim Neha clinch silver in Budapest Ranking Series
World.content:
Reigning U20 world champion wrestler Kajal clinched the women’s 76kg category gold with a commanding performance in the Budapest Ranking Series in Budapest.

Facing USA's Dymond Precious Guilford in a gripping gold medal clash, the young Indian wrestler exhibited immense tactical composure under pressure.

The high-stakes encounter ended in a 3-3 deadlock, but Kajal held her nerve to clinch the championship on criteria, securing India's third gold medal of the tournament.

India added two silver medals to its haul through strong campaigns in the 53kg and 57kg weight divisions.

In the 53kg championship final, Antim Panghal was forced to settle for silver after conceding her gold medal bout against Sweden's Emma Jonna Denise Malmgren due to an injury (VIN).

Meanwhile, in the 57kg category, Neha Sharma put together an impressive run to reach the final.

Facing a formidable opponent in China's Kexin Hong in the title clash, Sharma fought valiantly but sustained a 0-4 defeat on points to finish second.

India secured an additional podium finish in the 53kg division as Nishu claimed a hard-fought bronze medal.

In a fiercely contested tactical battle against Romania's Andrea Beatrice Ana, Nishu displayed immense defensive resilience.

The bout ended in a 2-2 tie, but the Indian wrestler was declared the winner on criteria (VPO1) to secure her spot on the podium.

Now, India have accumulated an impressive 12 medals at the tournament, comprising three gold, four silver, and five bronze medals.

The Indians will now shift focus to the upcoming Greco-Roman weight categories as the contingent looks to finish the ranking series on a strong note.

World.title: Argentina vs Spain Live Score, FIFA World Cup 2026 Final: National anthem time before kickoff
World.content:
After over a month of breathtaking footballing action, we are finally down to two teams as Argentina and Spain will be vying for the crown in the New York New Jersey Stadium or the Metlife Stadium on Sunday night. Argentina are gunning for their fourth and Lionel Messi’s second World Cup title while Spain will be looking for their first title since 2010.

Argentina and Spain were supposed to meet in March for the Finalissima where the European champions take on the world champions in an exhibition match but the clash at Doha was cancelled after Iranian strikes on American bases in middle eastern countries. Now, finally the much anticipated contest is taking place in the biggest stage imaginable.

World.title: Rohit Sharma’s century at Lord’s came off Shardul Thakur’s bat
World.content:
Rohit Sharma’s sensational hundred at Lord’s against England came from the willow given by his team mate Shardul Thakur. Sharma used Thakur’s bat during a long chase but India failed to cross the winning line in the series decider. The 39-year-old Sharma slammed 138 off 110 balls in the third and final ODI with his future with India still uncertain.



“I am signed with SS bats and Jatin Sareen (owner) has been very kind to send me some excellent piece of willows. Rohit once requested me to give him a couple of bats since he loved them. We all love him and he’s given us so many joyful moments in the game of cricket that denying him the bats was out of question. And today I am really happy that he scored his historic hundred at Lord’s cricket ground using one of my bats,” Thakur told The Indian Express.

World.title: India lose in decisive 3rd ODI vs England at Lord’s, concede series 1-2
World.content:
Rohit Sharma slammed a blistering 138 while Virat Kohli and captain Shubman Gill chipped in with 74 and 77 respectively but a chase of 387 was beyond them as India fell to England by 27 runs in the 3rd and final ODI on Sunday, losing the series 2-1.

Except for the top 3, India’s middle order collapsed once again with Ishan Kishan (14), Shreyas Iyer (0) and KL Rahul (12) failing to build on the foundation set by Rohit, Kohli and Gill.

Earlier, Ben Duckett made mincemeat of an inexperienced Indian bowling attack with a fabulous 141 as England posted a mammoth 387 for 3, riding on a 192-run opening stand between the centurion and Jacob Bethell.

Jasprit Bumrah’s absence due to an impact injury on his left knee was certainly a blow for India and that proved to be telling for the visitors.

The four-pronged pace attack comprising Prasidh Krishna (2/69 in 10 overs), Arshdeep Singh (0/72 in 10 overs), Prince Yadav (1/79 on 10 overs) and Gurnoor Brar (0/97 in 10 overs), with a cumulative experience of 51 ODIs, lacked both skill and experience against an in-form batting line-up.

Duckett and Bethell (91 off 93 balls) were fantastic in terms of planning and execution. The batting powerplay of first 10 overs yielded 58 runs but the wheels came off between overs 11 to 30 when they literally ran the bowlers ragged.



With head coach Gautam Gambhir using Kuldeep Yadav in only 38 games out of a total 103 matches (across three formats) since his appointment, the lack of a second spinner save Axar Patel (0/61 in 10 overs) did hurt India.

While Duckett hit 18 boundaries in all apart from a six, Bethell, who looked comparatively more fluent at the onset, hit 11 fours and a six, before being holed out in the deep off Prasidh Krishna’s bowling.

Joe Root (74 no off 48 balls) continued his golden run of form with another half-century — his third in three games — to take the total past 350-run mark. Jos Buttler (41 no off 13 balls) also joined in the fun as Brar got a harsh lesson in international cricket, going for almost 100 runs.



At the onset, it didn’t help matters that rookie Prince, bowling up the famous Lord’s slope, struggled with his length as Bethell pulled him for a six over deep mid-wicket and then slapped him in the gap between deep mid-wicket and mid-on for a boundary.

The rusty Arshdeep Singh didn’t hold his line while Prasidh Krishna, despite beating Bethell’s bat on a number of occasions, also bowled the odd loose delivery.

However, Bethell did well to complete his half-century off 51 balls while England reached the team total of 100 by the 16th over. By that time, Indian bowlers have already conceded 15 boundaries and the lines were horribly wrong, allowing the opening pair to nicely settle into a rhythm. In all, they conceded 42 boundaries and six sixes.



It also established the fact that all the other Indian pacers look good when the brilliant Bumrah is at work at one end and that effectiveness vanishes once he is absent. One saw that in the T20Is and now in ODIs too.

World.title: ‘Right to raise voice peacefully’: Shabana Azmi joins CJP’s Jantar Mantar protest
World.content:
Veteran actor Shabana Azmi on Sunday joined the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar, extending support to protesters demanding education reforms and accountability over alleged examination irregularities, a day before the outfit’s planned ‘Chalo Sansad’ march.

Azmi visited the protest site Sunday evening, joining a growing list of public figures expressing solidarity with the agitation. Actor Prakash Raj, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra, CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and AAP leader Manish Sisodia also visited Jantar Mantar during the day.

Addressing the gathering, Azmi said she was standing with students because their demands deserved to be heard. “I have come here because I believe the concerns being raised by the students are important. In a democracy, people have the right to raise their voice peacefully,” she said, urging the authorities to engage in dialogue instead of confrontation.

Also Read | Hunger strike Day 21: Police shift Sonam Wangchuk to hospital

Azmi also met the All India Students’ Association – AISA president Neha Bora, who is sitting on an indefinite hunger strike with fellow students Aameen and Manish, on the 22nd day of their voluntary fasting. Visuals from the protest site showed the actor greeting and offering support in a heartfelt gesture to the students.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Neha (@neowsibora)

In a post on X, Neha also thanked Azmi for extending her support and solidarity to the movement.

During his visit, actor Prakash Raj also led protesters in raising the slogan “Aali re aali, aata Pradhan chi baari aali” (loosely translates to: “Now, Pradhan’s time has come”), targeting Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Extending the slogan with a satirical reference to his popular dialogue “Aata majhi satakli!” (Marathi for “Now I’ve had enough” or “I’ve finally snapped”), Raj drew loud cheers from the crowd as protesters echoed the chant in support of the movement.

Aali Re Aali Aata Pradhan Chi Bari Aali Prakash Raj says, “Aata Majhi satakli!” At Jantar Mantar pic.twitter.com/2n5HmPysiA — Cockroach Janta Party (@CJP_for_India) July 19, 2026

The protest site witnessed a surge in attendance on Sunday, with supporters gathering ahead of Monday’s proposed march to Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das claimed that nearly 20,000 people had gathered in and around Jantar Mantar by evening, although the figure could not be independently verified.

The demonstration has been ongoing since June 20, with the CJP demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, reforms in the examination system, and justice for affected students.

The protest took a turn on Saturday after activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been on an indefinite hunger strike, was shifted from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police. Police said the move was carried out in compliance with Delhi High Court directions and on medical advice because of Wangchuk’s deteriorating health.

Speaking at the protest on Sunday, Wangchuk’s wife Gitanjali Angmo said he would end his hunger strike on Monday if political leaders met him at Safdarjung Hospital and assured him that the issue of education accountability would be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.



“If political leaders meet Sonam in the hospital and assure him that they will raise the issue of education accountability during the Parliament session, he will end his hunger strike tomorrow,” Angmo said.

She also conveyed Wangchuk’s appeal to supporters to keep Monday’s mobilisation peaceful. “Sonam has requested all of us to take tomorrow’s march peacefully and ensure that this protest is not misused,” she said.

Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, who began his own indefinite hunger strike after Wangchuk was removed from the protest site, urged supporters to stay at Jantar Mantar overnight to ensure the march proceeds peacefully.

“Our protest is going on. Please come here in large numbers. Stay here for the night. If you don’t come, they will try to end the protest,” Dipke said in a video message. He added, “Our protest and march will be peaceful. I request everyone to follow the rules and follow the guidelines.”



Delhi Police, however, said no permission had been sought or granted for the proposed march and reiterated that prohibitory orders remain in force in the New Delhi district. Authorities have deployed multi-layered security around Parliament and Jantar Mantar ahead of Monday’s planned mobilisation.
